problems.stem: Lucia deposited $1,500 in a savings account that earns 6% interest, compounded once a year. She won't add or take out any money. The bank requires a $50 minimum balance.
problems.ask: How much will be in the account after 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 6% of $1,500 is $90, so the value goes to $1,500 + $90 = $1,590.

problems.stem: Victor drove 120 miles to visit his aunt and averaged 60 miles per hour on the way there. Coming home on the same roads, heavy traffic held him to an average of 40 miles per hour. His car gets about 30 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: What was Victor's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Dev's class kept track of how many books each student read over winter break, and the table shows the results. The school library lets each student borrow up to eight books at a time.
problems.ask: What is the median number of books read over the break?
steps: With 24 values in order, the median is the average of the 12th and 13th values.
Running totals: through 0: 1, through 1: 10, through 2: 17, through 3: 21, through 4: 22, through 5: 24.
Both fall in the row for 2 books, so the median is 2 books.

problems.stem: Zoe's booth at the town festival has 10 rubber ducks floating in a pool. A player pays $5, picks one duck at random, and wins the prize marked underneath; the duck then goes back in. The table shows the prizes. The festival lasts 7 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the booth make per game after paying out prizes?
steps: If each duck came up once, the prizes would total 2 × $5 + 3 × $2 = $16.
The booth keeps $5 − $1.60 = $3.40 per game on average.

problems.stem: Ingrid is laying square pavers for a backyard patio. The patio will be a rectangle 20 feet by 12 feet, and each paver is 24 inches on a side. The pavers fit exactly, with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many pavers does Ingrid need?
steps: 24 inches is 2 feet. Along the length: 20 ÷ 2 = 10 pavers.

problems.stem: A store is taking 20% off every desk chair, and Noor finds one with a regular price of $235. She also has a member coupon that takes 25% off the already reduced price. The sale price is good for 9 more days.
problems.ask: How much does Noor pay for the desk chair, before tax?
steps: 20% of $235 is $47, so the sale price is $235 − $47 = $188.
The extra 25% comes off $188, not the original price: 25% of $188 is $47.

problems.stem: Paige bought a set of wireless headphones at an electronics store during a 50%-off sale, and she also used a $10 coupon. The register took 50% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. The headphones run about 24 hours on a full charge. Before tax, Paige paid $80.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the headphones?
steps: $90 is what was left after 50% off, so it is 50% of the original price.

problems.stem: Amara's running club timed its members in a 5-kilometer race. The 9 runners in the morning group averaged 32 minutes, and the 21 runners in the evening group averaged 27 minutes. The course had three water stations.
problems.ask: What was the average time for all the runners in both groups, in minutes?

problems.stem: Lucia's board game comes with a cloth bag holding 4 red tokens and 7 yellow tokens. The box says the game is for ages 10 and up. To start the game, she draws two tokens at random without putting the first one back.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both tokens are the same color?

bonus.stem: Victor is laying a 7-by-7 patio of square tiles, all the same size. Looking at the grid lines, Victor wonders how many squares can be traced, counting every size, from single tiles up to the biggest square that fits.
bonus.ask: How many squares of all sizes are in the 7-by-7 grid?
steps: A k-by-k square can start in 7 − k + 1 spots across and the same number down, so there are (7 − k + 1)² of them.

problems.stem: Fatima is running a lemonade stand. She makes eight pitchers of lemonade, and each pitcher holds 6 cups. There are 4 cups in a quart.
problems.ask: How many quarts of lemonade does Fatima make?
steps: There are 4 cups in a quart: 48 ÷ 4 = 12 quarts.

problems.stem: Carmen is driving to a college campus for a tour, which is 140 miles from home, and then driving back. Her car gets 20 miles per gallon, and gas costs $3.80 per gallon. She plans to leave at 7 in the morning.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the round trip?

problems.stem: Mei is painting the four walls of her bedroom, which is 19 feet long, 12 feet wide and 10 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. The door and windows take up 60 square feet that won't be painted. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $28 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Mei need to buy?
steps: Minus the door and windows: 620 − 60 = 560 square feet.
1,120 ÷ 350 = 3.2, which is more than 3, so round up to 4 gallons.

problems.stem: Amara is growing bacteria for a biology lab. She starts a dish with 200 bacteria, and under these conditions the population doubles every 30 minutes. The dish is 10 centimeters across.
problems.ask: How many bacteria will be in the dish after 3.5 hours?

problems.stem: Five friends, including Hugo and Nadia, have 5 seats together in one row at the movies. Hugo and Nadia both talk during movies, so the group agrees they won't sit side by side. The movie runs 105 minutes.
problems.ask: In how many different ways can the 5 friends fill the 5 seats?
steps: Orders with them together: glue them into a block, 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24, times 2 for their order = 48.

problems.stem: At 9:50 a.m., Ezra started a volunteer shift at the library. The shift ended at 1:15 p.m., and he walked home.
problems.ask: How many minutes long was the shift?
steps: From 9:50 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 10 minutes.
From 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. is 3 hours, or 180 minutes.
From 1:00 p.m. to 1:15 p.m. is 15 minutes.

problems.stem: Jamal is picking up breakfast for his study group at a coffee shop. The prices, which include tax, are in the table. The shop opens at 6:30 every morning. Jamal orders two blueberry muffins, four lattes, and two drip coffees.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Jamal's order?

problems.stem: Sofia is buying laundry detergent. The store sells the same brand in the three sizes shown in the table. She does about six loads of laundry a week.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per fluid ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Luis has a recipe for a 6-inch round cake, but he wants to bake it in an 8-inch round pan instead, filled to the same depth. The oven is set to 325 degrees.
problems.ask: How many times the original recipe should Luis make to fill the bigger pan?

problems.stem: In a board game, Carmen's piece is stuck in the jail space. Under the house rules, she rolls a standard six-sided die three times, and she escapes if any roll is a 6. The board has 30 spaces in all.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Carmen escapes?
steps: Work with the opposite: one roll is not a 6 with probability 5/6.

problems.stem: Ingrid and three friends rent a lake cabin for a weekend. The rental costs $340, plus a $130 cleaning fee. They split the whole cost evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Ingrid plus three others makes 4 people.

problems.stem: Aiyana is putting laminate flooring in a rectangular bedroom that measures 10 feet by 8 feet. Each box of flooring covers 24 square feet and weighs 33 pounds. The store sells only whole boxes.
problems.ask: Ignoring waste, how many boxes does Aiyana need to buy?
steps: 3 boxes cover 3 × 24 = 72 square feet, which is not enough.
4 boxes cover 96 square feet, so Aiyana needs 4 boxes.

problems.stem: Caleb's company asked its employees how they usually get to work. Each person gave one answer, shown in the table. The office parking lot has 75 spaces.
problems.ask: What percent of the employees surveyed chose either "Drive" or "Bike"?

problems.stem: Raul owns 40 shares of a company's stock. On Monday the share price rose 50%. On Tuesday it fell 25% from Monday's closing price.
problems.ask: By what percent is Tuesday's closing price higher than the price before Monday's change?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
112.5 is 12.5 above 100, so it is 12.5% higher.

problems.stem: Sofia buys 23 stamps at the post office: some 60-cent postcard stamps and some 75-cent letter stamps. She spends $15.45 in all. There are 8 people in line behind her.
problems.ask: How many letter stamps does Sofia buy?
steps: Suppose all 23 were postcard stamps: 23 × 60 cents = 1,380 cents.
The real total is 1,545 cents, which is 1,545 cents − 1,380 cents = 165 cents more.
Each letter stamp adds 15 cents more than a postcard stamp, so there are 165 cents ÷ 15 cents = 11 letter stamps (check: 11 × 15 cents = 165 cents).

problems.stem: Lucia is shopping for a new bike helmet and finds one priced at $36. The sales tax where she lives is 6%, added at the register.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the bike helmet, including tax?

problems.stem: Luis is driving to his grandparents' farm. He drives 45 miles on the highway at a steady 60 miles per hour, then 20 miles on country roads at a steady 40 miles per hour. His car's gas tank holds 14 gallons.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 45 ÷ 60 = 3/4 hour, which is 45 minutes.
Second part: 20 ÷ 40 = 1/2 hour, which is 30 minutes.

problems.stem: June wants to buy a couch at a furniture store. The price is $1,236 if she pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $150 down, then 6 monthly payments of $186. The couch is 90 inches long.
problems.ask: How much more would June pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Ingrid leans a 25-foot ladder against the side of her house to clean the gutters. For safety, the bottom of the ladder sits 7 feet out from the wall, on level ground. The ladder is rated to hold 250 pounds.
problems.ask: How high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach, in feet?
steps: The wall, the ground and the ladder form a right triangle, with the ladder as the hypotenuse.

problems.stem: At a pizza shop, customers build a pizza by choosing exactly 2 different toppings from a list of 11. Every pizza also gets one of 2 crusts: thin or regular. A large pizza is cut into 12 slices. The order the toppings are chosen in doesn't matter.
problems.ask: How many different pizzas can a customer build?
steps: Pick 2 of 11 toppings: 11 × 10 = 110 ordered picks, ÷ 2 because order doesn't matter = 55 sets.
Each set can go with any of the 2 crusts: 55 × 2 = 110 pizzas.

problems.stem: Yuki spots a rolling suitcase with a price tag of $82. A sign on the rack says the price will be 25% off at the register.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the rolling suitcase, before tax?

problems.stem: Felix works at a bike shop for $16 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times his regular rate. The bike shop has 21 employees. Last week he worked 47 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Felix earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $16 = $24 an hour, for 47 − 40 = 7 hours.

problems.stem: Ben built a rectangular backyard pond that is 10 feet long, 6 feet wide and 2.5 feet deep, and he stocked it with nine goldfish. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the pond hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Fatima mixed 11 liters of liquid plant food that is 30% concentrate. The label says seedlings need a mix that is only 12% concentrate, so she will dilute it with water. She is growing seven trays of seedlings.
problems.ask: How many liters of water should Fatima add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 12% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 30/12 = 5/2: 11 × 5/2 = 27.5 liters.

problems.stem: Caleb slides a tray of muffins into the oven when the kitchen clock reads 1:46. The recipe says to bake them for 24 minutes. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 46 × 6 = 276 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 1 × 30 + 46 × 0.5 = 53 degrees past the 12.
That's more than 180, so the smaller angle is 360 − 223 = 137 degrees.

problems.stem: Chloe is sewing curtains. The fabric she likes costs $30 for 4 yards, and the shop sells it by the yard at that same rate. She needs 11 yards.
problems.ask: How much will the fabric cost?

problems.stem: On a trip to Mexico, Fatima exchanges money at a rate of 20 pesos per U.S. dollar. At an outdoor market, she buys a woven blanket for 660 pesos and a pair of sandals for 160 pesos. She has five days left on the trip.
problems.ask: How much did Fatima spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Paige buys a monthly bus pass. Last year the pass cost $90, and this year the transit agency raised the price to $99. She rides the bus about 20 days a month.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bus pass increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $9 ÷ $90 = 1/10 = 0.1.
As a percent, that is an increase of 10%.

problems.stem: Ruth is mixing concrete for a garden path that is 15 feet long. Her mix uses cement, sand and gravel in the ratio 2:1:2 by volume. She needs 40 buckets of mix in all.
problems.ask: How many more buckets of gravel than sand does Ruth need?
steps: Gravel minus sand: 2 − 1 = 1 part, and 1 × 8 = 8 buckets.

problems.stem: Theo wants to start going to a climbing gym and is choosing between the two plans in the table. The gym is open until 11 o'clock on weeknights.
problems.ask: For how many visits would the two plans cost exactly the same?
steps: Member plan costs $70 more up front.
Basic plan costs $5 more per visit, so each visit closes the gap by $5.
Check: $80 + 14 × $6 = $164 and $10 + 14 × $11 = $164, so the answer is 14 visits.

problems.stem: Ben's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 70 minutes.
problems.ask: What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
steps: With 17 values in order, the median is the 9th value.
Running totals: through 0: 1, through 1: 4, through 2: 5, through 3: 6, through 4: 11, through 5: 17.
The 9th value falls in the row for 4 goals, so the median is 4 goals.

problems.stem: A café asked 64 regular customers which drinks they had ordered in the past month. The results are in the table. The "Iced coffee" and "Hot tea" counts include the customers who ordered both drinks. The café has 9 tables.
problems.ask: How many customers ordered both drinks?
steps: So the extra count is the 'both' group: 32 − 27 = 5.

problems.stem: Malik orders takeout noodles and dumplings for the family. The order comes to $88.60, and he adds a 15% tip for the delivery driver.
problems.ask: How much does Malik pay in all, including the tip?

problems.stem: Victor must be at work by 9:15 a.m. for a meeting. He walks 10 minutes to the train station, rides the train for 30 minutes, and then walks 10 minutes to the office. A train ticket costs $3, and a train leaves the moment he reaches the platform. It is 8:10 a.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Victor wait before leaving home?
steps: From 8:10 a.m. to 9:15 a.m. is 65 minutes.

problems.stem: Raul's world history grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and his average so far. There are 25 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Raul need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 88?
steps: To finish at 88, the final must add 88 − 59.8 = 28.2 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 28.2 ÷ 0.3 = 94.

problems.stem: Arjun set out on his bike along the river trail, riding at a steady 9 miles per hour. Eli left from the same spot 20 minutes later and followed the same trail at a steady 15 miles per hour. The trail is 25 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting did Eli catch up to Arjun?
steps: Head start: in 20 minutes (1/3 hour), Arjun covers 9 × 1/3 = 3 miles.
Time to close the gap: 3 ÷ 6 = 1/2 hour = 30 minutes.

problems.stem: Ingrid is four times as old as her niece, Rosa. This spring they planted 9 tomato plants together. In 16 years, Ingrid will be twice as old as Rosa.
problems.ask: How old is Rosa now, in years?
steps: Let Rosa's age now be x, so Ingrid is 4x.
Subtract 2x and 16 from both sides: 2x = 32 − 16 = 16, so x = 8.
So Rosa is 8 years old now. Check: in 16 years, 48 = 2 × 24.

problems.stem: Omar keeps a weather log for a science project. The daily high temperatures from Monday to Friday were 86, 74, 87, 72, and 81 degrees Fahrenheit.
problems.ask: What was the average daily high for those five days, in degrees?

problems.stem: Leah is picking up sandwiches for the noon volunteer shift at the food bank. The deli sells sandwiches in packs of 6 for $4.50, or one at a time for $0.85 each. Eleven volunteers are on the list, and Leah wants at least one sandwich per person. Leftovers are fine, but she can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Leah can spend?
steps: 11 ÷ 6 = 1 full packs, with 5 people left over.

problems.stem: Hana ran the ticket table for the drama club's spring play and sold 62 tickets in all. Adult tickets cost $8 and student tickets cost $4. The auditorium has 400 seats, and at the end of the night the cash box held $344 from ticket sales.
problems.ask: How many adult tickets did Hana sell?
steps: If all 62 were student tickets, the total would be 62 × $4 = $248.
The actual total is $344 − $248 = $96 more than that.
Each adult ticket brings in $4 more than each student ticket, so adult tickets: $96 ÷ $4 = 24.

problems.stem: Fatima and Ravi are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Fatima could paint it in 6 hours, and Ravi could paint it in 12 hours. The fence is 200 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Fatima does 1/6 of the fence and Ravi does 1/12.
Together: 1/6 + 1/12 = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: Tess is saving for a new bike. She puts $16 in a jar the first week, and every week after that she puts in $1 more than the week before. She started the plan on her 12th birthday.
problems.ask: How much will Tess have saved in all after 13 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 13, week 2 with week 12, and so on: each pair adds to $16 + $28 = $44.
With 13 weeks, the average week is $44 ÷ 2 = $22, so the total is 13 × $22 = $286.

problems.stem: Kenji is saving for a camping tent that costs $390. He already has $65 saved and puts away $25 each week.
problems.ask: How many more weeks will it take Kenji to have exactly enough?

problems.stem: Hugo's pancake recipe makes 12 pancakes and calls for 1 1/2 cups of flour. He is making 16 pancakes for a family brunch. The recipe says to cook each pancake for 2 minutes per side.
problems.ask: If he scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of flour will he need?

problems.stem: Amara ordered lunch from a café for a team meeting that ran 60 minutes. The order was three sandwich boxes at $13 each plus a fruit tray for $7. Sales tax is 8%, and she added a 20% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the lunch order, including tax and tip?

problems.stem: At the warehouse where Chloe works, the 20 workers on the day shift packed an average of 67 boxes each on Monday. The 10 workers on the night shift, which started at 11 p.m., packed an average of 52 boxes each.
problems.ask: What was the average number of boxes packed per worker across both shifts?

problems.stem: Zoe's booth at the town festival has 12 rubber ducks floating in a pool. A player pays $3, picks one duck at random, and wins the prize marked underneath; the duck then goes back in. The table shows the prizes. The festival lasts 6 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the booth make per game after paying out prizes?
steps: If each duck came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $5 + 5 × $2 = $15.
The booth keeps $3 − $1.25 = $1.75 per game on average.

problems.stem: Eli runs to the pet store for his dog. He buys a bag of treats for $5.75, a chew toy for $3.50, and a new leash for $11.50. There's no sales tax, and he pays with a $50 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Eli get back?

problems.stem: Ezra is planning a road trip to the coast with a paper map. On the map, 1 inch represents 10 miles. The route has two straight stretches: the first measures 2 inches, and the second measures 3 inches. He plans to leave at 7 in the morning.
problems.ask: How many miles long is the route?

problems.stem: Imani bought a used car for $20,000. Her mechanic estimates that the car will lose 20% of its value each year, based on what it is worth at the start of that year. The car gets about 34 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: Using that estimate, how much value will the car lose over the 2 years?

problems.stem: Omar rode his bike 24 miles to a lake, mostly uphill, averaging 6 miles per hour. He rode home the same way, mostly downhill, at 12 miles per hour. He packed two bottles of water for the ride.
problems.ask: What was Omar's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 48 ÷ 6 = 8 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: On level ground, Ingrid holds a 3-foot yardstick straight up, and its shadow is 2 feet long. At the same moment, the shadow of a nearby flagpole is 60 feet long. The flagpole was put up 22 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the flagpole, in feet?
steps: The sun hits both at the same angle, so height ÷ shadow is the same for the flagpole and the yardstick: 3 ÷ 2.
The flagpole's shadow is 60 ÷ 2 = 30 times as long as the yardstick's.
So the flagpole is 30 × 3 = 90 feet tall.

bonus.stem: Jade buys a dog bed and a leash at a pet store for $28 in total. The dog bed costs exactly $15 more than the leash.
bonus.ask: How much does the dog bed cost?
steps: Call the price of the leash x, so the dog bed costs x + $15.

problems.stem: Wes is building a rectangular pen for his chickens that measures 26 feet by 6 feet. He'll fence all four sides.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Wes need?
steps: One length plus one width: 26 + 6 = 32 feet.
Going all the way around doubles that: 2 × 32 = 64 feet.

problems.stem: Ruth is shopping for a desk chair. The one she wants normally sells for $195, but it's on sale for 40% off. The cashier then applies an extra 20% off the sale price for new members. The store is 5 miles from her home.
problems.ask: How much does Ruth pay for the desk chair, before tax?
steps: 40% of $195 is $78, so the sale price is $195 − $78 = $117.
The extra 20% comes off $117, not the original price: 20% of $117 is $23.40.

problems.stem: Hana bought a pair of running shoes at a sporting-goods store during a 20%-off sale, and she also used a $5 coupon. The register took 20% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. Only two pairs in her size were left on the shelf. Before tax, Hana paid $51.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the shoes?
steps: $56 is what was left after 20% off, so it is 80% of the original price.

problems.stem: Algae is spreading across the pond on Esme's farm. Right now it covers 3 square feet, and the area it covers doubles every 3 days. The pond is about 6 feet deep.
problems.ask: If it keeps doubling at this rate, how many square feet will the algae cover 12 days from now?

problems.stem: Mei and Chloe are 154 miles apart on the same highway and drive toward each other to meet for dinner. Mei drives at 50 miles per hour, and Chloe drives at 60 miles per hour. They leave at the same time. Mei's car holds 11 gallons of gas.
problems.ask: How many minutes after they leave do they meet?
steps: The gap closes at 50 + 60 = 110 miles per hour.

problems.stem: Marcus is running a lemonade stand. He makes four pitchers of lemonade, and each pitcher holds 6 cups. There are 4 cups in a quart.
problems.ask: How many quarts of lemonade does Marcus make?
steps: There are 4 cups in a quart: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 quarts.

problems.stem: Imani is driving to a state park, which is 240 miles from home, and then driving back. Her car gets 40 miles per gallon, and gas costs $3.00 per gallon. Her car's tank holds 12 gallons.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the round trip?

problems.stem: Paige is painting the four walls of her home office, which is 20 feet long, 15 feet wide and 10 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. The door and windows take up 50 square feet that won't be painted. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $32 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Paige need to buy?
steps: Minus the door and windows: 700 − 50 = 650 square feet.
1,300 ÷ 350 ≈ 3.7, which is more than 3, so round up to 4 gallons.

problems.stem: Silas is writing a report about his town. Its population shrank by 10% from 2016 to 2020, then grew by 20% from 2020 to 2024. The town has 6 public parks.
problems.ask: By what percent is the 2024 population higher than the 2016 population?
steps: Start with a population of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
108 is 8 above 100, so it is 8% higher.

problems.stem: Ingrid, Yuki, Zoe and two of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Ingrid, Yuki and Zoe are triplets and want to stand together, side by side. The photographer charges $75 for the session.
problems.ask: In how many different orders can the 5 of them line up?
steps: Glue the three into one block, leaving 3 units: 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 orders.
Inside the block the three can be ordered 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 ways.

bonus.stem: Before a chess tournament, each of the 21 players shakes hands with every other player once. Ben, the organizer, just watches.
bonus.ask: How many handshakes are there in all?
steps: Each of the 21 players takes part in 20 handshakes: 21 × 20 = 420.
That counts every one twice (once for each person in it), so divide by 2: 420 ÷ 2 = 210.

problems.stem: Jordan is tiling a small laundry room floor that measures 9 feet by 3 feet. He picked square tiles that are 6 inches on each side, and they fit exactly with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many tiles does Jordan need?
steps: 6 inches is half a foot, so 2 tiles fit in each foot.
Along the length: 9 × 2 = 18. Along the width: 3 × 2 = 6.

problems.stem: Sam is stocking up at a garden center for his spring planting. The prices, with tax included, are in the table. The garden center is 3 miles from his house. Sam orders four seed packets, one tomato plant, and three flower pots.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Sam's order?

problems.stem: Malik is buying laundry detergent. The store sells the same brand in the three sizes shown in the table. He does about three loads of laundry a week.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per fluid ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Dev is making trail mix for a weekend hike. His recipe mixes peanuts, raisins and chocolate chips in the ratio 6:5:1 by weight. He wants 96 ounces of trail mix in all, which he'll pack into four bags.
problems.ask: How many more ounces of peanuts than raisins will the mix contain?
steps: Peanuts minus raisins: 6 − 5 = 1 part, and 1 × 8 = 8 ounces.

problems.stem: Owen needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. He plans to pick up the car at 9:15 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $9 more up front.
Company B costs $0.05 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.05.

problems.stem: Diego and Lucia are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Diego could paint it in 6 hours, and Lucia could paint it in 12 hours. The fence is 120 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Diego does 1/6 of the fence and Lucia does 1/12.
Together: 1/6 + 1/12 = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: At the school fair, a spinner has 8 equal sections, and two of them are marked Prize. Eli trades 4 tickets for two spins.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Eli lands on Prize at least once?
steps: Work with the opposite: one spin misses Prize with probability 6/8 = 3/4.

problems.stem: At 12:40 p.m., Nadia started a volunteer shift at the library. The shift ended at 4:40 p.m., and she walked home.
problems.ask: How many minutes long was the shift?
steps: From 12:40 p.m. to 1:00 p.m. is 20 minutes.
From 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 3 hours, or 180 minutes.
From 4:00 p.m. to 4:40 p.m. is 40 minutes.

problems.stem: Jade has taken four chemistry tests this term and scored 78, 89, 85, and 80. There are 34 students in the class, and one test is left. She wants her average on all five tests to be exactly 85.
problems.ask: What score does Jade need on the last test?
steps: An average of 85 over 5 tests means a total of 85 × 5 = 425.

problems.stem: Sofia works at the town library and asked visitors their main reason for coming in. Each visitor gave one answer, shown in the table. The library is open 64 hours a week.
problems.ask: What percent of the visitors surveyed did not choose "Borrow books"?

problems.stem: Yuki is ordering pizza for eight friends. The pizzeria sells round pizzas in two sizes: a 12-inch small and an 18-inch large, where the size is the diameter. Both have the same crust and toppings.
problems.ask: The large pizza has how many times the area of the small pizza?

problems.stem: Ava keeps a tin of cookies on her desk. It holds 5 chocolate chip cookies and 8 oatmeal cookies, all the same size. The tin was a gift from her neighbor 3 years ago. Without looking, she takes out two cookies, one after the other, and doesn't put either back.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both cookies are the same kind?

problems.stem: A toaster at the local store is marked $40. Paige decides to buy it, and 6% sales tax is added at checkout.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the toaster, including tax?

problems.stem: Ava is sealing a rectangular concrete patio that is 21 feet long and 14 feet wide. One gallon of sealer covers 50 square feet, and it needs 24 hours to dry. Sealer is sold only by the whole gallon.
problems.ask: How many gallons must Ava buy to give the patio one coat?
steps: 5 gallons cover 5 × 50 = 250 square feet, which is not enough.
6 gallons cover 300 square feet, so Ava needs 6 gallons.

problems.stem: Raul built a rectangular backyard pond that is 10 feet long, 4 feet wide and 2 feet deep, and he stocked it with twelve goldfish. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the pond hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Ruth has 39 ounces of a cleaning spray that is 30% vinegar. For washing windows, she wants a weaker spray that is only 10% vinegar, so she'll add water. She has ten windows to clean.
problems.ask: How many ounces of water should Ruth add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 10% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 30/10 = 3: 39 × 3 = 117 ounces.

problems.stem: Tess buys 24 stamps at the post office: some 60-cent postcard stamps and some 75-cent letter stamps. She spends $15.90 in all. There are 9 people in line behind her.
problems.ask: How many postcard stamps does Tess buy?
steps: Suppose all 24 were postcard stamps: 24 × 60 cents = 1,440 cents.
The real total is 1,590 cents, which is 1,590 cents − 1,440 cents = 150 cents more.
Each letter stamp adds 15 cents more than a postcard stamp, so there are 150 cents ÷ 15 cents = 10 letter stamps (check: 10 × 15 cents = 150 cents).

bonus.stem: The bell in the town hall tower rings once for each hour, with the rings evenly spaced. Zoe times it at 6 o'clock: 20 seconds pass from the first ring to the last.
bonus.ask: How many seconds does it take from the first ring to the last at 12 o'clock?
steps: 6 rings have only 5 gaps between them, so each gap is 20 ÷ 5 = 4 seconds.

problems.stem: Leah and four friends go bowling. The lanes cost $64 for the night, and shoe rentals add $24.50. They split the total evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Leah plus four others makes 5 people.

problems.stem: Theo bikes to work. He rides 9 miles on a bike path at a steady 15 miles per hour, then 3 miles through city streets at a steady 6 miles per hour. His bike has 17 gears.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 9 ÷ 15 = 3/5 hour, which is 36 minutes.
Second part: 3 ÷ 6 = 1/2 hour, which is 30 minutes.

problems.stem: Ava buys a monthly bus pass. Last year the pass cost $115, and this year the transit agency raised the price to $138. She rides the bus about 23 days a month.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bus pass increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $23 ÷ $115 = 1/5 = 0.2.
As a percent, that is an increase of 20%.

problems.stem: Ingrid's class kept track of how many books each student read over winter break, and the table shows the results. The school library lets each student borrow up to ten books at a time.
problems.ask: What is the median number of books read over the break?
steps: With 23 values in order, the median is the 12th value.
Running totals: through 0: 2, through 1: 8, through 2: 11, through 3: 14, through 4: 22, through 5: 23.
The 12th value falls in the row for 3 books, so the median is 3 books.

problems.stem: Tess snaps a photo of the clock tower in the town square at exactly 9:10. The tower is 75 feet tall. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 10 × 6 = 60 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 9 × 30 + 10 × 0.5 = 275 degrees past the 12.
That's more than 180, so the smaller angle is 360 − 215 = 145 degrees.

bonus.stem: Grace numbered every page of a long report, starting at 1, one digit at a time. When she finished, she had printed 894 digits in all.
bonus.ask: How many pages does the report have?
steps: Pages 1–9 use 9 digits and pages 10–99 use 90 × 2 = 180, so 189 digits through page 99.
Digits left: 894 − 189 = 705. Each page from 100 on uses 3: 705 ÷ 3 = 235 pages.
Those are pages 100 through 334, so there are 334 pages.

problems.stem: June spots a winter jacket with a price tag of $160. A sign on the rack says the price will be 30% off at the register.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the winter jacket, before tax?

problems.stem: Aiyana works at a hotel for $14 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times her regular rate. Her commute is 7 miles each way. Last week she worked 49 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Aiyana earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $14 = $21 an hour, for 49 − 40 = 9 hours.

problems.stem: Hana's biology grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and her average so far. There are 22 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Hana need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 85?
steps: To finish at 85, the final must add 85 − 59.5 = 25.5 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 25.5 ÷ 0.3 = 85.

problems.stem: Malik is building a wooden garden gate shaped like a rectangle, 30 inches wide and 40 inches tall. To keep it from sagging, he will nail a straight brace from one corner to the opposite corner. The gate will hang on two hinges.
problems.ask: How long must the brace be, in inches?
steps: The brace is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs equal to the width and height.

problems.stem: Eli surveyed all 64 students in his grade about pets at home. The results are in the table. The "Has a dog" and "Has a cat" counts include the students who have both a dog and a cat. He handed out the surveys during a 16-minute homeroom.
problems.ask: How many of the 64 students have neither a dog nor a cat?

bonus.stem: Today is Thursday. Dev will be away for the next 48 days, starting tomorrow. Trash is picked up every Sunday morning, so his neighbor has offered to take the bins out while he is gone.
bonus.ask: How many Sunday pickups will fall during those 48 days?
steps: Each full week has exactly one Sunday: 6.
The 6 extra days fall on the same weekdays as the first 6: Friday through Wednesday, which includes one more Sunday.

problems.stem: A farm stand sells a 5-pound bag of apples for $12.50. Dmitri wants 3 pounds for pies, and the stand will weigh out any amount at the same price per pound.
problems.ask: How much will 3 pounds of apples cost?

problems.stem: On a trip to Mexico, Felix exchanges money at a rate of 20 pesos per U.S. dollar. At an outdoor market, he buys a woven blanket for 520 pesos and a pair of sandals for 160 pesos. He has three days left on the trip.
problems.ask: How much did Felix spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Malik wants to buy a couch at a furniture store. The price is $805 if he pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $200 down, then 10 monthly payments of $73. The couch is 90 inches long.
problems.ask: How much more would Malik pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: At the warehouse where Nico works, the 11 workers on the day shift packed an average of 78 boxes each on Monday. The 19 workers on the night shift, which started at 11 p.m., packed an average of 48 boxes each.
problems.ask: What was the average number of boxes packed per worker across both shifts?

problems.stem: Sofia is four times as old as her nephew, Tariq. Every summer the two of them go fishing at a lake 19 miles from home. In 12 years, Sofia will be twice as old as Tariq.
problems.ask: How old is Sofia now, in years?
steps: Let Tariq's age now be x, so Sofia is 4x.
Subtract 2x and 12 from both sides: 2x = 24 − 12 = 12, so x = 6.
So Sofia is 4 × 6 = 24 years old now. Check: in 12 years, 36 = 2 × 18.

problems.stem: Kenji bowled four games at his league night on Saturday. His scores were 164, 167, 174, and 187.
problems.ask: What was Kenji's average score for the four games?

problems.stem: Ingrid must be at work by 8:45 a.m. for a meeting. She walks 10 minutes to the train station, rides the train for 25 minutes, and then walks 10 minutes to the office. A train ticket costs $2.25, and a train leaves the moment she reaches the platform. It is 7:35 a.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Ingrid wait before leaving home?
steps: From 7:35 a.m. to 8:45 a.m. is 70 minutes.

problems.stem: Dev's swim team held a car wash to raise money. They charged $7 for each car and $9 for each truck or SUV. Over six hours on Saturday, they washed 183 vehicles and collected $1,355.
problems.ask: How many trucks and SUVs did the team wash?
steps: If all 183 were cars, the total would be 183 × $7 = $1,281.
The actual total is $1,355 − $1,281 = $74 more than that.
Each truck or SUV brings in $2 more than each car, so trucks and SUVs: $74 ÷ $2 = 37.

problems.stem: Isaac paddled a kayak 12 miles upstream at 4 miles per hour, then turned around and paddled the same 12 miles back downstream at 6 miles per hour. His kayak is 14 feet long.
problems.ask: What was Isaac's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 24 ÷ 5 = 4.8 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: At an ice cream stand, customers build a sundae by choosing exactly 3 different toppings from a list of 8. Every sundae also gets one of 2 ice cream flavors: vanilla or chocolate. Each sundae comes in a 16-ounce cup. The order the toppings are chosen in doesn't matter.
problems.ask: How many different sundaes can a customer build?
steps: Pick 3 of 8 toppings: 8 × 7 × 6 = 336 ordered picks, ÷ 6 (the 3 × 2 × 1 orders of the same three) = 56 sets.
Each set can go with any of the 2 ice cream flavors: 56 × 2 = 112 sundaes.

bonus.stem: A hallway at Lucia's school has 178 closed lockers, numbered 1 to 178. Then 178 students walk by one at a time. Student 1 opens every locker. Student 2 switches every 2nd locker (closing it if open, opening it if closed), student 3 switches every 3rd locker, and so on, until student 178 switches only locker 178.
bonus.ask: How many lockers are closed at the end?
steps: A locker is switched once for each number that divides it (locker 12: by 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12).
Divisors come in pairs (1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4), so most lockers are switched an even number of times and end closed.
Only perfect squares have an odd number of divisors, because one pair repeats (6 × 6 = 36).
Perfect squares up to 178: 1, 4, 9, …, 169, which is 13 lockers open.

problems.stem: Arjun and two coworkers stop at a diner for breakfast, and Arjun offers to pay. The check is $54.80. He plans to add a 20% tip on the full check.
problems.ask: How much is the tip?

problems.stem: A muffin recipe makes 6 muffins and uses 1 1/2 cups of sugar. Esme needs 4 muffins for a school bake sale. The muffins bake at 375 degrees for 20 minutes.
problems.ask: If she scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of sugar will she need?

problems.stem: Isaac deposited $2,400 in a savings account that earns 4% interest, compounded once a year. He won't add or take out any money. The bank requires a $25 minimum balance.
problems.ask: How much interest will Isaac earn over the 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 4% of $2,400 is $96, so the value goes to $2,400 + $96 = $2,496.

problems.stem: Elena is painting the four walls of her living room, which is 18 feet long, 16 feet wide and 9 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. The door and windows take up 60 square feet that won't be painted. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $32 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Elena need to buy?
steps: Minus the door and windows: 612 − 60 = 552 square feet.
1,104 ÷ 350 ≈ 3.2, which is more than 3, so round up to 4 gallons.

problems.stem: Priya started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 4 miles per hour. Omar started running from the same spot 12 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 6 miles per hour. The path is 6 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Omar catch up to Priya?
steps: Head start: in 12 minutes (1/5 hour), Priya covers 4 × 1/5 = 0.8 miles.
Time to close the gap: 0.8 ÷ 2 = 2/5 hour = 24 minutes.

problems.stem: Grace is signing up for pottery classes at a local studio, which offers the two options in the table. Each class lasts 150 minutes.
problems.ask: How many classes in a month would make the two options cost exactly the same?
steps: Drop-in costs $4 more per class, so each class closes the gap by $4.
Check: $20 + 5 × $10 = $70 and $0 + 5 × $14 = $70, so the answer is 5 classes.

problems.stem: Amara's booth at the town festival has 10 rubber ducks floating in a pool. A player pays $2, picks one duck at random, and wins the prize marked underneath; the duck then goes back in. The table shows the prizes. The festival lasts 8 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the booth make per game after paying out prizes?
steps: If each duck came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $5 + 3 × $2 = $11.
The booth keeps $2 − $1.10 = $0.90 per game on average.

problems.stem: Noor is working on a 750-piece jigsaw puzzle. She has placed 450 pieces so far and places 25 more pieces each night.
problems.ask: How many more nights will it take to finish the puzzle?

problems.stem: Owen is picking up bagels for the team's 9:30 a.m. meeting. The bakery sells bagels in packs of 4 for $4, or one at a time for $1.10 each. 21 people are coming, and Owen wants at least one bagel per person. Leftovers are fine, but he can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Owen can spend?
steps: 21 ÷ 4 = 5 full packs, with 1 person left over.

problems.stem: Caleb's company asked its employees how they usually get to work. Each person gave one answer, shown in the table. The office parking lot has 60 spaces.
problems.ask: What percent of the employees surveyed chose either "Drive" or "Bike"?

problems.stem: Kofi takes a 500-milligram dose of a medicine at 7:30 a.m. with a glass of water. The amount of the medicine in the body drops by half every 5 hours.
problems.ask: How many milligrams of the medicine are left in his body 25 hours after the dose?

problems.stem: Zoe, who is 6 feet tall, stands on level ground and notices that her shadow is 3 feet long. At the same moment, the shadow of a nearby oak tree is 44 feet long. The tree was planted about 25 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the oak tree, in feet?
steps: The sun hits both at the same angle, so height ÷ shadow is the same for the oak tree and Zoe: 6 ÷ 3.
Height of the oak tree = 44 × 6 ÷ 3 = 264 ÷ 3 = 88 feet.

problems.stem: Esme is fencing in a rectangular play area for her kids. The area is 27 feet long and 23 feet wide. One 27-foot side runs along the garage wall, so it needs no fence.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Esme need?
steps: Fence the other 27-foot side and both 23-foot sides.

problems.stem: Ezra is planning a hike with a trail map where 1 centimeter represents 2 kilometers. The trail to the waterfall measures 5 centimeters on the map, and the trail back to the parking lot measures 1.5 centimeters. The parking lot has 70 spaces.
problems.ask: How many kilometers long is the whole hike?

problems.stem: Tariq took his family out for brunch at a diner that opened 20 years ago. They ordered four pancake plates at $22 each and a pitcher of orange juice for $8. Sales tax is 5%, and they added a 20% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the brunch, including tax and tip?

problems.stem: Isaac is writing a report about his town. Its population grew by 20% from 2016 to 2020, then shrank by 10% from 2020 to 2024. The town has 12 public parks.
problems.ask: By what percent is the 2024 population higher than the 2016 population?
steps: Start with a population of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
108 is 8 above 100, so it is 8% higher.

problems.stem: Amara is saving for a new bike. She puts $20 in a jar the first week, and every week after that she puts in $1 more than the week before. She started the plan on her 15th birthday.
problems.ask: How much will Amara have saved in all after 20 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 20, week 2 with week 19, and so on: each pair adds to $20 + $39 = $59.

problems.stem: Marcus buys three cans of tomatoes for a big pot of chili. Each can holds 8 ounces, and there are 16 ounces in a pound.
problems.ask: How many pounds of tomatoes is that in all?
steps: There are 16 ounces in a pound: 24 ÷ 16 = 1.5 pounds.

problems.stem: Yuki has her eye on a desk chair with a regular price of $120. This week it's marked 20% off. At checkout, she also uses a coupon for an extra 25% off the sale price. She waited in line for 4 minutes to pay.
problems.ask: How much does Yuki pay for the desk chair, before tax?
steps: 20% of $120 is $24, so the sale price is $120 − $24 = $96.
The extra 25% comes off $96, not the original price: 25% of $96 is $24.

problems.stem: Tess bought a winter coat at a department store during a 50%-off sale, and she also used a $5 coupon. The register took 50% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. The sale lasted three days. Before tax, Tess paid $103.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the coat?
steps: $108 is what was left after 50% off, so it is 50% of the original price.

problems.stem: Andre and Eli are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Andre could paint it in 3 hours, and Eli could paint it in 6 hours. The fence is 150 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Andre does 1/3 of the fence and Eli does 1/6.
Together: 1/3 + 1/6 = 2/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: At the school fair, a spinner has 4 equal sections, and two of them are marked Prize. Tariq trades 5 tickets for two spins.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Tariq lands on Prize at least once?
steps: Work with the opposite: one spin misses Prize with probability 2/4 = 1/2.

problems.stem: Lena shops at the farmers market on Saturday morning. She buys a jar of honey for $7.25, a loaf of sourdough for $5.50, and a pint of blueberries for $3.99. There's no sales tax, and she pays with a $20 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Lena get back?

problems.stem: Hugo is stocking up at a garden center for his spring planting. The prices, with tax included, are in the table. The garden center is 3 miles from his house. Hugo orders three seed packets, two flower pots, and three tomato plants.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Hugo's order?

problems.stem: Ingrid is making trail mix for a weekend hike. Her recipe mixes peanuts, raisins and chocolate chips in the ratio 1:5:3 by weight. She wants 72 ounces of trail mix in all, which she'll pack into four bags.
problems.ask: How many ounces of chocolate chips should Ingrid use?

problems.stem: Nadia's living room has a round rug that is 6 feet across. She wants to replace it with a round rug that is 10 feet across. The room is 14 feet long.
problems.ask: The new rug will cover how many times as much floor area as the old rug?

problems.stem: Silas and Raul live 19 miles apart along a straight bike trail, and they ride toward each other to meet for lunch. Silas rides at 14 miles per hour, and Raul rides at 16 miles per hour. They leave at the same time. The trail has 14 benches along the way.
problems.ask: How many minutes after they leave do they meet?
steps: The gap closes at 14 + 16 = 30 miles per hour.

problems.stem: Ruth is tiling a small laundry room floor that measures 5 feet by 3 feet. She picked square tiles that are 6 inches on each side, and they fit exactly with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many tiles does Ruth need?
steps: 6 inches is half a foot, so 2 tiles fit in each foot.
Along the length: 5 × 2 = 10. Along the width: 3 × 2 = 6.

problems.stem: Jordan is driving to a college campus for a tour, which is 140 miles from home, and then driving back. His car gets 20 miles per gallon, and gas costs $3.50 per gallon. The drive takes about 3 hours each way, with one stop for lunch.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the round trip?

problems.stem: Esme built a rectangular backyard pond that is 8 feet long, 6 feet wide and 2.5 feet deep, and she stocked it with seven goldfish. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the pond hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Jamal mixed 10 cups of fruit punch that is 40% juice for a party. It tastes too sweet, so he wants to add water until the punch is only 25% juice. Eight guests are coming.
problems.ask: How many cups of water should Jamal add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 25% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 40/25 = 8/5: 10 × 8/5 = 16 cups.

problems.stem: Six friends, including Aiyana and Priya, have 6 seats together in one row at the movies. Aiyana and Priya both talk during movies, so the group agrees they won't sit side by side. The movie runs 105 minutes.
problems.ask: In how many different ways can the 6 friends fill the 6 seats?
steps: Orders with them together: glue them into a block, 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120, times 2 for their order = 240.

problems.stem: Rosa orders a pair of headphones that costs $40 before tax. Her state charges an 8% sales tax on the purchase.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the pair of headphones, including tax?

problems.stem: Isaac bowls in a league with 20 teams. So far this season he has bowled three games, scoring 195, 148, and 172. He wants his average after the next game to be exactly 170.
problems.ask: What score does Isaac need in the next game?
steps: An average of 170 over 4 games means a total of 170 × 4 = 680.

problems.stem: Caleb is stocking up on peanut butter and compares the three jar sizes in the table. He goes through about three jars a month.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Hugo is building a wooden garden gate shaped like a rectangle, 40 inches wide and 42 inches tall. To keep it from sagging, he will nail a straight brace from one corner to the opposite corner. The gate will hang on three hinges.
problems.ask: How long must the brace be, in inches?
steps: The brace is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs equal to the width and height.

problems.stem: Ben packed a cooler for a beach day with 6 bottles of lemonade and 5 bottles of iced tea. The beach is 26 miles from his apartment. Later, he reaches into the ice without looking and pulls out two bottles, one after the other.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both bottles are the same drink?

bonus.stem: Wes is helping sell tickets for an outdoor theater with 30 rows of seats. The front row has 18 seats, and each row behind it has 3 more seats than the row in front of it.
bonus.ask: How many seats are there in all?
steps: Pair the first and last rows, the second and second-to-last, and so on: each pair holds 18 + 105 = 123.

problems.stem: At 8:30 a.m., Omar started a volunteer shift at the library. The shift ended at 11:55 a.m., and he walked home.
problems.ask: How many minutes long was the shift?
steps: From 8:30 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. is 30 minutes.
From 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. is 2 hours, or 120 minutes.
From 11:00 a.m. to 11:55 a.m. is 55 minutes.

problems.stem: Noor is putting laminate flooring in a rectangular home office that measures 13 feet by 9 feet. Each box of flooring covers 20 square feet and weighs 34 pounds. The store sells only whole boxes.
problems.ask: Ignoring waste, how many boxes does Noor need to buy?
steps: 5 boxes cover 5 × 20 = 100 square feet, which is not enough.
6 boxes cover 120 square feet, so Noor needs 6 boxes.

problems.stem: Last month, a bag of coffee beans at Ezra's grocery store cost $20. This month the same bag costs $17.50. Ezra goes through about one bag every 9 days.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bag decrease?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $2.50 ÷ $20 = 1/8 = 0.125.
As a percent, that is a decrease of 12.5%.

problems.stem: Ravi's chemistry grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and his average so far. There are 24 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Ravi need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 85?
steps: To finish at 85, the final must add 85 − 61 = 24 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 24 ÷ 0.3 = 80.

problems.stem: Ben's class kept track of how many books each student read over winter break, and the table shows the results. The school library lets each student borrow up to six books at a time.
problems.ask: What is the median number of books read over the break?
steps: With 24 values in order, the median is the average of the 12th and 13th values.
Running totals: through 0: 4, through 1: 12, through 2: 17, through 3: 20, through 4: 22, through 5: 24.
They are 1 and 2, so the median is (1 + 2) ÷ 2 = 1.5 books.

problems.stem: Sofia rode her bike 21 miles to a lake, mostly uphill, averaging 6 miles per hour. She rode home the same way, mostly downhill, at 14 miles per hour. She packed three bottles of water for the ride.
problems.ask: What was Sofia's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 42 ÷ 5 = 8.4 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: A café asked 80 regular customers which drinks they had ordered in the past month. The results are in the table. The "Iced coffee" and "Hot tea" counts include the customers who ordered both drinks. The café has 10 tables.
problems.ask: How many customers ordered both drinks?
steps: So the extra count is the 'both' group: 41 − 36 = 5.

problems.stem: Leah spots a pair of hiking boots with a price tag of $90. A sign on the rack says the price will be 40% off at the register.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the pair of hiking boots, before tax?

problems.stem: Isaac works at a warehouse for $18 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times his regular rate. His shifts start at 7:00 each morning. Last week he worked 46 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Isaac earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $18 = $27 an hour, for 46 − 40 = 6 hours.

problems.stem: Imani helped run a pancake breakfast at the fire station. Adult plates cost $8 and kids' plates cost $4. They served 153 plates and took in $872, with nine volunteers working the griddles.
problems.ask: How many kids' plates did they serve?
steps: If all 153 were kids' plates, the total would be 153 × $4 = $612.
The actual total is $872 − $612 = $260 more than that.
Each adult plate brings in $4 more than each kids' plate, so adult plates: $260 ÷ $4 = 65.

problems.stem: Diego teaches two sections of algebra. On Friday's test, the 12 students in his first-period class averaged 88 points, and the 28 students in his fourth-period class averaged 83 points. The test had 20 questions.
problems.ask: What was the average score for all of the students in both classes together, in points?

problems.stem: The clock at the train station has a face 4 feet across. While Mei waits on the platform, it reads 7:07. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 7 × 6 = 42 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 7 × 30 + 7 × 0.5 = 213.5 degrees past the 12.
That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 171.5 degrees.

problems.stem: The bulk bin at the grocery store charges $8.50 for 2 pounds of trail mix. Isaac wants 3 pounds for a camping trip.
problems.ask: At the same price per pound, how much will 3 pounds cost?

problems.stem: On a trip to Mexico, Diego exchanges money at a rate of 20 pesos per U.S. dollar. At an outdoor market, he buys a painted bowl for 510 pesos and a straw hat for 250 pesos. He has six days left on the trip.
problems.ask: How much did Diego spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Jamal wants to buy a laptop at an electronics store. The price is $581 if he pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $100 down, then 6 monthly payments of $111. The laptop weighs about 3 pounds.
problems.ask: How much more would Jamal pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Wes needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. He plans to pick up the car at 8 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $15 more up front.
Company B costs $0.10 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.10.

problems.stem: Yuki is organizing a volleyball league with 7 teams this season. Every team will play every other team exactly once during the regular season. Each game takes about 30 minutes.
problems.ask: How many games will be played in the regular season?
steps: Each game is a pair of teams. Each of the 7 teams pairs with 6 others: 7 × 6 = 42.
That counts every pair twice, so divide by 2: 42 ÷ 2 = 21 pairs.
Each pair plays once, so there are 21 games.

problems.stem: Hana and four coworkers chip in for a retirement gift: a gift card worth $75 and a cake that costs $39. They split the cost evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Hana plus four others makes 5 people.

problems.stem: Luis bikes to work. He rides 12 miles on a bike path at a steady 15 miles per hour, then 2 miles through city streets at a steady 6 miles per hour. His bike has 14 gears.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 12 ÷ 15 = 4/5 hour, which is 48 minutes.
Second part: 2 ÷ 6 = 1/3 hour, which is 20 minutes.

problems.stem: Esme is painting the four walls of her basement playroom, which is 17 feet long, 11 feet wide and 10 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $42 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Esme need to buy?
steps: 1,120 ÷ 350 = 3.2, which is more than 3, so round up to 4 gallons.

problems.stem: Algae is spreading across the pond on Raul's farm. Right now it covers 5 square feet, and the area it covers doubles every 3 days. The pond is about 5 feet deep.
problems.ask: If it keeps doubling at this rate, how many square feet will the algae cover 12 days from now?

problems.stem: Ravi empties the cup holder in his car and finds nothing but dimes and nickels. There are 16 coins in all, worth $0.95 together. He has had the car for 6 years.
problems.ask: How many nickels are in the cup holder?
steps: Suppose all 16 were nickels: 16 × 5 cents = 80 cents.
The real total is 95 cents, which is 95 cents − 80 cents = 15 cents more.
Each dime adds 5 cents more than a nickel, so there are 15 cents ÷ 5 cents = 3 dimes.

problems.stem: Hugo bowled four games at his league night on Saturday. His scores were 124, 161, 144, and 139.
problems.ask: What was Hugo's average score for the four games?

problems.stem: A smoothie recipe makes 8 servings and calls for 1/2 cup of plain yogurt. Ruth is making 24 servings for her soccer team after practice. The yogurt was on sale for $3.50 a tub.
problems.ask: If she scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of yogurt will she need?

problems.stem: Jade's grandmother gave her $2,000 for her 17th birthday. She put all of it in a certificate of deposit that pays 2% interest, compounded once a year, and left it alone.
problems.ask: How much will the certificate of deposit be worth after 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 2% of $2,000 is $40, so the value goes to $2,000 + $40 = $2,040.

problems.stem: In March, the hardware store where Grace works raised the price of a garden hose by 20%. In June, the store put it on sale for 40% off that new price. Grace has worked at the store for 8 months.
problems.ask: By what percent is the June price lower than the original price?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
72 is 28 below 100, so it is 28% lower.

problems.stem: Carmen is four times as old as her son, Sam. Every summer the two of them go fishing at a lake 6 miles from home. Exactly 3 years ago, Carmen was five times as old as Sam.
problems.ask: How old is Sam now, in years?
steps: Let Sam's age now be x, so Carmen is 4x.
Move the x terms to one side: x = 15 − 3 = 12.
So Sam is 12 years old now. Check: 3 years ago, 45 = 5 × 9.

bonus.stem: It takes Rosa 30 minutes to saw a log into 6 pieces for the fire pit. Each cut takes the same amount of time.
bonus.ask: At the same pace, how many minutes would it take Rosa to saw an identical log into 14 pieces?
steps: 6 pieces take only 5 cuts, so each cut takes 30 ÷ 5 = 6 minutes.

problems.stem: Rosa takes her parents out for a birthday lunch. The bill comes to $53.60 before the tip, and she wants to leave a 15% tip on that amount.
problems.ask: How much does Rosa pay in all, including the tip?

problems.stem: Leah is baking a cake for a birthday party, and it must be frosted by 4:00 p.m. when the guests arrive. Baking takes 30 minutes, cooling takes 45 minutes, and frosting takes 20 minutes, one after another. The cake will feed 18 people. It is 2:05 p.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Leah wait before starting?
steps: From 2:05 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 115 minutes.

problems.stem: Yuki works at the town library and asked visitors their main reason for coming in. Each visitor gave one answer, shown in the table. The library is open 64 hours a week.
problems.ask: What percent of the visitors surveyed chose "Use computers"?

problems.stem: Maya and Noor are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Maya could paint it in 3 hours, and Noor could paint it in 7 hours. The fence is 150 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Maya does 1/3 of the fence and Noor does 1/7.
Together: 1/3 + 1/7 = 7/21 + 3/21 = 10/21 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: Mei, who is 5 feet tall, stands on level ground in the shadow of a flagpole, 10 feet from its base. Her own shadow is 4 feet long and points the same way, and its tip lands exactly on the tip of the flagpole's shadow. The flagpole was put up 28 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the flagpole, in feet?
steps: The flagpole's shadow runs past Mei to the same tip: 10 + 4 = 14 feet long.
Same sun angle, so height ÷ shadow matches: 5 ÷ 4 for Mei.

problems.stem: Nadia is reading a 300-page novel for her book club and has already read 60 pages. She plans to read 40 pages each day until she finishes.
problems.ask: How many more days will it take to finish the book?

problems.stem: Marcus is picking up donuts for the class's 8 a.m. study session. The donut shop sells donuts in packs of 4 for $3.50, or one at a time for $1.25 each. 23 students signed up, and Marcus wants at least one donut per person. Leftovers are fine, but he can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Marcus can spend?
steps: 23 ÷ 4 = 5 full packs, with 3 people left over.

problems.stem: Dev is making trail mix for a weekend hike. His recipe mixes peanuts, raisins and chocolate chips in the ratio 2:1:3 by weight. He wants 54 ounces of trail mix in all, which he'll pack into five bags.
problems.ask: How many ounces of peanuts should Dev use?

problems.stem: June's living room has a round rug that is 6 feet across. She wants to replace it with a round rug that is 10 feet across. The room is 14 feet long.
problems.ask: The new rug will cover how many times as much floor area as the old rug?

problems.stem: Caleb runs a prize wheel at the school fair. The wheel has 20 equal sections, each equally likely to land on top, and a spin costs $5. The table shows what the sections pay. The fair runs for 5 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the prize wheel make per spin after paying out prizes?
steps: If each section came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $10 + 5 × $2 = $20.
The booth keeps $5 − $1 = $4 per spin on average.

problems.stem: Fatima is planting a rectangular vegetable garden that measures 17 feet by 11 feet. She wants a short fence around it to keep rabbits out. One 17-foot side runs along the shed wall, so it needs no fence.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Fatima need?
steps: Fence the other 17-foot side and both 11-foot sides.

problems.stem: Aiyana is planning a road trip to the coast with a paper map. On the map, 1 inch represents 10 miles. The route has two straight stretches: the first measures 2 1/2 inches, and the second measures 4 1/4 inches. She plans to leave at 6 in the morning.
problems.ask: How many miles long is the route?

problems.stem: Grace took her family out for brunch at a diner that opened 40 years ago. They ordered two pancake plates at $13 each and a pitcher of orange juice for $15. Sales tax is 8%, and they added a 20% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the brunch, including tax and tip?

problems.stem: Last month, a bag of coffee beans at Noor's grocery store cost $10. This month the same bag costs $8.50. Noor goes through about one bag every 11 days.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bag decrease?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $1.50 ÷ $10 = 3/20 = 0.15.
As a percent, that is a decrease of 15%.

problems.stem: Amara has 19 ounces of a cleaning spray that is 20% vinegar. For washing windows, she wants a weaker spray that is only 8% vinegar, so she'll add water. She has fifteen windows to clean.
problems.ask: How many ounces of water should Amara add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 8% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 20/8 = 5/2: 19 × 5/2 = 47.5 ounces.

problems.stem: Hugo set out on his bike along the river trail, riding at a steady 11 miles per hour. Dmitri left from the same spot 30 minutes later and followed the same trail at a steady 16 miles per hour. The trail is 20 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting did Dmitri catch up to Hugo?
steps: Head start: in 30 minutes (1/2 hour), Hugo covers 11 × 1/2 = 5.5 miles.
Time to close the gap: 5.5 ÷ 5 = 11/10 hours = 66 minutes.

problems.stem: Owen and his brother flip a coin each night to decide who washes the dinner dishes; heads means Owen washes. This week they'll flip for six nights in a row. Dinner is usually ready by 6:00 each evening.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Owen washes the dishes at least once in those 6 nights?
steps: Work with the opposite: Owen never washes only if every flip is tails. One flip is tails with probability 1/2.

problems.stem: June is running a lemonade stand. She makes eight pitchers of lemonade, and each pitcher holds 10 cups. There are 4 cups in a quart.
problems.ask: How many quarts of lemonade does June make?
steps: There are 4 cups in a quart: 80 ÷ 4 = 20 quarts.

problems.stem: Victor is shopping for a camping tent. The one he wants normally sells for $170, but it's on sale for 30% off. The cashier then applies an extra 10% off the sale price for new members. The sale price is good for 8 more days.
problems.ask: How much does Victor pay for the camping tent, before tax?
steps: 30% of $170 is $51, so the sale price is $170 − $51 = $119.
The extra 10% comes off $119, not the original price: 10% of $119 is $11.90.

problems.stem: Hugo bought a desk lamp at a home-goods store during a 25%-off sale, and he also used a $5 coupon. The register took 25% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. The lamp came with two light bulbs in the box. Before tax, Hugo paid $22.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the lamp?
steps: $27 is what was left after 25% off, so it is 75% of the original price.

problems.stem: Felix leans a 25-foot ladder against the side of his house to clean the gutters. For safety, the bottom of the ladder sits 7 feet out from the wall, on level ground. The ladder is rated to hold 225 pounds.
problems.ask: How high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach, in feet?
steps: The wall, the ground and the ladder form a right triangle, with the ladder as the hypotenuse.

problems.stem: Sam and Mei are 102 miles apart on the same highway and drive toward each other to meet for dinner. Sam drives at 45 miles per hour, and Mei drives at 40 miles per hour. They leave at the same time. Sam's car holds 12 gallons of gas.
problems.ask: How many minutes after they leave do they meet?
steps: The gap closes at 45 + 40 = 85 miles per hour.

bonus.stem: A row of 12 stepping stones crosses a creek. Ruth starts on the bank, and each hop moves her forward one or two stones. She must end exactly on the last stone.
bonus.ask: In how many different ways can Ruth hop from the bank to the last stone?
steps: To land on stone k, the last move came from k − 1 or k − 2, so ways(k) = ways(k − 1) + ways(k − 2).

problems.stem: Lucia stops at the hardware store for a weekend project. She buys a box of screws for $4.25, a roll of tape for $4.89, and a paintbrush for $6.50. There's no sales tax, and she pays with a $20 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Lucia get back?

problems.stem: Dev has taken four algebra tests this term and scored 83, 82, 96, and 84. There are 33 students in the class, and one test is left. He wants his average on all five tests to be exactly 88.
problems.ask: What score does Dev need on the last test?
steps: An average of 88 over 5 tests means a total of 88 × 5 = 440.

problems.stem: The water trough at Aiyana's farm is a rectangular metal tank 8 feet long, 2 feet wide and 2 feet deep. It serves the five horses in the north pasture. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the trough hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Silas paddled a kayak 8 miles upstream at 2 miles per hour, then turned around and paddled the same 8 miles back downstream at 8 miles per hour. His kayak is 12 feet long.
problems.ask: What was Silas's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 16 ÷ 5 = 3.2 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Sofia is saving for a new bike. She puts $12 in a jar the first week, and every week after that she puts in $1.50 more than the week before. She started the plan on her 15th birthday.
problems.ask: How much will Sofia have saved in all after 17 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 17, week 2 with week 16, and so on: each pair adds to $12 + $36 = $48.
With 17 weeks, the average week is $48 ÷ 2 = $24, so the total is 17 × $24 = $408.

problems.stem: Caleb is tiling a small laundry room floor that measures 5 feet by 4 feet. He picked square tiles that are 12 inches on each side, and they fit exactly with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many tiles does Caleb need?
steps: 12 inches is 1 foot, so each tile covers 1 square foot.

problems.stem: Mei is stocking up at a garden center for her spring planting. The prices, with tax included, are in the table. The garden center is 3 miles from her house. Mei orders three watering cans, one flower pot, and one tomato plant.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Mei's order?

problems.stem: Grace is stocking up on peanut butter and compares the three jar sizes in the table. She goes through about three jars a month.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Paige teaches two sections of algebra. On Friday's test, the 6 students in her first-period class averaged 76 points, and the 14 students in her fourth-period class averaged 81 points. The test had 30 questions.
problems.ask: What was the average score for all of the students in both classes together, in points?

problems.stem: Six friends, including Dev and Esme, have 6 seats together in one row at the movies. Dev and Esme both talk during movies, so the group agrees they won't sit side by side. The movie runs 110 minutes.
problems.ask: In how many different ways can the 6 friends fill the 6 seats?
steps: Orders with them together: glue them into a block, 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120, times 2 for their order = 240.

bonus.stem: Ezra's mudroom bin holds 3 pairs of black gloves and 6 pairs of brown gloves, all jumbled together. Each glove fits only a left hand or only a right hand. It's still dark when Ezra heads out, so he grabs gloves without looking.
bonus.ask: What is the fewest gloves Ezra must grab to be sure of getting a left and a right glove of the same color?
steps: Worst case: every glove he grabs is a left glove: 3 + 6 = 9 gloves, and still no match.
Now only right gloves are left, so the next one matches a left glove of its color: 9 + 1 = 10 gloves.

problems.stem: At 12:30 p.m., Jade started a volunteer shift at the library. The shift ended at 4:25 p.m., and she walked home.
problems.ask: How many minutes long was the shift?
steps: From 12:30 p.m. to 1:00 p.m. is 30 minutes.
From 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 3 hours, or 180 minutes.
From 4:00 p.m. to 4:25 p.m. is 25 minutes.

problems.stem: Maya is sealing a rectangular concrete patio that is 19 feet long and 17 feet wide. One gallon of sealer covers 100 square feet, and it needs 24 hours to dry. Sealer is sold only by the whole gallon.
problems.ask: How many gallons must Maya buy to give the patio one coat?
steps: 3 gallons cover 3 × 100 = 300 square feet, which is not enough.
4 gallons cover 400 square feet, so Maya needs 4 gallons.

problems.stem: Owen's economics grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and his average so far. There are 30 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Owen need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 80?
steps: To finish at 80, the final must add 80 − 52.4 = 27.6 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 27.6 ÷ 0.3 = 92.

problems.stem: Priya's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 80 minutes.
problems.ask: What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
steps: With 32 values in order, the median is the average of the 16th and 17th values.
Running totals: through 0: 9, through 1: 16, through 2: 19, through 3: 23, through 4: 26, through 5: 32.
They are 1 and 2, so the median is (1 + 2) ÷ 2 = 1.5 goals.

problems.stem: A fruit bowl in Lena's kitchen holds 8 red apples and 6 green apples. She bought them at a farm stand that opened 23 years ago. On her way out the door, she grabs two apples at random, one after the other.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both apples are the same color?

bonus.stem: A snail at the bottom of a 22-foot well climbs 4 feet up the wall every day, then slides back 2 feet every night while it rests.
bonus.ask: On which day does the snail first reach the top of the well, if the first day of climbing is day 1?
steps: Each full day and night, the snail gains 4 − 2 = 2 feet.
On its last day it climbs 4 feet and never slides back, so it only needs to start that day at 22 − 4 = 18 feet.
Reaching 18 feet takes 18 ÷ 2 = 9 full days and nights.
It reaches the top on day 9 + 1 = 10.

problems.stem: June orders a bike helmet that costs $26 before tax. Her state charges a 6% sales tax on the purchase.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the bike helmet, including tax?

problems.stem: Ravi works at a garden center for $12 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times his regular rate. His commute is 7 miles each way. Last week he worked 45 hours.
