bonus.ask: At the same pace, how many minutes would it take Diego to saw an identical log into 14 pieces?
steps: 4 pieces take only 3 cuts, so each cut takes 27 ÷ 3 = 9 minutes.

problems.stem: Esme rode her bike to work four days this week. The rides took 30, 23, 28, and 35 minutes.
problems.ask: What was her average ride time, in minutes?

problems.stem: Lena is planning a road trip to the coast with a paper map. On the map, 1 inch represents 20 miles. The route has two straight stretches: the first measures 3 1/4 inches, and the second measures 2 1/2 inches. She plans to leave at 3 in the morning.
problems.ask: How many miles long is the route?

problems.stem: Kenji took his family out for brunch at a diner that opened 20 years ago. They ordered five pancake plates at $16 each and a pitcher of orange juice for $13. Sales tax is 8%, and they added a 20% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the brunch, including tax and tip?

problems.stem: Hugo started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 3 miles per hour. Grace started running from the same spot 12 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 5 miles per hour. The path is 5 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Grace catch up to Hugo?
steps: Head start: in 12 minutes (1/5 hour), Hugo covers 3 × 1/5 = 0.6 miles.
Time to close the gap: 0.6 ÷ 2 = 3/10 hour = 18 minutes.

problems.stem: Ben is four times as old as his son, Mateo. This spring they planted 17 tomato plants together. Exactly 6 years ago, Ben was seven times as old as Mateo.
problems.ask: How old is Mateo now, in years?
steps: Let Mateo's age now be x, so Ben is 4x.
Move the x terms to one side: 3x = 42 − 6 = 36, so x = 12.
So Mateo is 12 years old now. Check: 6 years ago, 42 = 7 × 6.

problems.stem: Omar picks up school supplies before classes start. He buys a binder for $4.25, a pack of pens for $3.25, and a calculator for $10.50. There's no sales tax, and he pays with a $20 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Omar get back?

problems.stem: A store is taking 20% off every winter coat, and Carmen finds one with a regular price of $175. She also has a member coupon that takes 20% off the already reduced price. The sale price is good for 9 more days.
problems.ask: How much does Carmen pay for the winter coat, before tax?
steps: 20% of $175 is $35, so the sale price is $175 − $35 = $140.
The extra 20% comes off $140, not the original price: 20% of $140 is $28.

problems.stem: Mei is painting the four walls of her living room, which is 18 feet long, 9 feet wide and 9 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. The door and windows take up 60 square feet that won't be painted. One gallon of paint covers 400 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $36 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Mei need to buy?
steps: Minus the door and windows: 486 − 60 = 426 square feet.
852 ÷ 400 ≈ 2.1, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

problems.stem: Andre and Elena are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Andre could paint it in 3 hours, and Elena could paint it in 7 hours. The fence is 200 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Andre does 1/3 of the fence and Elena does 1/7.
Together: 1/3 + 1/7 = 7/21 + 3/21 = 10/21 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: Nadia and her brother flip a coin each night to decide who washes the dinner dishes; heads means Nadia washes. This week they'll flip for six nights in a row. Dinner is usually ready by 6:30 each evening.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Nadia washes the dishes at least once in those 6 nights?
steps: Work with the opposite: Nadia never washes only if every flip is tails. One flip is tails with probability 1/2.

problems.stem: Hugo is building a rectangular pen for his chickens that measures 21 feet by 6 feet. One 21-foot side runs along the garage wall, so it needs no fence.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Hugo need?
steps: Fence the other 21-foot side and both 6-foot sides.

problems.stem: Ruth is baking a cake for a birthday party, and it must be frosted by 4:45 p.m. when the guests arrive. Baking takes 35 minutes, cooling takes 45 minutes, and frosting takes 15 minutes, one after another. The cake will feed 18 people. It is 2:55 p.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Ruth wait before starting?
steps: From 2:55 p.m. to 4:45 p.m. is 110 minutes.

problems.stem: Ravi bought a winter coat at a department store during a 10%-off sale, and he also used a $5 coupon. The register took 10% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. The sale lasted three days. Before tax, Ravi paid $103.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the coat?
steps: $108 is what was left after 10% off, so it is 90% of the original price.

problems.stem: Hana's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 70 minutes.
problems.ask: What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
steps: With 21 values in order, the median is the 11th value.
Running totals: through 0: 2, through 1: 3, through 2: 7, through 3: 12, through 4: 20, through 5: 21.
The 11th value falls in the row for 3 goals, so the median is 3 goals.

problems.stem: Isaac and Nico start at opposite ends of a 6-mile lakeside path and walk toward each other. Isaac walks at 2 miles per hour, and Nico walks at 3 miles per hour. Nico leaves 15 minutes after Isaac. The lake is about 9 feet deep in the middle.
problems.ask: How many minutes after Isaac leaves do they meet?
steps: Head start: in 15 minutes, Isaac covers 2 × 1/4 = 0.5 miles.
Distance left when Nico leaves: 6 − 0.5 = 5.5 miles.
Together they close 2 + 3 = 5 miles per hour: 5.5 ÷ 5 = 11/10 hours = 66 minutes after Nico leaves.
Counting from when Isaac leaves: 15 + 66 = 81 minutes.

problems.stem: Lucia is saving for a camping tent that costs $120. She already has $80 saved and puts away $5 each week.
problems.ask: How many more weeks will it take Lucia to have exactly enough?

problems.stem: Ravi is picking up bagels for the team's 8 a.m. meeting. The bakery sells bagels in packs of 6 for $6, or one at a time for $1.25 each. Ten people are coming, and Ravi wants at least one bagel per person. Leftovers are fine, but he can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Ravi can spend?
steps: 10 ÷ 6 = 1 full packs, with 4 people left over.

problems.stem: Leah works at the town library and asked visitors their main reason for coming in. Each visitor gave one answer, shown in the table. The library is open 48 hours a week.
problems.ask: What percent of the visitors surveyed did not choose "Borrow books"?

problems.stem: Sofia's chemistry grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and her average so far. There are 34 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Sofia need on the final exam to finish with exactly a 90?
steps: To finish at 90, the final must add 90 − 50 = 40 points.
The final is worth 40%, so the score needed is 40 ÷ 0.4 = 100.

problems.stem: Diego has a recipe for a 6-inch round cake, but he wants to bake it in a 9-inch round pan instead, filled to the same depth. The oven is set to 325 degrees.
problems.ask: How many times the original recipe should Diego make to fill the bigger pan?
steps: A circle's area is π × radius², so area grows with the square of the diameter.

problems.stem: Algae is spreading across the pond on Felix's farm. Right now it covers 5 square feet, and the area it covers doubles every 4 days. The pond is about 5 feet deep.
problems.ask: If it keeps doubling at this rate, how many square feet will the algae cover 20 days from now?

problems.stem: Victor, Kofi, Ben and two of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Victor, Kofi and Ben are triplets and want to stand together, side by side. The photographer charges $75 for the session.
problems.ask: In how many different orders can the 5 of them line up?
steps: Glue the three into one block, leaving 3 units: 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 orders.
Inside the block the three can be ordered 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 ways.

problems.stem: Jordan left home at 7:35 a.m. to drive to a lake cabin. He made no stops, and the dashboard clock read 9:55 a.m. when he pulled into the cabin's driveway.
problems.ask: How many minutes did the drive take?
steps: From 7:35 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. is 25 minutes.
From 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. is 1 hour, or 60 minutes.
From 9:00 a.m. to 9:55 a.m. is 55 minutes.

problems.stem: Kenji has taken three history tests this term and scored 72, 87, and 92. There are 29 students in the class, and one test is left. He wants his average on all four tests to be exactly 85.
problems.ask: What score does Kenji need on the last test?
steps: An average of 85 over 4 tests means a total of 85 × 4 = 340.

problems.stem: Paige is mixing concrete for a garden path that is 24 feet long. Her mix uses cement, sand and gravel in the ratio 1:4:2 by volume. She needs 63 buckets of mix in all.
problems.ask: How many buckets of gravel does Paige need?

problems.stem: A rectangular park near Andre's apartment is 720 meters long and 300 meters wide. Andre usually walks along two edges to get from one corner to the opposite corner. Today he cuts straight across the grass on the diagonal instead. The park has 19 benches.
problems.ask: How many meters shorter is the diagonal route than the route along the two edges?
steps: Shrink the numbers first: 720 = 60 × 12 and 300 = 60 × 5. Since 12² + 5² = 144 + 25 = 169 = 13², the diagonal is 60 × 13 = 780 meters.

problems.stem: Mei surveyed all 90 students in her grade about pets at home. The results are in the table. The "Has a dog" and "Has a cat" counts include the students who have both a dog and a cat. She handed out the surveys during a 6-minute homeroom.
problems.ask: How many students have both a dog and a cat?
steps: So the extra count is the 'both' group: 36 − 29 = 7.

problems.stem: Amara is laying square pavers for a backyard patio. The patio will be a rectangle 20 feet by 12 feet, and each paver is 24 inches on a side. The pavers fit exactly, with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many pavers does Amara need?
steps: 24 inches is 2 feet. Along the length: 20 ÷ 2 = 10 pavers.

problems.stem: Leah is stocking up at a garden center for her spring planting. The prices, with tax included, are in the table. The garden center is 3 miles from her house. Leah orders one flower pot, two tomato plants, and one watering can.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Leah's order?

problems.stem: Caleb is buying laundry detergent. The store sells the same brand in the three sizes shown in the table. He does about five loads of laundry a week.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per fluid ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Jordan rode his bike 30 miles to a lake, mostly uphill, averaging 10 miles per hour. He rode home the same way, mostly downhill, at 15 miles per hour. He packed two bottles of water for the ride.
problems.ask: What was Jordan's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Lena's board game comes with a cloth bag holding 3 red tokens and 6 yellow tokens. The box says the game is for ages 8 and up. To start the game, she draws two tokens at random without putting the first one back.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both tokens are the same color?

problems.stem: A pair of headphones at the local store is marked $26. Elena decides to buy it, and 7% sales tax is added at checkout.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the pair of headphones, including tax?

problems.stem: On a trip to Mexico, Esme exchanges money at a rate of 20 pesos per U.S. dollar. At an outdoor market, she buys a painted bowl for 570 pesos and a straw hat for 480 pesos. She has four days left on the trip.
problems.ask: How much did Esme spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Nadia wants to buy a couch at a furniture store. The price is $1,006 if she pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $75 down, then 6 monthly payments of $186. The couch is 72 inches long.
problems.ask: How much more would Nadia pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Theo teaches two sections of algebra. On Friday's test, the 14 students in his first-period class averaged 72 points, and the 26 students in his fourth-period class averaged 92 points. The test had 20 questions.
problems.ask: What was the average score for all of the students in both classes together, in points?

problems.stem: Mateo just started a dog-walking business. He moves $3 into savings the first week, and each week after that he moves $2 more than the week before. He has 7 regular customers.
problems.ask: How much will Mateo have set aside in all after 15 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 15, week 2 with week 14, and so on: each pair adds to $3 + $31 = $34.
With 15 weeks, the average week is $34 ÷ 2 = $17, so the total is 15 × $17 = $255.

problems.stem: Yuki is wrapping eight gifts for a holiday party. Each gift needs a piece of ribbon 42 inches long.
problems.ask: How many feet of ribbon does Yuki need in all?
steps: There are 12 inches in a foot: 336 ÷ 12 = 28 feet.

problems.stem: Ingrid is sealing a rectangular concrete patio that is 21 feet long and 19 feet wide. One gallon of sealer covers 50 square feet, and it needs 12 hours to dry. Sealer is sold only by the whole gallon.
problems.ask: How many gallons must Ingrid buy to give the patio one coat?
steps: 7 gallons cover 7 × 50 = 350 square feet, which is not enough.
8 gallons cover 400 square feet, so Ingrid needs 8 gallons.

problems.stem: Wes's swim team held a car wash to raise money. They charged $8 for each car and $14 for each truck or SUV. Over four hours on Saturday, they washed 125 vehicles and collected $1,228.
problems.ask: How many cars did the team wash?
steps: If all 125 were cars, the total would be 125 × $8 = $1,000.
The actual total is $1,228 − $1,000 = $228 more than that.
Each truck or SUV brings in $6 more than each car, so trucks and SUVs: $228 ÷ $6 = 38.

problems.stem: Leah mixed 12 cups of fruit punch that is 25% juice for a party. It tastes too sweet, so she wants to add water until the punch is only 20% juice. Twenty guests are coming.
problems.ask: How many cups of water should Leah add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 20% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 25/20 = 5/4: 12 × 5/4 = 15 cups.

problems.stem: Luis's booth at the town festival has 10 rubber ducks floating in a pool. A player pays $3, picks one duck at random, and wins the prize marked underneath; the duck then goes back in. The table shows the prizes. The festival lasts 6 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the booth make per game after paying out prizes?
steps: If each duck came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $10 + 3 × $3 = $19.
The booth keeps $3 − $1.90 = $1.10 per game on average.

problems.stem: A farm stand sells a 3-pound bag of apples for $3.75. Andre wants 7 pounds for pies, and the stand will weigh out any amount at the same price per pound.
problems.ask: How much will 7 pounds of apples cost?

problems.stem: Ezra works at a bike shop for $14 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times his regular rate. The bike shop has 59 employees. Last week he worked 50 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Ezra earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $14 = $21 an hour, for 50 − 40 = 10 hours.

problems.stem: Marcus buys a monthly bus pass. Last year the pass cost $100, and this year the transit agency raised the price to $115. He rides the bus about 18 days a month.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bus pass increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $15 ÷ $100 = 3/20 = 0.15.
As a percent, that is an increase of 15%.

problems.stem: Mateo wants to start going to a climbing gym and is choosing between the two plans in the table. The gym is open until 10 o'clock on weeknights.
problems.ask: For how many visits would the two plans cost exactly the same?
steps: Member plan costs $90 more up front.
Basic plan costs $6 more per visit, so each visit closes the gap by $6.
Check: $90 + 15 × $7 = $195 and $0 + 15 × $13 = $195, so the answer is 15 visits.

problems.stem: At a burrito stand, customers build a burrito bowl by choosing exactly 2 different fillings from a list of 8. Every burrito bowl also gets one of 2 bases: white rice or brown rice. The stand serves about 250 bowls on a busy day. The order the fillings are chosen in doesn't matter.
problems.ask: How many different burrito bowls can a customer build?
steps: Pick 2 of 8 fillings: 8 × 7 = 56 ordered picks, ÷ 2 because order doesn't matter = 28 sets.
Each set can go with any of the 2 bases: 28 × 2 = 56 burrito bowls.

bonus.stem: Ingrid is stacking soup cans into a flat, triangle-shaped display in a store window. The bottom row has 18 cans, each row has one fewer can than the row below it, and the top row has 3 cans.
bonus.ask: How many cans are in the display?
steps: Rows: from 3 up to 18 cans is 18 − 3 + 1 = 16 rows.
Pair the first and last rows, the second and second-to-last, and so on: each pair holds 3 + 18 = 21.

problems.stem: The store is taking 20% off everything this week, including the board game Grace has had her eye on. Its regular price is $25.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the board game, before tax?

problems.stem: Imani is driving to a state park, which is 280 miles from home, and then driving back. Her car gets 35 miles per gallon, and gas costs $3.80 per gallon. She plans to leave at 7 in the morning.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the round trip?

problems.stem: Sofia built a rectangular backyard pond that is 8 feet long, 5 feet wide and 1.5 feet deep, and she stocked it with nine goldfish. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the pond hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Wes started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 3 miles per hour. Elena started running from the same spot 6 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 5 miles per hour. The path is 6 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Elena catch up to Wes?
steps: Head start: in 6 minutes (1/10 hour), Wes covers 3 × 1/10 = 0.3 miles.
Time to close the gap: 0.3 ÷ 2 = 3/20 hour = 9 minutes.

problems.stem: Kofi buys 20 stamps at the post office: some 60-cent postcard stamps and some 75-cent letter stamps. He spends $12.90 in all. There are 6 people in line behind him.
problems.ask: How many postcard stamps does Kofi buy?
steps: Suppose all 20 were postcard stamps: 20 × 60 cents = 1,200 cents.
The real total is 1,290 cents, which is 1,290 cents − 1,200 cents = 90 cents more.
Each letter stamp adds 15 cents more than a postcard stamp, so there are 90 cents ÷ 15 cents = 6 letter stamps (check: 6 × 15 cents = 90 cents).

problems.stem: After a long hike, Malik stops at a cafe for dinner. His bill is $88.60 before tip. He always tips 15% of the bill.
problems.ask: How much is the tip?

problems.stem: A muffin recipe makes 18 muffins and uses 1/4 cup of sugar. Zoe needs 24 muffins for a school bake sale. The muffins bake at 375 degrees for 20 minutes.
problems.ask: If she scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of sugar will she need?

problems.stem: Ravi deposited $1,200 in a savings account that earns 6% interest, compounded once a year. He won't add or take out any money. The bank requires a $50 minimum balance.
problems.ask: How much will be in the account after 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 6% of $1,200 is $72, so the value goes to $1,200 + $72 = $1,272.

problems.stem: Esme is painting the four walls of her bedroom, which is 16 feet long, 10 feet wide and 9 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. One gallon of paint covers 400 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $28 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Esme need to buy?
steps: 936 ÷ 400 ≈ 2.3, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

problems.stem: Nadia is writing a report about her town. Its population grew by 20% from 2016 to 2020, then shrank by 10% from 2020 to 2024. The town has 12 public parks.
problems.ask: By what percent is the 2024 population higher than the 2016 population?
steps: Start with a population of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
108 is 8 above 100, so it is 8% higher.

problems.stem: Fatima and Diego are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Fatima could paint it in 8 hours, and Diego could paint it in 24 hours. The fence is 80 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Fatima does 1/8 of the fence and Diego does 1/24.
Together: 1/8 + 1/24 = 3/24 + 1/24 = 4/24 = 1/6 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: Nadia is seven times as old as her grandson, Omar. This spring they planted 16 tomato plants together. In 18 years, Nadia will be three times as old as Omar.
problems.ask: How old is Omar now, in years?
steps: Let Omar's age now be x, so Nadia is 7x.
Subtract 3x and 18 from both sides: 4x = 54 − 18 = 36, so x = 9.
So Omar is 9 years old now. Check: in 18 years, 81 = 3 × 27.

problems.stem: Victor is tracking how long he practices piano. From Monday to Friday, he practiced 45, 44, 39, 58, and 59 minutes.
problems.ask: What was his average practice time per day, in minutes?

problems.stem: Diego bikes to work. He rides 10 miles on a bike path at a steady 10 miles per hour, then 4 miles through city streets at a steady 8 miles per hour. His bike has 19 gears.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 10 ÷ 10 = 1 hour, which is 60 minutes.
Second part: 4 ÷ 8 = 1/2 hour, which is 30 minutes.

problems.stem: Arjun took his family out for brunch at a diner that opened 25 years ago. They ordered five pancake plates at $20 each and a pitcher of orange juice for $10. Sales tax is 8%, and they added a 20% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the brunch, including tax and tip?

problems.stem: Grace's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 80 minutes.
problems.ask: What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
steps: With 28 values in order, the median is the average of the 14th and 15th values.
Running totals: through 0: 2, through 1: 5, through 2: 10, through 3: 15, through 4: 23, through 5: 28.
Both fall in the row for 3 goals, so the median is 3 goals.

problems.stem: On level ground, Jamal holds a 3-foot yardstick straight up, and its shadow is 7 feet long. At the same moment, the shadow of a nearby oak tree is 63 feet long. The tree was planted about 54 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the oak tree, in feet?
steps: The sun hits both at the same angle, so height ÷ shadow is the same for the oak tree and the yardstick: 3 ÷ 7.
The oak tree's shadow is 63 ÷ 7 = 9 times as long as the yardstick's.
So the oak tree is 9 × 3 = 27 feet tall.

problems.stem: Felix and four coworkers chip in for a retirement gift: a gift card worth $135 and a cake that costs $31. They split the cost evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Felix plus four others makes 5 people.

problems.stem: Ravi is planning a hike with a trail map where 1 centimeter represents 2 kilometers. The trail to the waterfall measures 3 centimeters on the map, and the trail back to the parking lot measures 6 centimeters. The parking lot has 80 spaces.
problems.ask: How many kilometers long is the whole hike?

problems.stem: Chloe's company asked its employees how they usually get to work. Each person gave one answer, shown in the table. The office parking lot has 40 spaces.
problems.ask: What percent of the employees surveyed chose "Bike"?

problems.stem: Ruth is ordering pizza for eight friends. The pizzeria sells round pizzas in two sizes: a 10-inch small and a 12-inch large, where the size is the diameter. Both have the same crust and toppings.
problems.ask: The large pizza has how many times the area of the small pizza?

problems.stem: In a board game, Theo's piece is stuck in the jail space. Under the house rules, he rolls a standard six-sided die two times, and he escapes if any roll is a 5 or a 6. The board has 36 spaces in all.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Theo escapes?
steps: Work with the opposite: one roll is not a 5 or a 6 with probability 4/6 = 2/3.

problems.stem: Jamal is building a rectangular pen for his chickens that measures 15 feet by 11 feet. One 15-foot side runs along the shed wall, so it needs no fence.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Jamal need?
steps: Fence the other 15-foot side and both 11-foot sides.

problems.stem: Hana is baking a cake for a birthday party, and it must be frosted by 2:00 p.m. when the guests arrive. Baking takes 40 minutes, cooling takes 50 minutes, and frosting takes 20 minutes, one after another. The cake will feed 15 people. It is 11:40 a.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Hana wait before starting?
steps: From 11:40 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. is 140 minutes.

problems.stem: Fatima's world history grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and her average so far. There are 34 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Fatima need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 88?
steps: To finish at 88, the final must add 88 − 58.6 = 29.4 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 29.4 ÷ 0.3 = 98.

problems.stem: Sam takes a 250-milligram dose of a medicine at 7:30 a.m. with a glass of water. The amount of the medicine in the body drops by half every 3 hours.
problems.ask: How many milligrams of the medicine are left in his body 12 hours after the dose?

problems.stem: Andre, Priya and three of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Andre and Priya keep making each other laugh, so they can't stand side by side. The photographer charges $75 for the session.
problems.ask: In how many different orders can the 5 of them line up?
steps: Orders with them together: glue them into a block, 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24, times 2 for their order = 48.

bonus.stem: The staircase up to Ben's apartment has 12 steps. He climbs either one or two steps at a time, mixing them however he likes.
bonus.ask: In how many different ways can Ben climb the 12 steps?
steps: To land on step k, the last move came from k − 1 or k − 2, so ways(k) = ways(k − 1) + ways(k − 2).

problems.stem: Elena shops at the farmers market on Saturday morning. She buys a jar of honey for $7.25, a loaf of sourdough for $5.50, and a pint of blueberries for $4.50. There's no sales tax, and she pays with a $20 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Elena get back?

problems.stem: Noor has her eye on a winter coat with a regular price of $90. This week it's marked 50% off. At checkout, she also uses a coupon for an extra 20% off the sale price. The sale ends in 4 days.
problems.ask: How much does Noor pay for the winter coat, before tax?
steps: 50% of $90 is $45, so the sale price is $90 − $45 = $45.
The extra 20% comes off $45, not the original price: 20% of $45 is $9.

problems.stem: Caleb's club ran a bake sale on Saturday morning. They sold cookies, brownies and muffins in the ratio 2:1:2, and they sold 60 items in all. Every item was priced at $1.50.
problems.ask: How many muffins did the club sell?

problems.stem: Dmitri is building a wooden garden gate shaped like a rectangle, 36 inches wide and 48 inches tall. To keep it from sagging, he will nail a straight brace from one corner to the opposite corner. The gate will hang on two hinges.
problems.ask: How long must the brace be, in inches?
steps: The brace is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs equal to the width and height.

problems.stem: A café asked 40 regular customers which drinks they had ordered in the past month. The results are in the table. The "Iced coffee" and "Hot tea" counts include the customers who ordered both drinks. The café has 13 tables.
problems.ask: How many customers ordered both drinks?
steps: So the extra count is the 'both' group: 25 − 21 = 4.

bonus.stem: Nico is blindfolded for a party game and reaches into a box of 9 red, 8 blue and 10 green colored pencils, which all feel the same.
bonus.ask: What is the fewest pencils Nico must pull out to be sure of getting two blue pencils?
steps: Worst case: he pulls every non-blue one first: 9 + 10 = 19.
Even the next one only gives him a single blue one.
One more must be blue, making two: 19 + 2 = 21 pencils.

problems.stem: Raul is reading a 330-page novel for his book club and has already read 180 pages. He plans to read 25 pages each day until he finishes.
problems.ask: How many more days will it take to finish the book?

problems.stem: Arjun is picking up donuts for the class's noon study session. The donut shop sells donuts in packs of 6 for $4.50, or one at a time for $0.85 each. 22 students signed up, and Arjun wants at least one donut per person. Leftovers are fine, but he can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Arjun can spend?
steps: 22 ÷ 6 = 3 full packs, with 4 people left over.

problems.stem: Malik helped run a pancake breakfast at the fire station. Adult plates cost $9 and kids' plates cost $6. They served 71 plates and took in $525, with nine volunteers working the griddles.
problems.ask: How many adult plates did they serve?
steps: If all 71 were kids' plates, the total would be 71 × $6 = $426.
The actual total is $525 − $426 = $99 more than that.
Each adult plate brings in $3 more than each kids' plate, so adult plates: $99 ÷ $3 = 33.

problems.stem: Diego teaches two sections of algebra. On Friday's test, the 20 students in his first-period class averaged 63 points, and the 10 students in his fourth-period class averaged 78 points. The test had 30 questions.
problems.ask: What was the average score for all of the students in both classes together, in points?

problems.stem: Kofi snaps a photo of the clock tower in the town square at exactly 9:14. The tower is 87 feet tall. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 14 × 6 = 84 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 9 × 30 + 14 × 0.5 = 277 degrees past the 12.
That's more than 180, so the smaller angle is 360 − 193 = 167 degrees.

problems.stem: Rosa is tiling her kitchen floor, a rectangle 11 feet long and 10 feet wide. She is using square tiles that measure 12 inches on each side, and they fit exactly with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many tiles does Rosa need?
steps: 12 inches is 1 foot, so each tile covers 1 square foot.

problems.stem: Andre is stocking up at a garden center for his spring planting. The prices, with tax included, are in the table. The garden center is 3 miles from his house. Andre orders four bags of potting soil, three flower pots, and three tomato plants.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Andre's order?

problems.stem: Carmen bought a set of wireless headphones at an electronics store during a 40%-off sale, and she also used a $10 coupon. The register took 40% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. The headphones run about 20 hours on a full charge. Before tax, Carmen paid $89.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the headphones?
steps: $99 is what was left after 40% off, so it is 60% of the original price.

problems.stem: Esme has 8 ounces of a cleaning spray that is 20% vinegar. For washing windows, she wants a weaker spray that is only 8% vinegar, so she'll add water. She has thirteen windows to clean.
problems.ask: How many ounces of water should Esme add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 8% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 20/8 = 5/2: 8 × 5/2 = 20 ounces.

problems.stem: Luis and Mei live 16 miles apart along a straight bike trail, and they ride toward each other to meet for lunch. Luis rides at 10 miles per hour, and Mei rides at 14 miles per hour. They leave at the same time. The trail has 20 benches along the way.
problems.ask: How many minutes after they leave do they meet?
steps: The gap closes at 10 + 14 = 24 miles per hour.

problems.stem: A bike helmet at the local store is marked $25. Fatima decides to buy it, and 5% sales tax is added at checkout.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the bike helmet, including tax?
steps: 10% of $25 is $2.50, so 5% is half of that: $1.25.

problems.stem: On a trip to Mexico, Ingrid exchanges money at a rate of 20 pesos per U.S. dollar. At an outdoor market, she buys a painted bowl for 560 pesos and a straw hat for 120 pesos. She has four days left on the trip.
problems.ask: How much did Ingrid spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Luis wants to buy an electric bike at a bike shop. The price is $959 if he pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $50 down, then 6 monthly payments of $174. Its battery can go about 40 miles on one charge.
problems.ask: How much more would Luis pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Elena deposited $6,000 in a savings account that earns 4% interest, compounded once a year. She won't add or take out any money. The bank requires a $25 minimum balance.
problems.ask: How much will be in the account after 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 4% of $6,000 is $240, so the value goes to $6,000 + $240 = $6,240.

problems.stem: Nadia drove 180 miles to visit her aunt and averaged 60 miles per hour on the way there. Coming home on the same roads, heavy traffic held her to an average of 30 miles per hour. Her car gets about 25 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: What was Nadia's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 360 ÷ 9 = 40 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Hana needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. She plans to pick up the car at 9:15 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $10 more up front.
Company B costs $0.05 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.05.

problems.stem: Silas's board game comes with a cloth bag holding 8 red tokens and 3 yellow tokens. The box says the game is for ages 10 and up. To start the game, he draws two tokens at random without putting the first one back.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both tokens are the same color?

problems.stem: At 9:40 a.m., Malik put a loaf of bread in the oven. He took it out at 10:35 a.m., when the crust was golden brown.
problems.ask: For how many minutes did the bread bake?
steps: From 9:40 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 20 minutes.
From 10:00 a.m. to 10:35 a.m. is 35 minutes.

problems.stem: Tariq is putting laminate flooring in a rectangular bedroom that measures 12 feet by 9 feet. Each box of flooring covers 20 square feet and weighs 37 pounds. The store sells only whole boxes.
problems.ask: Ignoring waste, how many boxes does Tariq need to buy?
steps: 5 boxes cover 5 × 20 = 100 square feet, which is not enough.
6 boxes cover 120 square feet, so Tariq needs 6 boxes.

problems.stem: Tess is buying laundry detergent. The store sells the same brand in the three sizes shown in the table. She does about three loads of laundry a week.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per fluid ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Hana started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 3 miles per hour. Andre started running from the same spot 10 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 5 miles per hour. The path is 8 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Andre catch up to Hana?
steps: Head start: in 10 minutes (1/6 hour), Hana covers 3 × 1/6 = 0.5 miles.
Time to close the gap: 0.5 ÷ 2 = 1/4 hour = 15 minutes.

problems.stem: Imani runs a prize wheel at the school fair. The wheel has 20 equal sections, each equally likely to land on top, and a spin costs $3. The table shows what the sections pay. The fair runs for 8 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the prize wheel make per spin after paying out prizes?
steps: If each section came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $20 + 4 × $3 = $32.
The booth keeps $3 − $1.60 = $1.40 per spin on average.

bonus.stem: A frog at the bottom of a 35-foot ditch hops 7 feet up the muddy bank every day, then slips back 3 feet every night.
bonus.ask: On which day does the frog first reach the top of the bank, if the first day of climbing is day 1?
steps: Each full day and night, the frog gains 7 − 3 = 4 feet.
On its last day it climbs 7 feet and never slides back, so it only needs to start that day at 35 − 7 = 28 feet.
Reaching 28 feet takes 28 ÷ 4 = 7 full days and nights.
It reaches the top on day 7 + 1 = 8.

problems.stem: At the hardware store, 6 feet of rope costs $2.10. Leah needs 11 feet to hang a porch swing, and the store cuts rope to any length at the same price per foot.
problems.ask: How much will 11 feet of rope cost?

problems.stem: Rosa has taken three history tests this term and scored 97, 93, and 94. There are 33 students in the class, and one test is left. She wants her average on all four tests to be exactly 90.
problems.ask: What score does Rosa need on the last test?
steps: An average of 90 over 4 tests means a total of 90 × 4 = 360.

problems.stem: Diego's home internet bill used to be $50 a month. After he upgraded his plan, the monthly bill became $70. The new plan has a download speed of 300 megabits per second.
problems.ask: By what percent did Diego's monthly internet bill increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $20 ÷ $50 = 2/5 = 0.4.
As a percent, that is an increase of 40%.

problems.stem: Lena asked every household on her street how many pets it has and recorded the results in the table. It took her three afternoons to reach everyone.
problems.ask: What is the median number of pets per household?
steps: With 18 values in order, the median is the average of the 9th and 10th values.
Running totals: through 0: 9, through 1: 14, through 2: 15, through 3: 17, through 4: 18.
They are 0 and 1, so the median is (0 + 1) ÷ 2 = 0.5 pets.

problems.stem: Omar is saving for a new bike. He puts $8 in a jar the first week, and every week after that he puts in $2 more than the week before. He started the plan on his 12th birthday.
problems.ask: How much will Omar have saved in all after 8 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 8, week 2 with week 7, and so on: each pair adds to $8 + $22 = $30.

problems.stem: Zoe is running a lemonade stand. She makes eight pitchers of lemonade, and each pitcher holds 10 cups. There are 4 cups in a quart.
problems.ask: How many quarts of lemonade does Zoe make?
steps: There are 4 cups in a quart: 80 ÷ 4 = 20 quarts.

problems.stem: Hugo works at a restaurant for $16 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times his regular rate. The restaurant has 42 employees. Last week he worked 50 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Hugo earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $16 = $24 an hour, for 50 − 40 = 10 hours.

problems.stem: Nadia is painting the four walls of her living room, which is 15 feet long, 9 feet wide and 10 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. The door and windows take up 50 square feet that won't be painted. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $39 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Nadia need to buy?
steps: Minus the door and windows: 480 − 50 = 430 square feet.
860 ÷ 350 ≈ 2.5, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

problems.stem: In March, the hardware store where Ben works cut the price of a cordless drill by 30%. In June, the store raised that new price by 30%. Ben has worked at the store for 6 months.
problems.ask: By what percent is the June price lower than the original price?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
91 is 9 below 100, so it is 9% lower.

problems.stem: At a pizza shop, customers build a pizza by choosing exactly 3 different toppings from a list of 7. Every pizza also gets one of 2 crusts: thin or regular. A large pizza is cut into 8 slices. The order the toppings are chosen in doesn't matter.
problems.ask: How many different pizzas can a customer build?
steps: Pick 3 of 7 toppings: 7 × 6 × 5 = 210 ordered picks, ÷ 6 (the 3 × 2 × 1 orders of the same three) = 35 sets.
Each set can go with any of the 2 crusts: 35 × 2 = 70 pizzas.

bonus.stem: Theo is sewing a quilt that is a 5-by-5 grid of square patches. Looking at the grid lines, Theo wonders how many squares can be traced, counting every size, from single patches up to the biggest square that fits.
bonus.ask: How many squares of all sizes are in the 5-by-5 grid?
steps: A k-by-k square can start in 5 − k + 1 spots across and the same number down, so there are (5 − k + 1)² of them.

problems.stem: The store is taking 25% off everything this week, including the pair of hiking boots Ruth has had her eye on. Its regular price is $74.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the pair of hiking boots, before tax?

problems.stem: Esme's pancake recipe makes 16 pancakes and calls for 3/4 cup of flour. She is making 32 pancakes for a family brunch. The recipe says to cook each pancake for 2 minutes per side.
problems.ask: If she scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of flour will she need?

problems.stem: Elena bought a rectangular glass aquarium that is 24 inches long, 18 inches wide and 12 inches tall. She plans to keep ten small fish in it. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the aquarium hold when completely full?
steps: Convert to feet (÷ 12): 24 in = 2 ft, 18 in = 1.5 ft, 12 in = 1 ft.

problems.stem: Aiyana and Omar are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Aiyana could paint it in 12 hours, and Omar could paint it in 24 hours. The fence is 200 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Aiyana does 1/12 of the fence and Omar does 1/24.
Together: 1/12 + 1/24 = 2/24 + 1/24 = 3/24 = 1/8 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: The drama club at Raul's school sold 124 tickets for its Saturday show. Adult tickets cost $12 and student tickets cost $7. Ticket sales came to $1,288 in all, and the auditorium has 250 seats.
problems.ask: How many adult tickets were sold?
steps: The real total is $1,288, which is $1,288 − $868 = $420 more.
Each adult ticket adds $5 more than a student ticket, so there are $420 ÷ $5 = 84 adult tickets.

bonus.stem: Sam buys a notebook and a pen at the campus bookstore for $4.50 in total. The notebook costs exactly $2 more than the pen.
bonus.ask: How much does the notebook cost?
steps: Call the price of the pen x, so the notebook costs x + $2.

problems.stem: Theo is tracking how long he practices piano. From Monday to Friday, he practiced 25, 43, 38, 43, and 36 minutes.
problems.ask: What was his average practice time per day, in minutes?

problems.stem: Nico bikes to work. He rides 9 miles on a bike path at a steady 12 miles per hour, then 2 miles through city streets at a steady 6 miles per hour. The bike path has 19 benches along the way.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 9 ÷ 12 = 3/4 hour, which is 45 minutes.
Second part: 2 ÷ 6 = 1/3 hour, which is 20 minutes.

problems.stem: Zoe took her family out for brunch at a diner that opened 12 years ago. They ordered three pancake plates at $22 each and a pitcher of orange juice for $14. Sales tax is 10%, and they added a 15% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the brunch, including tax and tip?
steps: Tip: 10% of $80 is $8, plus half of that, $4, gives $12.

problems.stem: Andre is studying an 800-gram sample of a radioactive substance in a lab. The substance has a half-life of 12 days, which means half of whatever is left decays every 12 days. The sample is stored in a case that weighs 20 pounds.
problems.ask: How many days will it take until only 200 grams of the substance remain?
steps: Halve until 200 grams remain: 800 → 400 → 200. That is 2 halvings.

problems.stem: Chloe, who is 5 feet tall, stands on level ground in the shadow of an oak tree, 25 feet from its base. Her own shadow is 10 feet long and points the same way, and its tip lands exactly on the tip of the oak tree's shadow. The tree was planted about 36 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the oak tree, in feet?
steps: The oak tree's shadow runs past Chloe to the same tip: 25 + 10 = 35 feet long.
Same sun angle, so height ÷ shadow matches: 5 ÷ 10 for Chloe.
Height of the oak tree = 35 × 5 ÷ 10 = 175 ÷ 10 = 17.5 feet.

problems.stem: Andre and two coworkers stop at a diner for breakfast, and Andre offers to pay. The check is $57.80. He plans to add a 15% tip on the full check.
problems.ask: How much does Andre pay in all, including the tip?

problems.stem: Chloe is planning a hike with a trail map where 1 centimeter represents 5 kilometers. The trail to the waterfall measures 3 centimeters on the map, and the trail back to the parking lot measures 3.5 centimeters. The parking lot has 60 spaces.
problems.ask: How many kilometers long is the whole hike?

problems.stem: Tariq works at the town library and asked visitors their main reason for coming in. Each visitor gave one answer, shown in the table. The library is open 56 hours a week.
problems.ask: What percent of the visitors surveyed chose either "Use computers" or "Study"?

problems.stem: Mei's living room has a round rug that is 6 feet across. She wants to replace it with a round rug that is 9 feet across. The room is 16 feet long.
problems.ask: The new rug will cover how many times as much floor area as the old rug?
steps: A circle's area is π × radius², so area grows with the square of the diameter.

problems.stem: In a board game, Isaac's piece is stuck in the jail space. Under the house rules, he rolls a standard six-sided die two times, and he escapes if any roll is a 5 or a 6. The board has 36 spaces in all.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Isaac escapes?
steps: Work with the opposite: one roll is not a 5 or a 6 with probability 4/6 = 2/3.

problems.stem: Jamal and four friends rent a lake cabin for a weekend. The rental costs $600, plus a $90 cleaning fee. They split the whole cost evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Jamal plus four others makes 5 people.

problems.stem: A store is taking 20% off every stand mixer, and Ravi finds one with a regular price of $265. He also has a member coupon that takes 10% off the already reduced price. The sale ends in 12 days.
problems.ask: How much does Ravi pay for the stand mixer, before tax?
steps: 20% of $265 is $53, so the sale price is $265 − $53 = $212.
The extra 10% comes off $212, not the original price: 10% of $212 is $21.20.

problems.stem: Dmitri's club ran a bake sale on Saturday morning. They sold cookies, brownies and muffins in the ratio 6:1:1, and they sold 32 items in all. Every item was priced at $2.
problems.ask: How many cookies did the club sell?

problems.stem: Ruth's statistics grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and her average so far. There are 20 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Ruth need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 85?
steps: To finish at 85, the final must add 85 − 61.9 = 23.1 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 23.1 ÷ 0.3 = 77.

problems.stem: Grace leans a 25-foot ladder against the side of her house to clean the gutters. For safety, the bottom of the ladder sits 7 feet out from the wall, on level ground. The ladder is rated to hold 250 pounds.
problems.ask: How high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach, in feet?
steps: The wall, the ground and the ladder form a right triangle, with the ladder as the hypotenuse.

problems.stem: Esme needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. She plans to pick up the car at 7:30 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $16 more up front.
Company B costs $0.10 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.10.

problems.stem: Six friends, including Kenji, Amara and Aiyana, have 6 seats together in one row at the movies. Kenji, Amara and Aiyana want three seats in a row together. The movie runs 95 minutes.
problems.ask: In how many different ways can the 6 friends fill the 6 seats?
steps: Glue the three into one block, leaving 4 units: 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24 orders.
Inside the block the three can be ordered 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 ways.

problems.stem: Ruth is building a rectangular dog run in her backyard. It will be 17 feet long and 10 feet wide. One 17-foot side runs along the barn wall, so it needs no fence.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Ruth need?
steps: Fence the other 17-foot side and both 10-foot sides.

problems.stem: Omar is driving to a state park, which is 50 miles from home, and then driving back. His car gets 25 miles per gallon, and gas costs $3.90 per gallon. His car's tank holds 14 gallons.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the round trip?

problems.stem: Caleb helped run a pancake breakfast at the fire station. Adult plates cost $8 and kids' plates cost $6. They served 131 plates and took in $872, with nine volunteers working the griddles.
problems.ask: How many adult plates did they serve?
steps: If all 131 were kids' plates, the total would be 131 × $6 = $786.
The actual total is $872 − $786 = $86 more than that.
Each adult plate brings in $2 more than each kids' plate, so adult plates: $86 ÷ $2 = 43.

problems.stem: Silas mixed 6 liters of liquid plant food that is 20% concentrate. The label says seedlings need a mix that is only 15% concentrate, so he will dilute it with water. He is growing three trays of seedlings.
problems.ask: How many liters of water should Silas add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 15% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 20/15 = 4/3: 6 × 4/3 = 8 liters.

problems.stem: A community center asked 48 members which summer trips they would sign up for. The results are in the table. The "Hiking trip" and "Kayaking trip" counts include the members who signed up for both trips. The sign-up sheet was posted for 13 days.
problems.ask: How many of the 48 members signed up for neither trip?

bonus.stem: The bell in the town hall tower rings once for each hour, with the rings evenly spaced. Ezra times it at 6 o'clock: 15 seconds pass from the first ring to the last.
bonus.ask: How many seconds does it take from the first ring to the last at 12 o'clock?
steps: 6 rings have only 5 gaps between them, so each gap is 15 ÷ 5 = 3 seconds.

problems.stem: Mei runs to the pet store for her dog. She buys a bag of treats for $4.99, a chew toy for $4.25, and a new leash for $12. There's no sales tax, and she pays with a $50 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Mei get back?

problems.stem: Theo must be at work by 8:45 a.m. for a meeting. He walks 10 minutes to the train station, rides the train for 45 minutes, and then walks 10 minutes to the office. A train ticket costs $2.25, and a train leaves the moment he reaches the platform. It is 7:20 a.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Theo wait before leaving home?
steps: From 7:20 a.m. to 8:45 a.m. is 85 minutes.

problems.stem: Lucia's grandmother gave her $2,500 for her 17th birthday. She put all of it in a certificate of deposit that pays 5% interest, compounded once a year, and left it alone.
problems.ask: How much interest will the money earn over the 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 5% of $2,500 is $125, so the value goes to $2,500 + $125 = $2,625.

problems.stem: Nadia drove 180 miles to visit her aunt and averaged 60 miles per hour on the way there. Coming home on the same roads, heavy traffic held her to an average of 30 miles per hour. Her car gets about 35 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: What was Nadia's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 360 ÷ 9 = 40 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Aiyana is eight times as old as her grandson, Malik. This spring they planted 23 tomato plants together. In 4 years, Aiyana will be six times as old as Malik.
problems.ask: How old is Malik now, in years?
steps: Let Malik's age now be x, so Aiyana is 8x.
Subtract 6x and 4 from both sides: 2x = 24 − 4 = 20, so x = 10.
So Malik is 10 years old now. Check: in 4 years, 84 = 6 × 14.

bonus.stem: There are 16 people at Silas's birthday party, counting Silas. Before the cake comes out, everyone shakes hands with everyone else exactly once.
bonus.ask: How many handshakes are there in all?
steps: Each of the 16 people takes part in 15 handshakes: 16 × 15 = 240.
That counts every one twice (once for each person in it), so divide by 2: 240 ÷ 2 = 120.

problems.stem: Dev is tiling his kitchen floor, a rectangle 18 feet long and 16 feet wide. He is using square tiles that measure 24 inches on each side, and they fit exactly with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many tiles does Dev need?
steps: 24 inches is 2 feet. Along the length: 18 ÷ 2 = 9 tiles.

problems.stem: Ravi is picking up donuts for the class's 7:45 a.m. study session. The donut shop sells donuts in packs of 4 for $4.25, or one at a time for $1.25 each. Nine students signed up, and Ravi wants at least one donut per person. Leftovers are fine, but he can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Ravi can spend?
steps: 9 ÷ 4 = 2 full packs, with 1 person left over.

problems.stem: The water trough at Andre's farm is a rectangular metal tank 6 feet long, 2 feet wide and 2 feet deep. It serves the six horses in the north pasture. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the trough hold when completely full?

problems.stem: At the warehouse where Eli works, the 8 workers on the day shift packed an average of 87 boxes each on Monday. The 12 workers on the night shift, which started at 10 p.m., packed an average of 57 boxes each.
problems.ask: What was the average number of boxes packed per worker across both shifts?

problems.stem: Maya keeps a tin of cookies on her desk. It holds 8 chocolate chip cookies and 4 oatmeal cookies, all the same size. The tin was a gift from her neighbor 2 years ago. Without looking, she takes out two cookies, one after the other, and doesn't put either back.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both cookies are the same kind?

problems.stem: Ben is working on a 750-piece jigsaw puzzle. He has placed 600 pieces so far and places 50 more pieces each night.
problems.ask: How many more nights will it take to finish the puzzle?

problems.stem: Omar is traveling in Italy, where prices are in euros. That week, 1 euro costs $1.10 in U.S. money. He buys a leather wallet for 18 euros and a scarf for 37 euros. His hotel is 6 blocks from the shop.
problems.ask: How much did Omar spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Ingrid bought a pair of running shoes at a sporting-goods store during a 25%-off sale, and she also used a $20 coupon. The register took 25% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. Only two pairs in her size were left on the shelf. Before tax, Ingrid paid $40.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the shoes?
steps: $60 is what was left after 25% off, so it is 75% of the original price.

problems.stem: Tess asked every household on her street how many pets it has and recorded the results in the table. It took her two afternoons to reach everyone.
problems.ask: What is the median number of pets per household?
steps: With 23 values in order, the median is the 12th value.
Running totals: through 0: 7, through 1: 12, through 2: 13, through 3: 22, through 4: 23.
The 12th value falls in the row for 1 pet, so the median is 1 pets.

problems.stem: Owen glances at the clock above the classroom door during a math quiz. It reads 11:59, and the quiz started 15 minutes earlier. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 59 × 6 = 354 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 11 × 30 + 59 × 0.5 = 359.5 degrees past the 12.
That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 5.5 degrees.

problems.stem: A pair of headphones at the local store is marked $72. Theo decides to buy it, and 7% sales tax is added at checkout.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the pair of headphones, including tax?

problems.stem: Omar is sealing a rectangular concrete patio that is 15 feet long and 11 feet wide. One gallon of sealer covers 50 square feet, and it needs 48 hours to dry. Sealer is sold only by the whole gallon.
problems.ask: How many gallons must Omar buy to give the patio one coat?
steps: 3 gallons cover 3 × 50 = 150 square feet, which is not enough.
4 gallons cover 200 square feet, so Omar needs 4 gallons.

problems.stem: Mei wants to buy a couch at a furniture store. The price is $885 if she pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $50 down, then 10 monthly payments of $97. The couch is 84 inches long.
problems.ask: How much more would Mei pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Noor set out on her bike along the river trail, riding at a steady 12 miles per hour. Wes left from the same spot 20 minutes later and followed the same trail at a steady 14 miles per hour. The trail is 30 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting did Wes catch up to Noor?
steps: Head start: in 20 minutes (1/3 hour), Noor covers 12 × 1/3 = 4 miles.
Time to close the gap: 4 ÷ 2 = 2 hours = 120 minutes.

problems.stem: Ingrid is saving for a new bike. She puts $14 in a jar the first week, and every week after that she puts in $5 more than the week before. She started the plan on her 12th birthday.
problems.ask: How much will Ingrid have saved in all after 11 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 11, week 2 with week 10, and so on: each pair adds to $14 + $64 = $78.
With 11 weeks, the average week is $78 ÷ 2 = $39, so the total is 11 × $39 = $429.

problems.stem: At 1:30 p.m., Omar started a volunteer shift at the library. The shift ended at 3:40 p.m., and he walked home.
problems.ask: How many minutes long was the shift?
steps: From 1:30 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. is 30 minutes.
From 2:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 1 hour, or 60 minutes.
From 3:00 p.m. to 3:40 p.m. is 40 minutes.

problems.stem: Kofi has taken four Spanish tests this term and scored 76, 87, 74, and 89. There are 24 students in the class, and one test is left. He wants his average on all five tests to be exactly 85.
problems.ask: What score does Kofi need on the last test?
steps: An average of 85 over 5 tests means a total of 85 × 5 = 425.

problems.stem: Mei cooks with olive oil almost every night. Her grocery store sells it in the three bottle sizes shown in the table, and she usually shops on Saturdays.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per fluid ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Hana and Jordan are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Hana could paint it in 6 hours, and Jordan could paint it in 9 hours. The fence is 150 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Hana does 1/6 of the fence and Jordan does 1/9.
Together: 1/6 + 1/9 = 3/18 + 2/18 = 5/18 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: Elena is organizing a kickball league with 10 teams this season. Every team will play every other team exactly twice during the regular season. Each game takes about 30 minutes.
problems.ask: How many games will be played in the regular season?
steps: Each game is a pair of teams. Each of the 10 teams pairs with 9 others: 10 × 9 = 90.
That counts every pair twice, so divide by 2: 90 ÷ 2 = 45 pairs.

problems.stem: A farm stand sells a 3-pound bag of apples for $6.75. Nadia wants 9 pounds for pies, and the stand will weigh out any amount at the same price per pound.
problems.ask: How much will 9 pounds of apples cost?

problems.stem: Theo is buying snacks for his family at a baseball game. The snack bar's prices, tax included, are in the table. Their seats are in row 14. Theo orders three hot dogs, two bottles of water, and one pretzel.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Theo's order?

problems.stem: Last month, a bag of coffee beans at Chloe's grocery store cost $15. This month the same bag costs $13.50. Chloe goes through about one bag every 9 days.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bag decrease?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $1.50 ÷ $15 = 1/10 = 0.1.
As a percent, that is a decrease of 10%.

problems.stem: June is painting the four walls of her dining room, which is 14 feet long, 13 feet wide and 8 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. The door and windows take up 40 square feet that won't be painted. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $36 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does June need to buy?
steps: Minus the door and windows: 432 − 40 = 392 square feet.
784 ÷ 350 ≈ 2.2, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

problems.stem: Jordan takes a 600-milligram dose of a medicine at 6:45 p.m. with a glass of water. The amount of the medicine in the body drops by half every 4 hours.
problems.ask: How many milligrams of the medicine are left in his body 20 hours after the dose?

problems.stem: Grace needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. She plans to pick up the car at 8 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $16 more up front.
Company B costs $0.10 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.10.

problems.stem: Ezra's booth at the town festival has 10 rubber ducks floating in a pool. A player pays $3, picks one duck at random, and wins the prize marked underneath; the duck then goes back in. The table shows the prizes. The festival lasts 6 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the booth make per game after paying out prizes?
steps: If each duck came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $20 + 4 × $1 = $24.
The booth keeps $3 − $2.40 = $0.60 per game on average.

problems.stem: The store is taking 30% off everything this week, including the desk lamp Lucia has had her eye on. Its regular price is $20.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the desk lamp, before tax?

problems.stem: June's pancake recipe makes 12 pancakes and calls for 1/4 cup of flour. She is making 16 pancakes for a family brunch. The recipe says to cook each pancake for 2 minutes per side.
problems.ask: If she scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of flour will she need?

problems.stem: Dev and one friends went out for dinner and waited 15 minutes for a table. They ordered two entrées at $12 each and one appetizer to share for $9. Sales tax is 5%, and they added a 20% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the dinner, including tax and tip?

problems.stem: Isaac's living room has a round rug that is 6 feet across. He wants to replace it with a round rug that is 8 feet across. The room is 16 feet long.
problems.ask: The new rug will cover how many times as much floor area as the old rug?

problems.stem: Maya buys 17 stamps at the post office: some 60-cent postcard stamps and some 75-cent letter stamps. She spends $11.70 in all. There are 8 people in line behind her.
problems.ask: How many letter stamps does Maya buy?
steps: Suppose all 17 were postcard stamps: 17 × 60 cents = 1,020 cents.
The real total is 1,170 cents, which is 1,170 cents − 1,020 cents = 150 cents more.
Each letter stamp adds 15 cents more than a postcard stamp, so there are 150 cents ÷ 15 cents = 10 letter stamps (check: 10 × 15 cents = 150 cents).

problems.stem: Tess is wrapping five gifts for a holiday party. Each gift needs a piece of ribbon 36 inches long.
problems.ask: How many feet of ribbon does Tess need in all?
steps: There are 12 inches in a foot: 180 ÷ 12 = 15 feet.

problems.stem: Ezra works at a restaurant for $14 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times his regular rate. His commute is 7 miles each way. Last week he worked 45 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Ezra earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $14 = $21 an hour, for 45 − 40 = 5 hours.

problems.stem: Amara's company asked its employees how they usually get to work. Each person gave one answer, shown in the table. The office parking lot has 40 spaces.
problems.ask: What percent of the employees surveyed chose "Bike"?

problems.stem: In March, the hardware store where Nadia works cut the price of a patio umbrella by 10%. In June, the store raised that new price by 10%. Nadia has worked at the store for 6 months.
problems.ask: By what percent is the June price lower than the original price?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
99 is 1 below 100, so it is 1% lower.

problems.stem: Imani, who is 5 feet tall, stands on level ground in the shadow of an oak tree, 21 feet from its base. Her own shadow is 10 feet long and points the same way, and its tip lands exactly on the tip of the oak tree's shadow. The tree was planted about 46 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the oak tree, in feet?
steps: The oak tree's shadow runs past Imani to the same tip: 21 + 10 = 31 feet long.
Same sun angle, so height ÷ shadow matches: 5 ÷ 10 for Imani.
Height of the oak tree = 31 × 5 ÷ 10 = 155 ÷ 10 = 15.5 feet.

problems.stem: Omar bowled four games at his league night on Saturday. His scores were 184, 188, 160, and 152.
problems.ask: What was Omar's average score for the four games?

problems.stem: Eli is mapping out a bike ride. On the town's trail map, 1 inch stands for 4 miles. The ride follows the river trail for 2 inches on the map, then the park loop for 3/4 inch. The trail map shows 7 drinking fountains.
problems.ask: How many miles long is the ride?

problems.stem: Dmitri's club ran a bake sale on Saturday morning. They sold cookies, brownies and muffins in the ratio 3:1:5, and they sold 135 items in all. Every item was priced at $2.50.
problems.ask: How many cookies did the club sell?

problems.stem: A rectangular park near Nico's apartment is 320 meters long and 240 meters wide. Nico usually walks along two edges to get from one corner to the opposite corner. Today he cuts straight across the grass on the diagonal instead. The park has 14 benches.
problems.ask: How many meters shorter is the diagonal route than the route along the two edges?
steps: Shrink the numbers first: 320 = 80 × 4 and 240 = 80 × 3. Since 4² + 3² = 16 + 9 = 25 = 5², the diagonal is 80 × 5 = 400 meters.

problems.stem: Owen and Theo live 27.5 miles apart along a straight bike trail, and they ride toward each other to meet for lunch. Owen rides at 13 miles per hour, and Theo rides at 8 miles per hour. Theo leaves 30 minutes after Owen. The trail has 17 benches along the way.
problems.ask: How many minutes after Owen leaves do they meet?
steps: Head start: in 30 minutes, Owen covers 13 × 1/2 = 6.5 miles.
Distance left when Theo leaves: 27.5 − 6.5 = 21 miles.
Together they close 13 + 8 = 21 miles per hour: 21 ÷ 21 = 1 hour = 60 minutes after Theo leaves.
Counting from when Owen leaves: 30 + 60 = 90 minutes.

problems.stem: Aiyana and two coworkers stop at a diner for breakfast, and Aiyana offers to pay. The check is $34. She plans to add a 15% tip on the full check.
problems.ask: How much is the tip?

problems.stem: Kenji bikes to work. He rides 4 miles on a bike path at a steady 12 miles per hour, then 4 miles through city streets at a steady 10 miles per hour. His office is on the fourth floor.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 4 ÷ 12 = 1/3 hour, which is 20 minutes.
Second part: 4 ÷ 10 = 2/5 hour, which is 24 minutes.

problems.stem: Leah's economics grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and her average so far. There are 29 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Leah need on the final exam to finish with exactly a 90?
steps: To finish at 90, the final must add 90 − 65.4 = 24.6 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 24.6 ÷ 0.3 = 82.

problems.stem: Noor mixed 16 cups of fruit punch that is 15% juice for a party. It tastes too sweet, so she wants to add water until the punch is only 12% juice. Eighteen guests are coming.
problems.ask: How many cups of water should Noor add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 12% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 15/12 = 5/4: 16 × 5/4 = 20 cups.

problems.stem: In a board game, Tariq's piece is stuck in the jail space. Under the house rules, he rolls a standard six-sided die three times, and he escapes if any roll is a 6. The board has 30 spaces in all.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Tariq escapes?
steps: Work with the opposite: one roll is not a 6 with probability 5/6.

problems.stem: Tariq and four friends go bowling. The lanes cost $52 for the night, and shoe rentals add $16.50. They split the total evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Tariq plus four others makes 5 people.

problems.stem: Mateo is baking a cake for a birthday party, and it must be frosted by 3:15 p.m. when the guests arrive. Baking takes 35 minutes, cooling takes 50 minutes, and frosting takes 15 minutes, one after another. The cake will feed 15 people. It is 1:05 p.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Mateo wait before starting?
steps: From 1:05 p.m. to 3:15 p.m. is 130 minutes.

problems.stem: Luis ran the ticket table for the drama club's spring play and sold 228 tickets in all. Adult tickets cost $6 and student tickets cost $4. The auditorium has 300 seats, and at the end of the night the cash box held $1,040 from ticket sales.
problems.ask: How many student tickets did Luis sell?
steps: If all 228 were student tickets, the total would be 228 × $4 = $912.
The actual total is $1,040 − $912 = $128 more than that.
Each adult ticket brings in $2 more than each student ticket, so adult tickets: $128 ÷ $2 = 64.

problems.stem: Carmen paddled a kayak 9 miles upstream at 2 miles per hour, then turned around and paddled the same 9 miles back downstream at 6 miles per hour. Her kayak is 14 feet long.
problems.ask: What was Carmen's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 18 ÷ 6 = 3 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: A community center asked 120 members which summer trips they would sign up for. The results are in the table. The "Hiking trip" and "Kayaking trip" counts include the members who signed up for both trips. The sign-up sheet was posted for 15 days.
problems.ask: How many of the 120 members signed up for neither trip?

problems.stem: Theo is building a rectangular dog run in his backyard. It will be 11 feet long and 6 feet wide. He'll fence all four sides.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Theo need?
steps: One length plus one width: 11 + 6 = 17 feet.
Going all the way around doubles that: 2 × 17 = 34 feet.

problems.stem: A store is taking 20% off every camping tent, and Lena finds one with a regular price of $155. She also has a member coupon that takes 20% off the already reduced price. The store is 3 miles from her home.
problems.ask: How much does Lena pay for the camping tent, before tax?
steps: 20% of $155 is $31, so the sale price is $155 − $31 = $124.
The extra 20% comes off $124, not the original price: 20% of $124 is $24.80.

problems.stem: Jamal deposited $2,500 in a savings account that earns 2% interest, compounded once a year. He won't add or take out any money. The bank requires a $25 minimum balance.
problems.ask: How much interest will Jamal earn over the 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 2% of $2,500 is $50, so the value goes to $2,500 + $50 = $2,550.

problems.stem: At the warehouse where Isaac works, the 10 workers on the day shift packed an average of 45 boxes each on Monday. The 30 workers on the night shift, which started at midnight, packed an average of 85 boxes each.
problems.ask: What was the average number of boxes packed per worker across both shifts?

problems.stem: Maya is four times as old as her niece, Rosa. They live 6 blocks apart and walk together most weekends. In 14 years, Maya will be twice as old as Rosa.
problems.ask: How old is Maya now, in years?
steps: Let Rosa's age now be x, so Maya is 4x.
Subtract 2x and 14 from both sides: 2x = 28 − 14 = 14, so x = 7.
So Maya is 4 × 7 = 28 years old now. Check: in 14 years, 42 = 2 × 21.

bonus.stem: Today is Wednesday. A summer art program that Caleb signed up for starts tomorrow and meets every day for 48 days in a row. Every Monday is pizza day.
bonus.ask: How many pizza days will the program have?
steps: Each full week has exactly one Monday: 6.
The 6 extra days fall on the same weekdays as the first 6: Thursday through Tuesday, which includes one more Monday.

problems.stem: Caleb runs to the pet store for his dog. He buys a bag of treats for $6.25, a chew toy for $3.50, and a new leash for $11.50. There's no sales tax, and he pays with a $50 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Caleb get back?

problems.stem: Leah is visiting Japan, where 1 U.S. dollar is worth 150 yen that week. At a train station, she buys a set of chopsticks for 1,100 yen and a train snack for 250 yen. The station has 13 platforms.
problems.ask: How much did Leah spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Nadia is painting the four walls of her basement playroom, which is 13 feet long, 11 feet wide and 8 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $32 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Nadia need to buy?
steps: 768 ÷ 350 ≈ 2.2, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

problems.stem: Kofi buys a monthly bus pass. Last year the pass cost $30, and this year the transit agency raised the price to $42. He rides the bus about 20 days a month.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bus pass increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $12 ÷ $30 = 2/5 = 0.4.
As a percent, that is an increase of 40%.

problems.stem: Hana's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 70 minutes.
problems.ask: What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
steps: With 32 values in order, the median is the average of the 16th and 17th values.
Running totals: through 0: 7, through 1: 15, through 2: 19, through 3: 24, through 4: 27, through 5: 32.
Both fall in the row for 2 goals, so the median is 2 goals.

problems.stem: Silas started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 4 miles per hour. Fatima started running from the same spot 15 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 6 miles per hour. The path is 5 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Fatima catch up to Silas?
steps: Head start: in 15 minutes (1/4 hour), Silas covers 4 × 1/4 = 1 mile.
Time to close the gap: 1 ÷ 2 = 1/2 hour = 30 minutes.

problems.stem: Ezra, Yuki, Paige and two of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Ezra, Yuki and Paige are triplets and want to stand together, side by side. The photographer charges $50 for the session.
problems.ask: In how many different orders can the 5 of them line up?
steps: Glue the three into one block, leaving 3 units: 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 orders.
Inside the block the three can be ordered 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 ways.

problems.stem: Diego is tiling his kitchen floor, a rectangle 16 feet long and 10 feet wide. He is using square tiles that measure 24 inches on each side, and they fit exactly with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many tiles does Diego need?
steps: 24 inches is 2 feet. Along the length: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 tiles.

problems.stem: Yuki is driving 160 miles to her cousin's wedding, where she'll catch a ride home with family. Her car gets 32 miles per gallon, and gas costs $3.30 per gallon. Her car's tank holds 14 gallons.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the drive?

problems.stem: The water trough at Caleb's farm is a rectangular metal tank 5 feet long, 2 feet wide and 1.5 feet deep. It serves the four horses in the north pasture. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the trough hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Owen and Jade are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Owen could paint it in 6 hours, and Jade could paint it in 18 hours. The fence is 150 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Owen does 1/6 of the fence and Jade does 1/18.
Together: 1/6 + 1/18 = 3/18 + 1/18 = 4/18 = 2/9 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: Jordan packed a cooler for a beach day with 7 bottles of lemonade and 9 bottles of iced tea. The beach is 29 miles from his apartment. Later, he reaches into the ice without looking and pulls out two bottles, one after the other.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both bottles are the same drink?

problems.stem: Ravi is reading a 250-page novel for his book club and has already read 40 pages. He plans to read 30 pages each day until he finishes.
problems.ask: How many more days will it take to finish the book?
