problems.stem: Tariq is picking up bagels for the team's 8 a.m. meeting. The bakery sells bagels in packs of 4 for $3.50, or one at a time for $1.25 each. Nine people are coming, and Tariq wants at least one bagel per person. Leftovers are fine, but he can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Tariq can spend?
steps: 9 ÷ 4 = 2 full packs, with 1 person left over.

problems.stem: Eli surveyed the students in his grade about their favorite school lunch. Each student picked exactly one option, and the table shows the results. He collected the answers over five days.
problems.ask: What percent of the students surveyed did not choose "Pasta"?

problems.stem: Leah wants to start going to a climbing gym and is choosing between the two plans in the table. The gym is open until 10 o'clock on weeknights.
problems.ask: For how many visits would the two plans cost exactly the same?
steps: Member plan costs $90 more up front.
Basic plan costs $3 more per visit, so each visit closes the gap by $3.
Check: $90 + 30 × $12 = $450 and $0 + 30 × $15 = $450, so the answer is 30 visits.

problems.stem: The clock at the train station has a face 3 feet across. While Fatima waits on the platform, it reads 2:01. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 1 × 6 = 6 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 2 × 30 + 1 × 0.5 = 60.5 degrees past the 12.
That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 54.5 degrees.

bonus.stem: A hallway at Hugo's school has 103 closed lockers, numbered 1 to 103. Then 103 students walk by one at a time. Student 1 opens every locker. Student 2 switches every 2nd locker (closing it if open, opening it if closed), student 3 switches every 3rd locker, and so on, until student 103 switches only locker 103.
bonus.ask: How many lockers are closed at the end?
steps: A locker is switched once for each number that divides it (locker 12: by 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12).
Divisors come in pairs (1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4), so most lockers are switched an even number of times and end closed.
Only perfect squares have an odd number of divisors, because one pair repeats (6 × 6 = 36).
Perfect squares up to 103: 1, 4, 9, …, 100, which is 10 lockers open.

problems.stem: Mei is shopping for a new set of mixing bowls and finds one priced at $23. The sales tax where she lives is 8%, added at the register.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the set of mixing bowls, including tax?

problems.stem: Jordan is reseeding a rectangular lawn that measures 50 feet by 45 feet. A bag of grass seed covers 200 square feet, and the lawn gets about 6 hours of sun a day. Seed is sold only in whole bags.
problems.ask: How many bags of seed must Jordan buy to cover the whole lawn?
steps: 11 bags cover 11 × 200 = 2,200 square feet, which is not enough.
12 bags cover 2,400 square feet, so Jordan needs 12 bags.

problems.stem: Tariq bought a pair of running shoes at a sporting-goods store during a 25%-off sale, and he also used a $5 coupon. The register took 25% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. Only four pairs in his size were left on the shelf. Before tax, Tariq paid $91.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the shoes?
steps: $96 is what was left after 25% off, so it is 75% of the original price.

problems.stem: Ingrid is growing bacteria for a biology lab. She starts a dish with 150 bacteria, and under these conditions the population doubles every 30 minutes. The dish is 15 centimeters across.
problems.ask: How many bacteria will be in the dish after 2 hours?

problems.stem: At an ice cream stand, customers build a sundae by choosing exactly 2 different toppings from a list of 8. Every sundae also gets one of 3 ice cream flavors: vanilla, chocolate or strawberry. Each sundae comes in a 10-ounce cup. The order the toppings are chosen in doesn't matter.
problems.ask: How many different sundaes can a customer build?
steps: Pick 2 of 8 toppings: 8 × 7 = 56 ordered picks, ÷ 2 because order doesn't matter = 28 sets.
Each set can go with any of the 3 ice cream flavors: 28 × 3 = 84 sundaes.

bonus.stem: Kenji is numbering the pages of his scrapbook, from page 1 to page 84, by hand with a number stamp.
bonus.ask: How many digits will that take in all?

problems.stem: At 1:40 p.m., Jordan started a volunteer shift at the library. The shift ended at 4:05 p.m., and he walked home.
problems.ask: How many minutes long was the shift?
steps: From 1:40 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. is 20 minutes.
From 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 2 hours, or 120 minutes.
From 4:00 p.m. to 4:05 p.m. is 5 minutes.

problems.stem: Leah bowls in a league with 21 teams. So far this season she has bowled four games, scoring 154, 202, 156, and 182. She wants her average after the next game to be exactly 180.
problems.ask: What score does Leah need in the next game?
steps: An average of 180 over 5 games means a total of 180 × 5 = 900.

problems.stem: Luis wants to buy a laptop at an electronics store. The price is $751 if he pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $50 down, then 18 monthly payments of $52. The laptop weighs about 5 pounds.
problems.ask: How much more would Luis pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: In March, the hardware store where Nadia works raised the price of a snow shovel by 40%. In June, the store put it on sale for 40% off that new price. Nadia has worked at the store for 6 months.
problems.ask: By what percent is the June price lower than the original price?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
84 is 16 below 100, so it is 16% lower.

problems.stem: Ingrid is saving for a new bike. She puts $9 in a jar the first week, and every week after that she puts in $5 more than the week before. She started the plan on her 12th birthday.
problems.ask: How much will Ingrid have saved in all after 19 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 19, week 2 with week 18, and so on: each pair adds to $9 + $99 = $108.
With 19 weeks, the average week is $108 ÷ 2 = $54, so the total is 19 × $54 = $1,026.

problems.stem: Ravi is sewing curtains. The fabric he likes costs $22.50 for 5 yards, and the shop sells it by the yard at that same rate. He needs 7 yards.
problems.ask: How much will the fabric cost?

problems.stem: Nico is buying snacks for his family at a baseball game. The snack bar's prices, tax included, are in the table. Their seats are in row 14. Nico orders two bottles of water, one pretzel, and four bags of popcorn.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Nico's order?

problems.stem: Aiyana took her family out for brunch at a diner that opened 40 years ago. They ordered two pancake plates at $18 each and a pitcher of orange juice for $12. Sales tax is 8%, and they added a 15% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the brunch, including tax and tip?
steps: Tip: 10% of $48 is $4.80, plus half of that, $2.40, gives $7.20.

problems.stem: Felix's living room has a round rug that is 5 feet across. He wants to replace it with a round rug that is 6 feet across. The room is 16 feet long.
problems.ask: The new rug will cover how many times as much floor area as the old rug?
steps: A circle's area is π × radius², so area grows with the square of the diameter.

problems.stem: Andre's booth at the town festival has 8 rubber ducks floating in a pool. A player pays $5, picks one duck at random, and wins the prize marked underneath; the duck then goes back in. The table shows the prizes. The festival lasts 3 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the booth make per game after paying out prizes?
steps: If each duck came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $20 + 2 × $3 = $26.
The booth keeps $5 − $3.25 = $1.75 per game on average.

problems.stem: Kofi is running a lemonade stand. He makes seven pitchers of lemonade, and each pitcher holds 8 cups. There are 4 cups in a quart.
problems.ask: How many quarts of lemonade does Kofi make?
steps: There are 4 cups in a quart: 56 ÷ 4 = 14 quarts.

problems.stem: Nadia works at a warehouse for $14 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times her regular rate. She has worked there for 8 years. Last week she worked 42 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Nadia earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $14 = $21 an hour, for 42 − 40 = 2 hours.

problems.stem: Kenji is mixing concrete for a garden path that is 30 feet long. His mix uses cement, sand and gravel in the ratio 2:4:1 by volume. He needs 28 buckets of mix in all.
problems.ask: How many more buckets of sand than cement does Kenji need?
steps: Sand minus cement: 4 − 2 = 2 parts, and 2 × 4 = 8 buckets.

problems.stem: A rectangular park near Sofia's apartment is 360 meters long and 150 meters wide. Sofia usually walks along two edges to get from one corner to the opposite corner. Today she cuts straight across the grass on the diagonal instead. The park has 10 benches.
problems.ask: How many meters shorter is the diagonal route than the route along the two edges?
steps: Shrink the numbers first: 360 = 30 × 12 and 150 = 30 × 5. Since 12² + 5² = 144 + 25 = 169 = 13², the diagonal is 30 × 13 = 390 meters.

problems.stem: Caleb and Ruth are 40 miles apart on the same highway and drive toward each other to meet for dinner. Caleb drives at 40 miles per hour, and Ruth drives at 50 miles per hour. Ruth leaves 15 minutes after Caleb. Caleb's car holds 11 gallons of gas.
problems.ask: How many minutes after Caleb leaves do they meet?
steps: Head start: in 15 minutes, Caleb covers 40 × 1/4 = 10 miles.
Distance left when Ruth leaves: 40 − 10 = 30 miles.
Together they close 40 + 50 = 90 miles per hour: 30 ÷ 90 = 1/3 hour = 20 minutes after Ruth leaves.
Counting from when Caleb leaves: 15 + 20 = 35 minutes.

problems.stem: Amara has been waiting for a sale on a winter jacket that normally costs $158. This weekend the store has it marked 50% off.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the winter jacket, before tax?

problems.stem: A smoothie recipe makes 4 servings and calls for 1/2 cup of plain yogurt. Ben is making 3 servings for his soccer team after practice. The yogurt was on sale for $3.50 a tub.
problems.ask: If he scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of yogurt will he need?

problems.stem: Rosa is buying laundry detergent. The store sells the same brand in the three sizes shown in the table. She does about three loads of laundry a week.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per fluid ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Omar's world history grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and his average so far. There are 19 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Omar need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 85?
steps: To finish at 85, the final must add 85 − 60.4 = 24.6 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 24.6 ÷ 0.3 = 82.

problems.stem: Malik drove 120 miles to visit his aunt and averaged 60 miles per hour on the way there. Coming home on the same roads, heavy traffic held him to an average of 40 miles per hour. His car gets about 25 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: What was Malik's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Theo needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. He plans to pick up the car at 9:15 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $35 more up front.
Company B costs $0.10 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.10.

problems.stem: In a board game, Priya's piece is stuck in the jail space. Under the house rules, she rolls a standard six-sided die two times, and she escapes if any roll is a 5 or a 6. The board has 40 spaces in all.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Priya escapes?
steps: Work with the opposite: one roll is not a 5 or a 6 with probability 4/6 = 2/3.

problems.stem: Priya is tracking how long she practices piano. From Monday to Friday, she practiced 29, 46, 43, 31, and 31 minutes.
problems.ask: What was her average practice time per day, in minutes?

problems.stem: Jordan is mapping out a bike ride. On the town's trail map, 1 inch stands for 3 miles. The ride follows the river trail for 2 3/4 inches on the map, then the park loop for 2 1/4 inches. The trail map shows 12 drinking fountains.
problems.ask: How many miles long is the ride?

problems.stem: Sam helped run a pancake breakfast at the fire station. Adult plates cost $7 and kids' plates cost $5. They served 140 plates and took in $866, with twelve volunteers working the griddles.
problems.ask: How many adult plates did they serve?
steps: If all 140 were kids' plates, the total would be 140 × $5 = $700.
The actual total is $866 − $700 = $166 more than that.
Each adult plate brings in $2 more than each kids' plate, so adult plates: $166 ÷ $2 = 83.

problems.stem: Ava mixed 4 liters of liquid plant food that is 20% concentrate. The label says seedlings need a mix that is only 8% concentrate, so she will dilute it with water. She is growing three trays of seedlings.
problems.ask: How many liters of water should Ava add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 8% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 20/8 = 5/2: 4 × 5/2 = 10 liters.

problems.stem: A community center asked 50 members which summer trips they would sign up for. The results are in the table. The "Hiking trip" and "Kayaking trip" counts include the members who signed up for both trips. The sign-up sheet was posted for 16 days.
problems.ask: How many of the 50 members signed up for neither trip?

bonus.stem: Nadia is helping sell tickets for an outdoor amphitheater with 29 rows of seats. The front row has 22 seats, and each row behind it has 2 more seats than the row in front of it.
bonus.ask: How many seats are there in all?
steps: Pair the first and last rows, the second and second-to-last, and so on: each pair holds 22 + 78 = 100.
With 29 rows, the average row is 100 ÷ 2 = 50, so the total is 29 × 50 = 1,450 seats.

problems.stem: Lucia and two coworkers stop at a diner for breakfast, and Lucia offers to pay. The check is $32.80. She plans to add a 15% tip on the full check.
problems.ask: How much does Lucia pay in all, including the tip?

problems.stem: Jordan must be at work by 9:15 a.m. for a meeting. He walks 10 minutes to the train station, rides the train for 25 minutes, and then walks 10 minutes to the office. A train ticket costs $2.75, and a train leaves the moment he reaches the platform. It is 7:50 a.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Jordan wait before leaving home?
steps: From 7:50 a.m. to 9:15 a.m. is 85 minutes.

problems.stem: Diego deposited $1,000 in a savings account that earns 10% interest, compounded once a year. He won't add or take out any money. The bank requires a $50 minimum balance.
problems.ask: How much interest will Diego earn over the 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 10% of $1,000 is $100, so the value goes to $1,000 + $100 = $1,100.

problems.stem: Owen started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 4 miles per hour. Raul started running from the same spot 6 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 6 miles per hour. The path is 5 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Raul catch up to Owen?
steps: Head start: in 6 minutes (1/10 hour), Owen covers 4 × 1/10 = 0.4 miles.
Time to close the gap: 0.4 ÷ 2 = 1/5 hour = 12 minutes.

problems.stem: Ava buys 15 stamps at the post office: some 60-cent postcard stamps and some 75-cent letter stamps. She spends $10.80 in all. There are 5 people in line behind her.
problems.ask: How many letter stamps does Ava buy?
steps: Suppose all 15 were postcard stamps: 15 × 60 cents = 900 cents.
The real total is 1,080 cents, which is 1,080 cents − 900 cents = 180 cents more.
Each letter stamp adds 15 cents more than a postcard stamp, so there are 180 cents ÷ 15 cents = 12 letter stamps (check: 12 × 15 cents = 180 cents).

problems.stem: Jamal and three coworkers chip in for a retirement gift: a gift card worth $105 and a cake that costs $38. They split the cost evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Jamal plus three others makes 4 people.

problems.stem: Dev has his eye on a winter coat with a regular price of $240. This week it's marked 25% off. At checkout, he also uses a coupon for an extra 25% off the sale price. The sale ends in 7 days.
problems.ask: How much does Dev pay for the winter coat, before tax?
steps: 25% of $240 is $60, so the sale price is $240 − $60 = $180.
The extra 25% comes off $180, not the original price: 25% of $180 is $45.

problems.stem: Imani is painting the four walls of her living room, which is 17 feet long, 15 feet wide and 10 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. One gallon of paint covers 400 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $45 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Imani need to buy?
steps: 1,280 ÷ 400 = 3.2, which is more than 3, so round up to 4 gallons.

problems.stem: Andre asked every household on his street how many pets it has and recorded the results in the table. It took him two afternoons to reach everyone.
problems.ask: What is the median number of pets per household?
steps: With 26 values in order, the median is the average of the 13th and 14th values.
Running totals: through 0: 5, through 1: 13, through 2: 16, through 3: 23, through 4: 26.
They are 1 and 2, so the median is (1 + 2) ÷ 2 = 1.5 pets.

problems.stem: Ava, Mateo, Hana and three of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Ava, Mateo and Hana are triplets and want to stand together, side by side. The photographer charges $60 for the session.
problems.ask: In how many different orders can the 6 of them line up?
steps: Glue the three into one block, leaving 4 units: 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24 orders.
Inside the block the three can be ordered 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 ways.

problems.stem: Tariq is building a rectangular dog run in his backyard. It will be 26 feet long and 24 feet wide. One 26-foot side runs along the shed wall, so it needs no fence.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Tariq need?
steps: Fence the other 26-foot side and both 24-foot sides.

problems.stem: Ravi bikes to work. He rides 10 miles on a bike path at a steady 15 miles per hour, then 5 miles through city streets at a steady 10 miles per hour. His bike has 14 gears.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 10 ÷ 15 = 2/3 hour, which is 40 minutes.
Second part: 5 ÷ 10 = 1/2 hour, which is 30 minutes.

problems.stem: Grace built a rectangular backyard pond that is 12 feet long, 6 feet wide and 1.5 feet deep, and she stocked it with fifteen goldfish. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the pond hold when completely full?

problems.stem: At the warehouse where Andre works, the 7 workers on the day shift packed an average of 78 boxes each on Monday. The 13 workers on the night shift, which started at 10 p.m., packed an average of 68 boxes each.
problems.ask: What was the average number of boxes packed per worker across both shifts?

problems.stem: A fruit bowl in Chloe's kitchen holds 4 red apples and 7 green apples. She bought them at a farm stand that opened 27 years ago. On her way out the door, she grabs two apples at random, one after the other.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both apples are the same color?

problems.stem: Jordan stops at the hardware store for a weekend project. He buys a box of screws for $4.25, a roll of tape for $4.50, and a paintbrush for $5.75. There's no sales tax, and he pays with a $20 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Jordan get back?

problems.stem: Mei is visiting Japan, where 1 U.S. dollar is worth 150 yen that week. At a train station, she buys a souvenir fan for 1,350 yen and a bowl of ramen for 450 yen. The station has 11 platforms.
problems.ask: How much did Mei spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Dmitri's home internet bill used to be $40 a month. After he upgraded his plan, the monthly bill became $45. The new plan has a download speed of 200 megabits per second.
problems.ask: By what percent did Dmitri's monthly internet bill increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $5 ÷ $40 = 1/8 = 0.125.
As a percent, that is an increase of 12.5%.

problems.stem: Mateo and Ezra are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Mateo could paint it in 3 hours, and Ezra could paint it in 7 hours. The fence is 200 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Mateo does 1/3 of the fence and Ezra does 1/7.
Together: 1/3 + 1/7 = 7/21 + 3/21 = 10/21 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: Dev, who is 6 feet tall, stands on level ground and notices that his shadow is 7 feet long. At the same moment, the shadow of a nearby oak tree is 77 feet long. The tree was planted about 45 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the oak tree, in feet?
steps: The sun hits both at the same angle, so height ÷ shadow is the same for the oak tree and Dev: 6 ÷ 7.
The oak tree's shadow is 77 ÷ 7 = 11 times as long as Dev's.
So the oak tree is 11 × 6 = 66 feet tall.

problems.stem: Luis is covering a playroom floor with square foam mats that are 24 inches on each side. The room is a rectangle 14 feet long and 8 feet wide, and the mats fit exactly.
problems.ask: How many mats does Luis need?
steps: 24 inches is 2 feet. Along the length: 14 ÷ 2 = 7 mats.

problems.stem: Carmen is driving to a lake house, which is 60 miles from home, and then driving back. Her car gets 30 miles per gallon, and gas costs $3.10 per gallon. The drive takes about 2 hours each way, with one stop for lunch.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the round trip?

problems.stem: Kenji surveyed the students in his grade about their favorite school lunch. Each student picked exactly one option, and the table shows the results. He collected the answers over three days.
problems.ask: What percent of the students surveyed chose either "Pizza" or "Salad bar"?

problems.stem: Tess takes a 600-milligram dose of a medicine at 6:45 p.m. with a glass of water. The amount of the medicine in the body drops by half every 3 hours.
problems.ask: How many milligrams of the medicine are left in her body 6 hours after the dose?

problems.stem: Eli is four times as old as his nephew, Owen. Every summer the two of them go fishing at a lake 20 miles from home. In 14 years, Eli will be twice as old as Owen.
problems.ask: How old is Eli now, in years?
steps: Let Owen's age now be x, so Eli is 4x.
Subtract 2x and 14 from both sides: 2x = 28 − 14 = 14, so x = 7.
So Eli is 4 × 7 = 28 years old now. Check: in 14 years, 42 = 2 × 21.

bonus.stem: The town is planting trees along both sides of a straight path that is 66 feet long. On each side, there will be a tree every 6 feet, with a tree at both ends. Ava volunteers to dig the holes.
bonus.ask: How many trees will be planted in all?
steps: There is one more tree than gaps (count the end): 11 + 1 = 12.
Both sides of the path: 2 × 12 = 24 trees.

problems.stem: Eli is working on a 1,000-piece jigsaw puzzle. He has placed 400 pieces so far and places 75 more pieces each night.
problems.ask: How many more nights will it take to finish the puzzle?

problems.stem: Rosa is picking up donuts for the class's 9:30 a.m. study session. The donut shop sells donuts in packs of 4 for $3.50, or one at a time for $1.10 each. Seventeen students signed up, and Rosa wants at least one donut per person. Leftovers are fine, but she can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Rosa can spend?
steps: 17 ÷ 4 = 4 full packs, with 1 person left over.

problems.stem: Maya's chemistry grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and her average so far. There are 33 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Maya need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 88?
steps: To finish at 88, the final must add 88 − 59.8 = 28.2 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 28.2 ÷ 0.3 = 94.

problems.stem: Noor's club ran a bake sale on Saturday morning. They sold cookies, brownies and muffins in the ratio 2:3:2, and they sold 84 items in all. Every item was priced at $1.50.
problems.ask: How many brownies did the club sell?

problems.stem: Zoe owns 15 shares of a company's stock. On Monday the share price fell 25%. On Tuesday it rose 30% from Monday's closing price.
problems.ask: By what percent is Tuesday's closing price lower than the price before Monday's change?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
97.5 is 2.5 below 100, so it is 2.5% lower.

problems.stem: Diego's living room has a round rug that is 5 feet across. He wants to replace it with a round rug that is 8 feet across. The room is 16 feet long.
problems.ask: The new rug will cover how many times as much floor area as the old rug?
steps: A circle's area is π × radius², so area grows with the square of the diameter.

problems.stem: Mateo just started a dog-walking business. He moves $13 into savings the first week, and each week after that he moves $2 more than the week before. He has 6 regular customers.
problems.ask: How much will Mateo have set aside in all after 9 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 9, week 2 with week 8, and so on: each pair adds to $13 + $29 = $42.
With 9 weeks, the average week is $42 ÷ 2 = $21, so the total is 9 × $21 = $189.

problems.stem: Eli is shopping for a new blender and finds one priced at $68. The sales tax where he lives is 6%, added at the register.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the blender, including tax?

problems.stem: Mateo is reseeding a rectangular lawn that measures 55 feet by 35 feet. A bag of grass seed covers 200 square feet, and the lawn gets about 7 hours of sun a day. Seed is sold only in whole bags.
problems.ask: How many bags of seed must Mateo buy to cover the whole lawn?
steps: 9 bags cover 9 × 200 = 1,800 square feet, which is not enough.
10 bags cover 2,000 square feet, so Mateo needs 10 bags.

problems.stem: Paige bought a winter coat at a department store during a 50%-off sale, and she also used a $15 coupon. The register took 50% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. The sale lasted three days. Before tax, Paige paid $72.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the coat?
steps: $87 is what was left after 50% off, so it is 50% of the original price.

problems.stem: Ava rode her bike 36 miles to a lake, mostly uphill, averaging 9 miles per hour. She rode home the same way, mostly downhill, at 18 miles per hour. She packed two bottles of water for the ride.
problems.ask: What was Ava's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 72 ÷ 6 = 12 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Caleb runs a prize wheel at the school fair. The wheel has 10 equal sections, each equally likely to land on top, and a spin costs $5. The table shows what the sections pay. The fair runs for 8 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the prize wheel make per spin after paying out prizes?
steps: If each section came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $20 + 3 × $1 = $23.
The booth keeps $5 − $2.30 = $2.70 per spin on average.

problems.stem: At the hardware store, 4 feet of rope costs $1.40. Dmitri needs 9 feet to hang a porch swing, and the store cuts rope to any length at the same price per foot.
problems.ask: How much will 9 feet of rope cost?

problems.stem: Jade is picking up breakfast for her study group at a coffee shop. The prices, which include tax, are in the table. The shop opens at 6:30 every morning. Jade orders four lattes, four drip coffees, and two blueberry muffins.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Jade's order?

problems.stem: Amara ordered lunch from a café for a team meeting that ran 60 minutes. The order was four sandwich boxes at $13 each plus a fruit tray for $7. Sales tax is 10%, and she added a 15% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the lunch order, including tax and tip?
steps: Tip: 10% of $59 is $5.90, plus half of that, $2.95, gives $8.85.

problems.stem: Jordan needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. He plans to pick up the car at 8 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $15 more up front.
Company B costs $0.10 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.10.

problems.stem: The clock at the train station has a face 3 feet across. While Malik waits on the platform, it reads 6:07. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 7 × 6 = 42 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 6 × 30 + 7 × 0.5 = 183.5 degrees past the 12.
That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 141.5 degrees.

bonus.stem: June's little cousin is racing up a set of 6 porch steps. Each jump takes her cousin up one, two or three steps, in any mix, and the last jump has to land exactly on the top step.
bonus.ask: How many different ways can the climb up all 6 steps go?
steps: To land on step k, the last move came from k − 1, k − 2 or k − 3, so ways(k) is the sum of the three before it.
Step 1: 1 way. Step 2: 2 ways. Step 3: 4 ways.
Keep adding three at a time: 1, 2, 4, 7, 13, 24. So step 6 has 24 ways.

problems.stem: At 3:35 p.m., Raul put a loaf of bread in the oven. He took it out at 4:25 p.m., when the crust was golden brown.
problems.ask: For how many minutes did the bread bake?
steps: From 3:35 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 25 minutes.
From 4:00 p.m. to 4:25 p.m. is 25 minutes.

problems.stem: Nico bowls in a league with 14 teams. So far this season he has bowled three games, scoring 195, 153, and 182. He wants his average after the next game to be exactly 170.
problems.ask: What score does Nico need in the next game?
steps: An average of 170 over 4 games means a total of 170 × 4 = 680.

problems.stem: Rosa wants to buy an electric bike at a bike shop. The price is $882 if she pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $200 down, then 6 monthly payments of $127. Its battery can go about 30 miles on one charge.
problems.ask: How much more would Rosa pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Arjun leans a 26-foot ladder against the side of his house to clean the gutters. For safety, the bottom of the ladder sits 10 feet out from the wall, on level ground. The ladder is rated to hold 300 pounds.
problems.ask: How high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach, in feet?
steps: The wall, the ground and the ladder form a right triangle, with the ladder as the hypotenuse.

problems.stem: Maya and Lucia live 34.5 miles apart along a straight bike trail, and they ride toward each other to meet for lunch. Maya rides at 14 miles per hour, and Lucia rides at 9 miles per hour. They leave at the same time. The trail has 17 benches along the way.
problems.ask: How many minutes after they leave do they meet?
steps: The gap closes at 14 + 9 = 23 miles per hour.

bonus.stem: A gumball machine holds 17 red, 11 green, 14 yellow and 12 blue gumballs, well mixed. Each coin gives one gumball at random. Ava wants three gumballs of the same color for a craft project.
bonus.ask: What is the fewest gumballs Ava must get to be sure of having three of the same color?
steps: Worst case: she gets two of every color and no third: 2 × 4 = 8 gumballs.
The next gumball must be a third of some color: 8 + 1 = 9 gumballs.

problems.stem: Hana is running a lemonade stand. She makes nine pitchers of lemonade, and each pitcher holds 8 cups. There are 4 cups in a quart.
problems.ask: How many quarts of lemonade does Hana make?
steps: There are 4 cups in a quart: 72 ÷ 4 = 18 quarts.

problems.stem: Zoe works at a grocery store for $18 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times her regular rate. Her commute is 7 miles each way. Last week she worked 44 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Zoe earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $18 = $27 an hour, for 44 − 40 = 4 hours.

problems.stem: Victor helped run a pancake breakfast at the fire station. Adult plates cost $9 and kids' plates cost $6. They served 237 plates and took in $1,620, with eight volunteers working the griddles.
problems.ask: How many kids' plates did they serve?
steps: If all 237 were kids' plates, the total would be 237 × $6 = $1,422.
The actual total is $1,620 − $1,422 = $198 more than that.
Each adult plate brings in $3 more than each kids' plate, so adult plates: $198 ÷ $3 = 66.

problems.stem: Ava mixed 6 liters of liquid plant food that is 20% concentrate. The label says seedlings need a mix that is only 15% concentrate, so she will dilute it with water. She is growing seven trays of seedlings.
problems.ask: How many liters of water should Ava add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 15% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 20/15 = 4/3: 6 × 4/3 = 8 liters.

problems.stem: At a pizza shop, customers build a pizza by choosing exactly 2 different toppings from a list of 8. Every pizza also gets one of 2 crusts: thin or regular. A large pizza is cut into 12 slices. The order the toppings are chosen in doesn't matter.
problems.ask: How many different pizzas can a customer build?
steps: Pick 2 of 8 toppings: 8 × 7 = 56 ordered picks, ÷ 2 because order doesn't matter = 28 sets.
Each set can go with any of the 2 crusts: 28 × 2 = 56 pizzas.

problems.stem: Esme spots a winter jacket with a price tag of $105. A sign on the rack says the price will be 50% off at the register.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the winter jacket, before tax?

problems.stem: Andre's pancake recipe makes 8 pancakes and calls for 2/3 cup of flour. He is making 24 pancakes for a family brunch. The recipe says to cook each pancake for 2 minutes per side.
problems.ask: If he scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of flour will he need?

problems.stem: Priya cooks with olive oil almost every night. Her grocery store sells it in the three bottle sizes shown in the table, and she usually shops on Mondays.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per fluid ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Omar set out on his bike along the river trail, riding at a steady 9 miles per hour. Sofia left from the same spot 30 minutes later and followed the same trail at a steady 19 miles per hour. The trail is 20 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting did Sofia catch up to Omar?
steps: Head start: in 30 minutes (1/2 hour), Omar covers 9 × 1/2 = 4.5 miles.
Time to close the gap: 4.5 ÷ 10 = 9/20 hour = 27 minutes.

problems.stem: Zoe surveyed all 75 students in her grade about pets at home. The results are in the table. The "Has a dog" and "Has a cat" counts include the students who have both a dog and a cat. She handed out the surveys during a 9-minute homeroom.
problems.ask: How many of the 75 students have neither a dog nor a cat?

problems.stem: Eli rode his bike to work four days this week. The rides took 30, 32, 24, and 22 minutes.
problems.ask: What was his average ride time, in minutes?

problems.stem: Hana is making lasagna for 8 guests and wants it ready to serve at 5:00 p.m. sharp. Assembling it takes 30 minutes, baking takes 60 minutes, and it must rest 15 minutes before serving. These steps happen one after another. It is 2:45 p.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Hana wait before starting?
steps: From 2:45 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 135 minutes.

problems.stem: Ruth bought a used car for $19,000. Her mechanic estimates that the car will lose 25% of its value each year, based on what it is worth at the start of that year. The car gets about 29 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: Using that estimate, how much value will the car lose over the 2 years?

problems.stem: Diego's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 60 minutes.
problems.ask: What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
steps: With 29 values in order, the median is the 15th value.
Running totals: through 0: 9, through 1: 11, through 2: 17, through 3: 18, through 4: 21, through 5: 29.
The 15th value falls in the row for 2 goals, so the median is 2 goals.

problems.stem: Victor and his brother flip a coin each night to decide who washes the dinner dishes; heads means Victor washes. This week they'll flip for six nights in a row. Dinner is usually ready by 6:30 each evening.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Victor washes the dishes at least once in those 6 nights?
steps: Work with the opposite: Victor never washes only if every flip is tails. One flip is tails with probability 1/2.

problems.stem: After a long hike, Sam stops at a cafe for dinner. His bill is $33 before tip. He always tips 20% of the bill.
problems.ask: How much is the tip?

problems.stem: Tess is planning a hike with a trail map where 1 centimeter represents 5 kilometers. The trail to the waterfall measures 7 centimeters on the map, and the trail back to the parking lot measures 6 centimeters. The parking lot has 60 spaces.
problems.ask: How many kilometers long is the whole hike?

problems.stem: Esme is painting the four walls of her living room, which is 19 feet long, 14 feet wide and 10 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. The door and windows take up 50 square feet that won't be painted. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $39 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Esme need to buy?
steps: Minus the door and windows: 660 − 50 = 610 square feet.
1,220 ÷ 350 ≈ 3.5, which is more than 3, so round up to 4 gallons.

problems.stem: Last month, a bag of coffee beans at Fatima's grocery store cost $8. This month the same bag costs $10. Fatima goes through about one bag every 13 days.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bag increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $2 ÷ $8 = 1/4 = 0.25.
As a percent, that is an increase of 25%.

problems.stem: Dmitri and Jordan are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Dmitri could paint it in 9 hours, and Jordan could paint it in 21 hours. The fence is 150 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Dmitri does 1/9 of the fence and Jordan does 1/21.
Together: 1/9 + 1/21 = 7/63 + 3/63 = 10/63 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: At the warehouse where Mateo works, the 6 workers on the day shift packed an average of 49 boxes each on Monday. The 14 workers on the night shift, which started at 10 p.m., packed an average of 59 boxes each.
problems.ask: What was the average number of boxes packed per worker across both shifts?

problems.stem: Ravi empties the cup holder in his car and finds nothing but quarters and nickels. There are 30 coins in all, worth $2.90 together. He has had the car for 3 years.
problems.ask: How many quarters are in the cup holder?
steps: Suppose all 30 were nickels: 30 × 5 cents = 150 cents.
The real total is 290 cents, which is 290 cents − 150 cents = 140 cents more.
Each quarter adds 20 cents more than a nickel, so there are 140 cents ÷ 20 cents = 7 quarters.

problems.stem: Sofia and three friends rent a lake cabin for a weekend. The rental costs $420, plus a $135 cleaning fee. They split the whole cost evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Sofia plus three others makes 4 people.

problems.stem: Malik is shopping for a desk chair. The one he wants normally sells for $110, but it's on sale for 40% off. The cashier then applies an extra 25% off the sale price for new members. The store is 11 miles from his home.
problems.ask: How much does Malik pay for the desk chair, before tax?
steps: 40% of $110 is $44, so the sale price is $110 − $44 = $66.
The extra 25% comes off $66, not the original price: 25% of $66 is $16.50.

problems.stem: Sam built a rectangular backyard pond that is 10 feet long, 4 feet wide and 2 feet deep, and he stocked it with nine goldfish. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the pond hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Grace is studying a 640-gram sample of a radioactive substance in a lab. The substance has a half-life of 12 days, which means half of whatever is left decays every 12 days. The sample is stored in a case that weighs 20 pounds.
problems.ask: How many days will it take until only 20 grams of the substance remain?
steps: Halve until 20 grams remain: 640 → 320 → 160 → 80 → 40 → 20. That is 5 halvings.

problems.stem: Dev, Leah, Wes and three of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Dev, Leah and Wes are triplets and want to stand together, side by side. The photographer charges $50 for the session.
problems.ask: In how many different orders can the 6 of them line up?
steps: Glue the three into one block, leaving 4 units: 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24 orders.
Inside the block the three can be ordered 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 ways.

bonus.stem: A beetle starts at the bottom of a 16-foot garden wall. Every day it crawls 4 feet up, and every night it slides back down 1 foot. Ezra checks on it each morning.
bonus.ask: On which day does the beetle first reach the top of the wall, if the first day of climbing is day 1?
steps: Each full day and night, the beetle gains 4 − 1 = 3 feet.
On its last day it climbs 4 feet and never slides back, so it only needs to start that day at 16 − 4 = 12 feet.
Reaching 12 feet takes 12 ÷ 3 = 4 full days and nights.
It reaches the top on day 4 + 1 = 5.

problems.stem: Amara is fencing in a rectangular play area for her kids. The area is 27 feet long and 18 feet wide. She'll fence all four sides.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Amara need?
steps: One length plus one width: 27 + 18 = 45 feet.
Going all the way around doubles that: 2 × 45 = 90 feet.

problems.stem: Jamal is traveling in Italy, where prices are in euros. That week, 1 euro costs $1.10 in U.S. money. He buys a pair of sunglasses for 32 euros and a cookbook for 23 euros. His hotel is 4 blocks from the shop.
problems.ask: How much did Jamal spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Diego surveyed the students in his grade about their favorite school lunch. Each student picked exactly one option, and the table shows the results. He collected the answers over three days.
problems.ask: What percent of the students surveyed chose either "Pasta" or "Pizza"?

problems.stem: Hugo is writing a report about his town. Its population shrank by 20% from 2016 to 2020, then grew by 20% from 2020 to 2024. The town has 6 public parks.
problems.ask: By what percent is the 2024 population lower than the 2016 population?
steps: Start with a population of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
96 is 4 below 100, so it is 4% lower.

problems.stem: Dmitri packed a cooler for a beach day with 3 bottles of lemonade and 6 bottles of iced tea. The beach is 19 miles from his apartment. Later, he reaches into the ice without looking and pulls out two bottles, one after the other.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both bottles are the same drink?

bonus.stem: A window in Dev's attic is divided into a 7-by-7 grid of square panes. Looking at the grid lines, Dev wonders how many squares can be traced, counting every size, from single panes up to the biggest square that fits.
bonus.ask: How many squares of all sizes are in the 7-by-7 grid?
steps: A k-by-k square can start in 7 − k + 1 spots across and the same number down, so there are (7 − k + 1)² of them.

problems.stem: Yuki stops at the hardware store for a weekend project. She buys a box of screws for $2.75, a roll of tape for $5.25, and a paintbrush for $7.25. There's no sales tax, and she pays with a $20 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Yuki get back?

problems.stem: Sofia is driving to her grandparents' farm. She drives 75 miles on the highway at a steady 50 miles per hour, then 20 miles on country roads at a steady 30 miles per hour. Two cousins are riding along with her.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 75 ÷ 50 = 1 1/2 hours, which is 90 minutes.
Second part: 20 ÷ 30 = 2/3 hour, which is 40 minutes.

problems.stem: Malik's chemistry grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and his average so far. There are 24 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Malik need on the final exam to finish with exactly a 90?
steps: To finish at 90, the final must add 90 − 50.4 = 39.6 points.
The final is worth 40%, so the score needed is 39.6 ÷ 0.4 = 99.

problems.stem: Aiyana has a recipe for a 6-inch round cake, but she wants to bake it in a 10-inch round pan instead, filled to the same depth. The oven is set to 325 degrees.
problems.ask: How many times the original recipe should Aiyana make to fill the bigger pan?

problems.stem: Maya just started a dog-walking business. She moves $6 into savings the first week, and each week after that she moves $5 more than the week before. She has 7 regular customers.
problems.ask: How much will Maya have set aside in all after 9 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 9, week 2 with week 8, and so on: each pair adds to $6 + $46 = $52.
With 9 weeks, the average week is $52 ÷ 2 = $26, so the total is 9 × $26 = $234.

problems.stem: Owen is tiling a small laundry room floor that measures 9 feet by 5 feet. He picked square tiles that are 6 inches on each side, and they fit exactly with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many tiles does Owen need?
steps: 6 inches is half a foot, so 2 tiles fit in each foot.
Along the length: 9 × 2 = 18. Along the width: 5 × 2 = 10.

problems.stem: Chloe is driving to a lake house, which is 80 miles from home, and then driving back. Her car gets 20 miles per gallon, and gas costs $3.00 per gallon. The drive takes about 2 hours each way, with one stop for lunch.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the round trip?

problems.stem: Ravi's club ran a bake sale on Saturday morning. They sold cookies, brownies and muffins in the ratio 5:1:3, and they sold 117 items in all. Every item was priced at $1.50.
problems.ask: How many muffins did the club sell?

problems.stem: Jamal drove 75 miles to visit his aunt and averaged 50 miles per hour on the way there. Coming home on the same roads, heavy traffic held him to an average of 30 miles per hour. His car gets about 25 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: What was Jamal's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 150 ÷ 4 = 37.5 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Victor is twice as old as his niece, Rosa. Every summer the two of them go fishing at a lake 20 miles from home. Exactly 8 years ago, Victor was three times as old as Rosa.
problems.ask: How old is Victor now, in years?
steps: Let Rosa's age now be x, so Victor is 2x.
Move the x terms to one side: x = 24 − 8 = 16.
So Victor is 2 × 16 = 32 years old now. Check: 8 years ago, 24 = 3 × 8.

bonus.stem: The bell in the town hall tower rings once for each hour, with the rings evenly spaced. Omar times it at 3 o'clock: 2 seconds pass from the first ring to the last.
bonus.ask: How many seconds does it take from the first ring to the last at 6 o'clock?
steps: 3 rings have only 2 gaps between them, so each gap is 2 ÷ 2 = 1 second.

problems.stem: A set of mixing bowls at the local store is marked $37. Caleb decides to buy it, and 6% sales tax is added at checkout.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the set of mixing bowls, including tax?

problems.stem: Silas is reseeding a rectangular lawn that measures 60 feet by 20 feet. A bag of grass seed covers 500 square feet, and the lawn gets about 5 hours of sun a day. Seed is sold only in whole bags.
problems.ask: How many bags of seed must Silas buy to cover the whole lawn?
steps: 2 bags cover 2 × 500 = 1,000 square feet, which is not enough.
3 bags cover 1,500 square feet, so Silas needs 3 bags.

problems.stem: Maya and two friends went out for dinner and waited 25 minutes for a table. They ordered three entrées at $14 each and one appetizer to share for $12. Sales tax is 10%, and they added a 15% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the dinner, including tax and tip?
steps: Tip: 10% of $54 is $5.40, plus half of that, $2.70, gives $8.10.

problems.stem: Kofi is signing up for pottery classes at a local studio, which offers the two options in the table. Each class lasts 90 minutes.
problems.ask: How many classes in a month would make the two options cost exactly the same?
steps: Drop-in costs $5 more per class, so each class closes the gap by $5.
Check: $40 + 8 × $12 = $136 and $0 + 8 × $17 = $136, so the answer is 8 classes.

problems.stem: Sam's booth at the town festival has 20 rubber ducks floating in a pool. A player pays $5, picks one duck at random, and wins the prize marked underneath; the duck then goes back in. The table shows the prizes. The festival lasts 8 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the booth make per game after paying out prizes?
steps: If each duck came up once, the prizes would total 2 × $20 + 5 × $1 = $45.
The booth keeps $5 − $2.25 = $2.75 per game on average.

bonus.stem: At Rosa's birthday party, every person there, Rosa included, shook hands with every other person exactly once. Rosa kept track and counted 171 handshakes in all.
bonus.ask: How many people were at the party, counting Rosa?
steps: With n people, the count is n × (n − 1) ÷ 2, so n × (n − 1) ÷ 2 = 171.
Look for two numbers in a row that multiply to 342: 19 × 18 = 342, so n = 19.

problems.stem: Hana is saving for a used guitar that costs $145. She already has $75 saved and puts away $10 each week.
problems.ask: How many more weeks will it take Hana to have exactly enough?

problems.stem: Dev is picking up bagels for the team's 9:30 a.m. meeting. The bakery sells bagels in packs of 4 for $2.50, or one at a time for $0.85 each. 23 people are coming, and Dev wants at least one bagel per person. Leftovers are fine, but he can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Dev can spend?
steps: 23 ÷ 4 = 5 full packs, with 3 people left over.

problems.stem: Caleb's swim team held a car wash to raise money. They charged $7 for each car and $9 for each truck or SUV. Over six hours on Saturday, they washed 216 vehicles and collected $1,624.
problems.ask: How many cars did the team wash?
steps: If all 216 were cars, the total would be 216 × $7 = $1,512.
The actual total is $1,624 − $1,512 = $112 more than that.
Each truck or SUV brings in $2 more than each car, so trucks and SUVs: $112 ÷ $2 = 56.

problems.stem: A rectangular park near Ava's apartment is 480 meters long and 200 meters wide. Ava usually walks along two edges to get from one corner to the opposite corner. Today she cuts straight across the grass on the diagonal instead. The park has 14 benches.
problems.ask: How many meters shorter is the diagonal route than the route along the two edges?
steps: Shrink the numbers first: 480 = 40 × 12 and 200 = 40 × 5. Since 12² + 5² = 144 + 25 = 169 = 13², the diagonal is 40 × 13 = 520 meters.

problems.stem: Theo is organizing a volleyball league with 12 teams this season. Every team will play every other team exactly twice during the regular season. Each game takes about 30 minutes.
problems.ask: How many games will be played in the regular season?
steps: Each game is a pair of teams. Each of the 12 teams pairs with 11 others: 12 × 11 = 132.
That counts every pair twice, so divide by 2: 132 ÷ 2 = 66 pairs.

problems.stem: A farm stand sells a 3-pound bag of apples for $8.25. Owen wants 10 pounds for pies, and the stand will weigh out any amount at the same price per pound.
problems.ask: How much will 10 pounds of apples cost?

problems.stem: Malik is stocking up at a garden center for his spring planting. The prices, with tax included, are in the table. The garden center is 3 miles from his house. Malik orders two watering cans, two seed packets, and four tomato plants.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Malik's order?

problems.stem: Dev wants to buy an electric bike at a bike shop. The price is $1,191 if he pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $150 down, then 6 monthly payments of $186. Its battery can go about 30 miles on one charge.
problems.ask: How much more would Dev pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Jamal deposited $800 in a savings account that earns 6% interest, compounded once a year. He won't add or take out any money. The bank requires a $25 minimum balance.
problems.ask: How much will be in the account after 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 6% of $800 is $48, so the value goes to $800 + $48 = $848.

problems.stem: Mateo mixed 12 liters of liquid plant food that is 25% concentrate. The label says seedlings need a mix that is only 15% concentrate, so he will dilute it with water. He is growing six trays of seedlings.
problems.ask: How many liters of water should Mateo add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 15% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 25/15 = 5/3: 12 × 5/3 = 20 liters.

problems.stem: Paige's running club timed its members in a 5-kilometer race. The 23 runners in the morning group averaged 39 minutes, and the 7 runners in the evening group averaged 24 minutes. The course had five water stations.
problems.ask: What was the average time for all the runners in both groups, in minutes?

problems.stem: Nadia, who is 6 feet tall, stands on level ground and notices that her shadow is 4 feet long. At the same moment, the shadow of a nearby flagpole is 17 feet long. The flagpole was put up 50 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the flagpole, in feet?
steps: The sun hits both at the same angle, so height ÷ shadow is the same for the flagpole and Nadia: 6 ÷ 4.

problems.stem: At 9:45 a.m., Hugo started a volunteer shift at the library. The shift ended at 1:05 p.m., and he walked home.
problems.ask: How many minutes long was the shift?
steps: From 9:45 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 15 minutes.
From 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. is 3 hours, or 180 minutes.
From 1:00 p.m. to 1:05 p.m. is 5 minutes.

problems.stem: Dmitri bowls in a league with 19 teams. So far this season he has bowled three games, scoring 126, 110, and 153. He wants his average after the next game to be exactly 140.
problems.ask: What score does Dmitri need in the next game?
steps: An average of 140 over 4 games means a total of 140 × 4 = 560.

problems.stem: Tess is comparing three sizes of the same cereal, shown in the table. She eats about three ounces each morning.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Jordan started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 3 miles per hour. Caleb started running from the same spot 15 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 8 miles per hour. The path is 6 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Caleb catch up to Jordan?
steps: Head start: in 15 minutes (1/4 hour), Jordan covers 3 × 1/4 = 0.75 miles.
Time to close the gap: 0.75 ÷ 5 = 3/20 hour = 9 minutes.

problems.stem: A café asked 64 regular customers which drinks they had ordered in the past month. The results are in the table. The "Iced coffee" and "Hot tea" counts include the customers who ordered both drinks. The café has 17 tables.
problems.ask: How many of the 64 customers ordered neither drink?

problems.stem: Grace spots a pair of hiking boots with a price tag of $64. A sign on the rack says the price will be 25% off at the register.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the pair of hiking boots, before tax?

problems.stem: A smoothie recipe makes 4 servings and calls for 1/2 cup of plain yogurt. Sofia is making 12 servings for her soccer team after practice. The yogurt was on sale for $3.50 a tub.
problems.ask: If she scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of yogurt will she need?

problems.stem: Theo bought a winter coat at a department store during a 20%-off sale, and he also used a $20 coupon. The register took 20% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. The sale lasted three days. Before tax, Theo paid $112.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the coat?
steps: $132 is what was left after 20% off, so it is 80% of the original price.

problems.stem: Ruth's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 90 minutes.
problems.ask: What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
steps: With 33 values in order, the median is the 17th value.
Running totals: through 0: 2, through 1: 11, through 2: 16, through 3: 22, through 4: 30, through 5: 33.
The 17th value falls in the row for 3 goals, so the median is 3 goals.

problems.stem: Ingrid snaps a photo of the clock tower in the town square at exactly 9:29. The tower is 69 feet tall. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 29 × 6 = 174 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 9 × 30 + 29 × 0.5 = 284.5 degrees past the 12.
That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 110.5 degrees.

problems.stem: Dev bowled four games at his league night on Saturday. His scores were 146, 154, 161, and 179.
problems.ask: What was Dev's average score for the four games?

problems.stem: Lucia works at a garden center for $24 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times her regular rate. Her shifts start at 7:00 each morning. Last week she worked 48 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Lucia earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $24 = $36 an hour, for 48 − 40 = 8 hours.

problems.stem: Dmitri is painting the four walls of his dining room, which is 14 feet long, 9 feet wide and 10 feet high. He wants two coats on every wall. One gallon of paint covers 400 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $28 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Dmitri need to buy?
steps: 920 ÷ 400 = 2.3, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

problems.stem: Mateo and Jamal are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Mateo could paint it in 5 hours, and Jamal could paint it in 20 hours. The fence is 120 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Mateo does 1/5 of the fence and Jamal does 1/20.
Together: 1/5 + 1/20 = 4/20 + 1/20 = 5/20 = 1/4 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: Wes empties the cup holder in his car and finds nothing but quarters and nickels. There are 16 coins in all, worth $2.20 together. He has had the car for 6 years.
problems.ask: How many quarters are in the cup holder?
steps: Suppose all 16 were nickels: 16 × 5 cents = 80 cents.
The real total is 220 cents, which is 220 cents − 80 cents = 140 cents more.
Each quarter adds 20 cents more than a nickel, so there are 140 cents ÷ 20 cents = 7 quarters.

problems.stem: Luis is running a lemonade stand. He makes five pitchers of lemonade, and each pitcher holds 12 cups. There are 4 cups in a quart.
problems.ask: How many quarts of lemonade does Luis make?
steps: There are 4 cups in a quart: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 quarts.

problems.stem: A store is taking 25% off every camping tent, and Hana finds one with a regular price of $80. She also has a member coupon that takes 10% off the already reduced price. The sale price is good for 10 more days.
problems.ask: How much does Hana pay for the camping tent, before tax?
steps: 25% of $80 is $20, so the sale price is $80 − $20 = $60.
The extra 10% comes off $60, not the original price: 10% of $60 is $6.

problems.stem: Ezra surveyed the students in his grade about their favorite school lunch. Each student picked exactly one option, and the table shows the results. He collected the answers over four days.
problems.ask: What percent of the students surveyed chose "Pizza"?

problems.stem: Malik takes a 250-milligram dose of a medicine at 7:30 a.m. with a glass of water. The amount of the medicine in the body drops by half every 8 hours.
problems.ask: How many milligrams of the medicine are left in his body 32 hours after the dose?

problems.stem: In a board game, Lucia's piece is stuck in the jail space. Under the house rules, she rolls a standard six-sided die two times, and she escapes if any roll is a 5 or a 6. The board has 40 spaces in all.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Lucia escapes?
steps: Work with the opposite: one roll is not a 5 or a 6 with probability 4/6 = 2/3.

problems.stem: Luis and two coworkers stop at a diner for breakfast, and Luis offers to pay. The check is $34.40. He plans to add a 20% tip on the full check.
problems.ask: How much is the tip?

problems.stem: Chloe is baking a cake for a birthday party, and it must be frosted by 1:30 p.m. when the guests arrive. Baking takes 35 minutes, cooling takes 45 minutes, and frosting takes 20 minutes, one after another. The cake will feed 15 people. It is 11:45 a.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Chloe wait before starting?
steps: From 11:45 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. is 105 minutes.

problems.stem: Lena's home internet bill used to be $95 a month. After she upgraded her plan, the monthly bill became $114. The new plan has a download speed of 200 megabits per second.
problems.ask: By what percent did Lena's monthly internet bill increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $19 ÷ $95 = 1/5 = 0.2.
As a percent, that is an increase of 20%.

problems.stem: Andre has a recipe for an 8-inch round cake, but he wants to bake it in a 10-inch round pan instead, filled to the same depth. The oven is set to 350 degrees.
problems.ask: How many times the original recipe should Andre make to fill the bigger pan?

problems.stem: Priya and Lucia are 62 miles apart on the same highway and drive toward each other to meet for dinner. Priya drives at 65 miles per hour, and Lucia drives at 55 miles per hour. They leave at the same time. Priya's car holds 15 gallons of gas.
problems.ask: How many minutes after they leave do they meet?
steps: The gap closes at 65 + 55 = 120 miles per hour.

problems.stem: Aiyana and five coworkers chip in for a retirement gift: a gift card worth $50 and a cake that costs $31. They split the cost evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Aiyana plus five others makes 6 people.

problems.stem: Sam is planning a road trip to the coast with a paper map. On the map, 1 inch represents 50 miles. The route has two straight stretches: the first measures 2 3/4 inches, and the second measures 3 inches. He plans to leave at 5 in the morning.
problems.ask: How many miles long is the route?

problems.stem: Ruth's chemistry grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and her average so far. There are 29 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Ruth need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 80?
steps: To finish at 80, the final must add 80 − 51.6 = 28.4 points.
The final is worth 40%, so the score needed is 28.4 ÷ 0.4 = 71.

problems.stem: Theo rode his bike 6 miles to a lake, mostly uphill, averaging 8 miles per hour. He rode home the same way, mostly downhill, at 24 miles per hour. He packed two bottles of water for the ride.
problems.ask: What was Theo's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 12 ÷ 1 = 12 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Four friends, including Rosa and Ezra, have 4 seats together in one row at the movies. Rosa and Ezra both talk during movies, so the group agrees they won't sit side by side. The movie runs 105 minutes.
problems.ask: In how many different ways can the 4 friends fill the 4 seats?
steps: Orders with them together: glue them into a block, 3 × 2 × 1 = 6, times 2 for their order = 12.

bonus.stem: Today is Tuesday. Zoe's new gym pass starts tomorrow and is good for 31 days in a row. Her favorite spin class meets once a week, every Wednesday.
bonus.ask: How many Wednesday spin classes fall within the 31 days of her pass?
steps: Each full week has exactly one Wednesday: 4.
The 3 extra days fall on the same weekdays as the first 3: Wednesday through Friday, which includes one more Wednesday.

problems.stem: Wes is building a rectangular pen for his chickens that measures 26 feet by 15 feet. He'll fence all four sides.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Wes need?
steps: One length plus one width: 26 + 15 = 41 feet.
Going all the way around doubles that: 2 × 41 = 82 feet.

problems.stem: Tess bikes to work. She rides 12 miles on a bike path at a steady 12 miles per hour, then 4 miles through city streets at a steady 8 miles per hour. Her office is on the fourth floor.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 12 ÷ 12 = 1 hour, which is 60 minutes.
Second part: 4 ÷ 8 = 1/2 hour, which is 30 minutes.

problems.stem: Arjun built a rectangular backyard pond that is 12 feet long, 5 feet wide and 2 feet deep, and he stocked it with twelve goldfish. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the pond hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Lena is mixing concrete for a garden path that is 24 feet long. Her mix uses cement, sand and gravel in the ratio 2:3:2 by volume. She needs 63 buckets of mix in all.
problems.ask: How many more buckets of sand than cement does Lena need?
steps: Sand minus cement: 3 − 2 = 1 part, and 1 × 9 = 9 buckets.

problems.stem: Jade is signing up for pottery classes at a local studio, which offers the two options in the table. Each class lasts 90 minutes.
problems.ask: How many classes in a month would make the two options cost exactly the same?
steps: Drop-in costs $9 more per class, so each class closes the gap by $9.
Check: $90 + 10 × $14 = $230 and $0 + 10 × $23 = $230, so the answer is 10 classes.

problems.stem: In March, the hardware store where Ezra works raised the price of a garden hose by 10%. In June, the store put it on sale for 30% off that new price. Ezra has worked at the store for 15 months.
problems.ask: By what percent is the June price lower than the original price?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
77 is 23 below 100, so it is 23% lower.

problems.stem: Nadia keeps a tin of cookies on her desk. It holds 8 chocolate chip cookies and 7 oatmeal cookies, all the same size. The tin was a gift from her neighbor 4 years ago. Without looking, she takes out two cookies, one after the other, and doesn't put either back.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both cookies are the same kind?

problems.stem: Hugo is covering a playroom floor with square foam mats that are 24 inches on each side. The room is a rectangle 12 feet long and 10 feet wide, and the mats fit exactly.
problems.ask: How many mats does Hugo need?
steps: 24 inches is 2 feet. Along the length: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 mats.

problems.stem: On a trip to Mexico, Grace exchanges money at a rate of 20 pesos per U.S. dollar. At an outdoor market, she buys a woven blanket for 320 pesos and a pair of sandals for 360 pesos. She has nine days left on the trip.
problems.ask: How much did Grace spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Dev and four friends went out for dinner and waited 25 minutes for a table. They ordered five entrées at $17 each and one appetizer to share for $15. Sales tax is 10%, and they added a 15% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the dinner, including tax and tip?
steps: Tip: 10% of $100 is $10, plus half of that, $5, gives $15.

problems.stem: Aiyana teaches two sections of algebra. On Friday's test, the 25 students in her first-period class averaged 81 points, and the 35 students in her fourth-period class averaged 63 points. The test had 20 questions.
problems.ask: What was the average score for all of the students in both classes together, in points?

problems.stem: Sofia is three times as old as her daughter, Esme. Every summer the two of them go fishing at a lake 23 miles from home. In 15 years, Sofia will be twice as old as Esme.
problems.ask: How old is Sofia now, in years?
steps: Let Esme's age now be x, so Sofia is 3x.
Subtract 2x and 15 from both sides: x = 30 − 15 = 15.
So Sofia is 3 × 15 = 45 years old now. Check: in 15 years, 60 = 2 × 30.

problems.stem: Grace shops at the farmers market on Saturday morning. She buys a jar of honey for $6.50, a loaf of sourdough for $6.25, and a pint of blueberries for $4.25. There's no sales tax, and she pays with a $20 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Grace get back?

problems.stem: Jade is putting laminate flooring in a rectangular bedroom that measures 14 feet by 13 feet. Each box of flooring covers 25 square feet and weighs 36 pounds. The store sells only whole boxes.
problems.ask: Ignoring waste, how many boxes does Jade need to buy?
steps: 7 boxes cover 7 × 25 = 175 square feet, which is not enough.
8 boxes cover 200 square feet, so Jade needs 8 boxes.

problems.stem: Sofia helped run a pancake breakfast at the fire station. Adult plates cost $12 and kids' plates cost $7. They served 70 plates and took in $590, with twelve volunteers working the griddles.
problems.ask: How many kids' plates did they serve?
steps: If all 70 were kids' plates, the total would be 70 × $7 = $490.
The actual total is $590 − $490 = $100 more than that.
Each adult plate brings in $5 more than each kids' plate, so adult plates: $100 ÷ $5 = 20.

problems.stem: Jordan mixed 8 cups of fruit punch that is 40% juice for a party. It tastes too sweet, so he wants to add water until the punch is only 20% juice. Fifteen guests are coming.
problems.ask: How many cups of water should Jordan add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 20% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 40/20 = 2: 8 × 2 = 16 cups.

problems.stem: Diego is saving for a new bike. He puts $11 in a jar the first week, and every week after that he puts in $1.50 more than the week before. He started the plan on his 14th birthday.
problems.ask: How much will Diego have saved in all after 16 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 16, week 2 with week 15, and so on: each pair adds to $11 + $33.50 = $44.50.

problems.stem: Nico is shopping for a new toaster and finds one priced at $46. The sales tax where he lives is 5%, added at the register.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the toaster, including tax?
steps: 10% of $46 is $4.60, so 5% is half of that: $2.30.

problems.stem: Noor is driving 160 miles to a family reunion, where she'll catch a ride home with family. Her car gets 40 miles per gallon, and gas costs $4.10 per gallon. Her car's tank holds 14 gallons.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the drive?

problems.stem: Elena bought a used car for $19,000. Her mechanic estimates that the car will lose 20% of its value each year, based on what it is worth at the start of that year. The car gets about 24 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: Using that estimate, what will the car be worth after 2 years?

problems.stem: June is building a wooden garden gate shaped like a rectangle, 60 inches wide and 63 inches tall. To keep it from sagging, she will nail a straight brace from one corner to the opposite corner. The gate will hang on two hinges.
problems.ask: How long must the brace be, in inches?
steps: The brace is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs equal to the width and height.

problems.stem: Sam runs a prize wheel at the school fair. The wheel has 10 equal sections, each equally likely to land on top, and a spin costs $5. The table shows what the sections pay. The fair runs for 7 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the prize wheel make per spin after paying out prizes?
steps: If each section came up once, the prizes would total 2 × $5 + 3 × $3 = $19.
The booth keeps $5 − $1.90 = $3.10 per spin on average.

problems.stem: At the hardware store, 2 feet of rope costs $1.60. Priya needs 8 feet to hang a porch swing, and the store cuts rope to any length at the same price per foot.
problems.ask: How much will 8 feet of rope cost?

problems.stem: Tess is stocking up at a garden center for her spring planting. The prices, with tax included, are in the table. The garden center is 3 miles from her house. Tess orders two bags of potting soil, two flower pots, and four watering cans.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Tess's order?

problems.stem: Esme wants to buy an electric bike at a bike shop. The price is $1,290 if she pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $150 down, then 6 monthly payments of $215. Its battery can go about 40 miles on one charge.
problems.ask: How much more would Esme pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Algae is spreading across the pond on Maya's farm. Right now it covers 6 square feet, and the area it covers doubles every 4 days. The pond is about 4 feet deep.
problems.ask: If it keeps doubling at this rate, how many square feet will the algae cover 20 days from now?

problems.stem: Theo is organizing a chess league with 9 players this season. Every player will play every other player exactly twice during the regular season. Each match takes about 50 minutes.
problems.ask: How many matches will be played in the regular season?
steps: Each match is a pair of players. Each of the 9 players pairs with 8 others: 9 × 8 = 72.
That counts every pair twice, so divide by 2: 72 ÷ 2 = 36 pairs.

problems.stem: Noor left home at 9:55 a.m. to drive to a lake cabin. She made no stops, and the dashboard clock read 12:30 p.m. when she pulled into the cabin's driveway.
problems.ask: How many minutes did the drive take?
steps: From 9:55 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 5 minutes.
From 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. is 2 hours, or 120 minutes.
From 12:00 p.m. to 12:30 p.m. is 30 minutes.

problems.stem: Hana is picking up bagels for the team's 8 a.m. meeting. The bakery sells bagels in packs of 6 for $6, or one at a time for $1.25 each. 21 people are coming, and Hana wants at least one bagel per person. Leftovers are fine, but she can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Hana can spend?
steps: 21 ÷ 6 = 3 full packs, with 3 people left over.

problems.stem: Paige is painting the four walls of her dining room, which is 10 feet long, 8 feet wide and 10 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. The door and windows take up 60 square feet that won't be painted. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $28 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Paige need to buy?
steps: Minus the door and windows: 360 − 60 = 300 square feet.
600 ÷ 350 ≈ 1.7, which is more than 1, so round up to 2 gallons.

problems.stem: Tess's class kept track of how many books each student read over winter break, and the table shows the results. The school library lets each student borrow up to eight books at a time.
problems.ask: What is the median number of books read over the break?
steps: With 30 values in order, the median is the average of the 15th and 16th values.
Running totals: through 0: 2, through 1: 9, through 2: 14, through 3: 19, through 4: 22, through 5: 30.
Both fall in the row for 3 books, so the median is 3 books.

problems.stem: Yuki surveyed all 75 students in her grade about pets at home. The results are in the table. The "Has a dog" and "Has a cat" counts include the students who have both a dog and a cat. She handed out the surveys during a 13-minute homeroom.
problems.ask: How many students have both a dog and a cat?
steps: So the extra count is the 'both' group: 47 − 39 = 8.

problems.stem: The store is taking 10% off everything this week, including the board game Lucia has had her eye on. Its regular price is $35.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the board game, before tax?

problems.stem: Dev bowls in a league with 16 teams. So far this season he has bowled four games, scoring 172, 184, 168, and 186. He wants his average after the next game to be exactly 180.
problems.ask: What score does Dev need in the next game?
steps: An average of 180 over 5 games means a total of 180 × 5 = 900.

problems.stem: Lena bought a set of wireless headphones at an electronics store during a 50%-off sale, and she also used a $15 coupon. The register took 50% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. The headphones run about 20 hours on a full charge. Before tax, Lena paid $76.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the headphones?
steps: $91 is what was left after 50% off, so it is 50% of the original price.

problems.stem: Kenji started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 4 miles per hour. Ravi started running from the same spot 12 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 6 miles per hour. The path is 5 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Ravi catch up to Kenji?
steps: Head start: in 12 minutes (1/5 hour), Kenji covers 4 × 1/5 = 0.8 miles.
Time to close the gap: 0.8 ÷ 2 = 2/5 hour = 24 minutes.

problems.stem: Jamal, who is 6 feet tall, stands on level ground and notices that his shadow is 4 feet long. At the same moment, the shadow of a nearby oak tree is 11 feet long. The tree was planted about 40 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the oak tree, in feet?
steps: The sun hits both at the same angle, so height ÷ shadow is the same for the oak tree and Jamal: 6 ÷ 4.
Height of the oak tree = 11 × 6 ÷ 4 = 66 ÷ 4 = 16.5 feet.

problems.stem: Ruth is reading a 310-page novel for her book club and has already read 170 pages. She plans to read 20 pages each day until she finishes.
problems.ask: How many more days will it take to finish the book?
