problems.stem: Mei's pancake recipe makes 8 pancakes and calls for 2/3 cup of flour. She is making 20 pancakes for a family brunch. The recipe says to cook each pancake for 2 minutes per side.
problems.ask: If she scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of flour will she need?

problems.stem: Jamal surveyed the students in his grade about their favorite school lunch. Each student picked exactly one option, and the table shows the results. He collected the answers over four days.
problems.ask: What percent of the students surveyed did not choose "Pasta"?

problems.stem: Noor is stocking up on peanut butter and compares the three jar sizes in the table. She goes through about two jars a month.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Tess has a recipe for an 8-inch round cake, but she wants to bake it in a 10-inch round pan instead, filled to the same depth. The oven is set to 325 degrees.
problems.ask: How many times the original recipe should Tess make to fill the bigger pan?

problems.stem: In March, the hardware store where June works cut the price of a cordless drill by 20%. In June, the store raised that new price by 40%. June has worked at the store for 8 months.
problems.ask: By what percent is the June price higher than the original price?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
112 is 12 above 100, so it is 12% higher.

problems.stem: In a board game, Grace's piece is stuck in the jail space. Under the house rules, she rolls a standard six-sided die two times, and she escapes if any roll is a 6. The board has 36 spaces in all.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Grace escapes?
steps: Work with the opposite: one roll is not a 6 with probability 5/6.

problems.stem: Priya is tracking how long she practices piano. From Monday to Friday, she practiced 49, 44, 55, 34, and 33 minutes.
problems.ask: What was her average practice time per day, in minutes?

problems.stem: June works at a garden center for $20 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times her regular rate. She has worked there for 7 years. Last week she worked 45 hours.
problems.ask: How much did June earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $20 = $30 an hour, for 45 − 40 = 5 hours.

problems.stem: Yuki buys a monthly bus pass. Last year the pass cost $50, and this year the transit agency raised the price to $62.50. She rides the bus about 23 days a month.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bus pass increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $12.50 ÷ $50 = 1/4 = 0.25.
As a percent, that is an increase of 25%.

problems.stem: Hana and Sam are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Hana could paint it in 4 hours, and Sam could paint it in 6 hours. The fence is 80 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Hana does 1/4 of the fence and Sam does 1/6.
Together: 1/4 + 1/6 = 3/12 + 2/12 = 5/12 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: The clock at the train station has a face 6 feet across. While Silas waits on the platform, it reads 3:44. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 44 × 6 = 264 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 3 × 30 + 44 × 0.5 = 112 degrees past the 12.
That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 152 degrees.

problems.stem: Victor spends a rainy Saturday watching a baking show. He watches three episodes, and each one is 40 minutes long.
problems.ask: How many hours of the show does Victor watch?
steps: There are 60 minutes in an hour: 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours.

problems.stem: A store is taking 40% off every pair of running shoes, and Yuki finds one with a regular price of $130. She also has a member coupon that takes 20% off the already reduced price. The store is 5 miles from her home.
problems.ask: How much does Yuki pay for the pair of running shoes, before tax?
steps: 40% of $130 is $52, so the sale price is $130 − $52 = $78.
The extra 20% comes off $78, not the original price: 20% of $78 is $15.60.

problems.stem: Ben's world history grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and his average so far. There are 26 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Ben need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 85?
steps: To finish at 85, the final must add 85 − 55.6 = 29.4 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 29.4 ÷ 0.3 = 98.

problems.stem: Esme paddled a kayak 9 miles upstream at 2 miles per hour, then turned around and paddled the same 9 miles back downstream at 6 miles per hour. Her kayak is 14 feet long.
problems.ask: What was Esme's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 18 ÷ 6 = 3 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Hana empties the cup holder in her car and finds nothing but quarters and dimes. There are 28 coins in all, worth $4.30 together. She has had the car for 6 years.
problems.ask: How many dimes are in the cup holder?
steps: Suppose all 28 were dimes: 28 × 10 cents = 280 cents.
The real total is 430 cents, which is 430 cents − 280 cents = 150 cents more.
Each quarter adds 15 cents more than a dime, so there are 150 cents ÷ 15 cents = 10 quarters (check: 10 × 15 cents = 150 cents).

bonus.stem: A hallway at Rosa's school has 112 closed lockers, numbered 1 to 112. Then 112 students walk by one at a time. Student 1 opens every locker. Student 2 switches every 2nd locker (closing it if open, opening it if closed), student 3 switches every 3rd locker, and so on, until student 112 switches only locker 112.
bonus.ask: How many lockers are open at the end?
steps: A locker is switched once for each number that divides it (locker 12: by 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12).
Divisors come in pairs (1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4), so most lockers are switched an even number of times and end closed.
Only perfect squares have an odd number of divisors, because one pair repeats (6 × 6 = 36).
Perfect squares up to 112: 1, 4, 9, …, 100, which is 10 lockers open.

problems.stem: Amara takes her parents out for a birthday lunch. The bill comes to $57 before the tip, and she wants to leave a 15% tip on that amount.
problems.ask: How much is the tip?

problems.stem: Diego is making lasagna for 11 guests and wants it ready to serve at 6:30 p.m. sharp. Assembling it takes 20 minutes, baking takes 45 minutes, and it must rest 10 minutes before serving. These steps happen one after another. It is 5:05 p.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Diego wait before starting?
steps: From 5:05 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. is 85 minutes.

problems.stem: Lena bought a rectangular glass aquarium that is 48 inches long, 12 inches wide and 24 inches tall. She plans to keep six small fish in it. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the aquarium hold when completely full?
steps: Convert to feet (÷ 12): 48 in = 4 ft, 12 in = 1 ft, 24 in = 2 ft.

problems.stem: Grace needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. She plans to pick up the car at 8 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $32 more up front.
Company B costs $0.10 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.10.

problems.stem: Kofi and Owen are 60 miles apart on the same highway and drive toward each other to meet for dinner. Kofi drives at 40 miles per hour, and Owen drives at 50 miles per hour. They leave at the same time. Kofi's car holds 15 gallons of gas.
problems.ask: How many minutes after they leave do they meet?
steps: The gap closes at 40 + 50 = 90 miles per hour.

bonus.stem: Malik manages an apartment building whose mailboxes are numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on with no gaps. Each number is made of stick-on digits, one sticker per digit, and the building used 876 digit stickers in all.
bonus.ask: How many mailboxes does the building have?
steps: Mailboxes 1–9 use 9 digits and mailboxes 10–99 use 90 × 2 = 180, so 189 digits through mailbox 99.
Digits left: 876 − 189 = 687. Each mailbox from 100 on uses 3: 687 ÷ 3 = 229 mailboxes.
Those are mailboxes 100 through 328, so there are 328 mailboxes.

problems.stem: Kenji is building a rectangular pen for his chickens that measures 20 feet by 7 feet. One 20-foot side runs along the house wall, so it needs no fence.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Kenji need?
steps: Fence the other 20-foot side and both 7-foot sides.

problems.stem: Rosa is driving to her grandparents' farm. She drives 90 miles on the highway at a steady 45 miles per hour, then 24 miles on country roads at a steady 30 miles per hour. The farm has 17 acres of corn.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 90 ÷ 45 = 2 hours, which is 120 minutes.
Second part: 24 ÷ 30 = 4/5 hour, which is 48 minutes.

problems.stem: Malik is making trail mix for a weekend hike. His recipe mixes peanuts, raisins and chocolate chips in the ratio 3:3:4 by weight. He wants 100 ounces of trail mix in all, which he'll pack into six bags.
problems.ask: How many more ounces of chocolate chips than raisins will the mix contain?
steps: Chocolate chips minus raisins: 4 − 3 = 1 part, and 1 × 10 = 10 ounces.

problems.stem: Mei teaches two sections of algebra. On Friday's test, the 24 students in her first-period class averaged 68 points, and the 6 students in her fourth-period class averaged 73 points. The test had 25 questions.
problems.ask: What was the average score for all of the students in both classes together, in points?

problems.stem: Nico, Hugo and three of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Nico and Hugo keep making each other laugh, so they can't stand side by side. The photographer charges $75 for the session.
problems.ask: In how many different orders can the 5 of them line up?
steps: Orders with them together: glue them into a block, 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24, times 2 for their order = 48.

problems.stem: Elena is tiling a small laundry room floor that measures 9 feet by 3 feet. She picked square tiles that are 6 inches on each side, and they fit exactly with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many tiles does Elena need?
steps: 6 inches is half a foot, so 2 tiles fit in each foot.
Along the length: 9 × 2 = 18. Along the width: 3 × 2 = 6.

problems.stem: On a trip to Mexico, Ravi exchanges money at a rate of 20 pesos per U.S. dollar. At an outdoor market, he buys a woven blanket for 750 pesos and a pair of sandals for 540 pesos. He has nine days left on the trip.
problems.ask: How much did Ravi spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Diego and three friends went out for dinner and waited 20 minutes for a table. They ordered four entrées at $12 each and one appetizer to share for $11. Sales tax is 5%, and they added a 20% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the dinner, including tax and tip?

problems.stem: Raul mixed 10 liters of liquid plant food that is 15% concentrate. The label says seedlings need a mix that is only 10% concentrate, so he will dilute it with water. He is growing six trays of seedlings.
problems.ask: How many liters of water should Raul add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 10% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 15/10 = 3/2: 10 × 3/2 = 15 liters.

problems.stem: Caleb keeps a tin of cookies on his desk. It holds 4 chocolate chip cookies and 8 oatmeal cookies, all the same size. The tin was a gift from his neighbor 7 years ago. Without looking, he takes out two cookies, one after the other, and doesn't put either back.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both cookies are the same kind?

bonus.stem: Andre buys a sandwich and a bottle of juice at a deli for $7.50 in total. The sandwich costs exactly $6 more than the bottle of juice.
bonus.ask: How much does the bottle of juice cost?
steps: Call the price of the bottle of juice x, so the sandwich costs x + $6.
x = $1.50 ÷ 2 = $0.75 for the bottle of juice.

problems.stem: Sam and three friends go bowling. The lanes cost $42 for the night, and shoe rentals add $15. They split the total evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Sam plus three others makes 4 people.

problems.stem: Luis is mapping out a bike ride. On the town's trail map, 1 inch stands for 4 miles. The ride follows the river trail for 2 1/4 inches on the map, then the park loop for 3/4 inch. The trail map shows 10 drinking fountains.
problems.ask: How many miles long is the ride?

problems.stem: Owen helped run a pancake breakfast at the fire station. Adult plates cost $8 and kids' plates cost $6. They served 183 plates and took in $1,382, with twelve volunteers working the griddles.
problems.ask: How many kids' plates did they serve?
steps: If all 183 were kids' plates, the total would be 183 × $6 = $1,098.
The actual total is $1,382 − $1,098 = $284 more than that.
Each adult plate brings in $2 more than each kids' plate, so adult plates: $284 ÷ $2 = 142.

problems.stem: Mateo leans a 25-foot ladder against the side of his house to clean the gutters. For safety, the bottom of the ladder sits 7 feet out from the wall, on level ground. The ladder is rated to hold 300 pounds.
problems.ask: How high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach, in feet?
steps: The wall, the ground and the ladder form a right triangle, with the ladder as the hypotenuse.

problems.stem: Jade is saving for a new bike. She puts $9 in a jar the first week, and every week after that she puts in $1 more than the week before. She started the plan on her 14th birthday.
problems.ask: How much will Jade have saved in all after 12 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 12, week 2 with week 11, and so on: each pair adds to $9 + $20 = $29.

bonus.stem: The town is planting trees along both sides of a straight path that is 168 feet long. On each side, there will be a tree every 8 feet, with a tree at both ends. Wes volunteers to dig the holes.
bonus.ask: How many trees will be planted in all?
steps: There is one more tree than gaps (count the end): 21 + 1 = 22.
Both sides of the path: 2 × 22 = 44 trees.

problems.stem: Victor is shopping for a new set of mixing bowls and finds one priced at $36. The sales tax where he lives is 8%, added at the register.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the set of mixing bowls, including tax?

problems.stem: Nadia is sealing a rectangular concrete patio that is 24 feet long and 19 feet wide. One gallon of sealer covers 50 square feet, and it needs 12 hours to dry. Sealer is sold only by the whole gallon.
problems.ask: How many gallons must Nadia buy to give the patio one coat?
steps: 9 gallons cover 9 × 50 = 450 square feet, which is not enough.
10 gallons cover 500 square feet, so Nadia needs 10 gallons.

problems.stem: Mateo deposited $6,000 in a savings account that earns 2% interest, compounded once a year. He won't add or take out any money. The bank requires a $50 minimum balance.
problems.ask: How much will be in the account after 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 2% of $6,000 is $120, so the value goes to $6,000 + $120 = $6,120.

problems.stem: Grace wants to buy a refrigerator at an appliance store. The price is $1,054 if she pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $100 down, then 24 monthly payments of $41. The store delivers for free within 15 miles.
problems.ask: How much more would Grace pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Felix asked every household on his street how many pets it has and recorded the results in the table. It took him two afternoons to reach everyone.
problems.ask: What is the median number of pets per household?
steps: With 19 values in order, the median is the 10th value.
Running totals: through 0: 9, through 1: 11, through 2: 13, through 3: 16, through 4: 19.
The 10th value falls in the row for 1 pet, so the median is 1 pets.

problems.stem: Malik and Ruth are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Malik could paint it in 10 hours, and Ruth could paint it in 30 hours. The fence is 80 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Malik does 1/10 of the fence and Ruth does 1/30.
Together: 1/10 + 1/30 = 3/30 + 1/30 = 4/30 = 2/15 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: Silas's booth at the town festival has 10 rubber ducks floating in a pool. A player pays $3, picks one duck at random, and wins the prize marked underneath; the duck then goes back in. The table shows the prizes. The festival lasts 8 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the booth make per game after paying out prizes?
steps: If each duck came up once, the prizes would total 2 × $5 + 5 × $1 = $15.
The booth keeps $3 − $1.50 = $1.50 per game on average.

problems.stem: Hana picks up school supplies before classes start. She buys a binder for $2.99, a pack of pens for $3.25, and a calculator for $8.95. There's no sales tax, and she pays with a $20 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Hana get back?

problems.stem: Carmen is buying snacks for her family at a baseball game. The snack bar's prices, tax included, are in the table. Their seats are in row 14. Carmen orders one pretzel, two lemonades, and two hot dogs.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Carmen's order?

problems.stem: Lena is painting the four walls of her bedroom, which is 14 feet long, 10 feet wide and 9 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. One gallon of paint covers 400 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $42 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Lena need to buy?
steps: 864 ÷ 400 ≈ 2.2, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

problems.stem: Caleb is growing bacteria for a biology lab. He starts a dish with 100 bacteria, and under these conditions the population doubles every 30 minutes. The dish is 15 centimeters across.
problems.ask: How many bacteria will be in the dish after 1.5 hours?

problems.stem: Owen is ten times as old as his granddaughter, Yuki. This spring they planted 20 tomato plants together. In 16 years, Owen will be four times as old as Yuki.
problems.ask: How old is Owen now, in years?
steps: Let Yuki's age now be x, so Owen is 10x.
Subtract 4x and 16 from both sides: 6x = 64 − 16 = 48, so x = 8.
So Owen is 10 × 8 = 80 years old now. Check: in 16 years, 96 = 4 × 24.

problems.stem: Noor's movie started at 2:05 p.m., and the credits began rolling at 4:10 p.m. as she headed for the exit.
problems.ask: How many minutes long was the movie, from start to credits?
steps: From 2:05 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 55 minutes.
From 3:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 1 hour, or 60 minutes.
From 4:00 p.m. to 4:10 p.m. is 10 minutes.

problems.stem: Dev is driving to his cousin's wedding, which is 210 miles from home, and then driving back. His car gets 30 miles per gallon, and gas costs $4.20 per gallon. He plans to leave at 7 in the morning.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the round trip?

problems.stem: June has been watching a mountain bike at a sporting-goods store. It was priced at $300, and this week the store marked it down to $225. The sale ends in 4 days.
problems.ask: By what percent was the price of the bike reduced?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $75 ÷ $300 = 1/4 = 0.25.
As a percent, that is a decrease of 25%.

problems.stem: Wes set out on his bike along the river trail, riding at a steady 9 miles per hour. Luis left from the same spot 10 minutes later and followed the same trail at a steady 12 miles per hour. The trail is 25 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting did Luis catch up to Wes?
steps: Head start: in 10 minutes (1/6 hour), Wes covers 9 × 1/6 = 1.5 miles.
Time to close the gap: 1.5 ÷ 3 = 1/2 hour = 30 minutes.

problems.stem: Carmen is organizing a chess league with 10 players this season. Every player will play every other player exactly once during the regular season. Each match takes about 30 minutes.
problems.ask: How many matches will be played in the regular season?
steps: Each match is a pair of players. Each of the 10 players pairs with 9 others: 10 × 9 = 90.
That counts every pair twice, so divide by 2: 90 ÷ 2 = 45 pairs.
Each pair plays once, so there are 45 matches.

bonus.stem: Hana is stacking soup cans into a flat, triangle-shaped display in a store window. The bottom row has 30 cans, each row has one fewer can than the row below it, and the top row has 3 cans.
bonus.ask: How many cans are in the display?
steps: Rows: from 3 up to 30 cans is 30 − 3 + 1 = 28 rows.
Pair the first and last rows, the second and second-to-last, and so on: each pair holds 3 + 30 = 33.

problems.stem: Arjun spots a pair of hiking boots with a price tag of $134. A sign on the rack says the price will be 25% off at the register.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the pair of hiking boots, before tax?

problems.stem: Nadia is picking up sandwiches for the 7:45 a.m. volunteer shift at the food bank. The deli sells sandwiches in packs of 6 for $4.50, or one at a time for $0.95 each. 21 volunteers are on the list, and Nadia wants at least one sandwich per person. Leftovers are fine, but she can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Nadia can spend?
steps: 21 ÷ 6 = 3 full packs, with 3 people left over.

problems.stem: Elena's company asked its employees how they usually get to work. Each person gave one answer, shown in the table. The office parking lot has 120 spaces.
problems.ask: What percent of the employees surveyed chose "Bus or train"?
steps: "Bus or train" was chosen by 48 employees.

problems.stem: Ingrid is ordering pizza for nine friends. The pizzeria sells round pizzas in two sizes: a 12-inch small and a 16-inch large, where the size is the diameter. Both have the same crust and toppings.
problems.ask: The large pizza has how many times the area of the small pizza?

problems.stem: At the school fair, a spinner has 10 equal sections, and three of them are marked Prize. Sam trades 4 tickets for three spins.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Sam lands on Prize at least once?
steps: Work with the opposite: one spin misses Prize with probability 7/10.

bonus.stem: Lucia's little cousin is racing up a set of 9 porch steps. Each jump takes her cousin up one, two or three steps, in any mix, and the last jump has to land exactly on the top step.
bonus.ask: How many different ways can the climb up all 9 steps go?
steps: To land on step k, the last move came from k − 1, k − 2 or k − 3, so ways(k) is the sum of the three before it.
Step 1: 1 way. Step 2: 2 ways. Step 3: 4 ways.
Keep adding three at a time: 1, 2, 4, 7, 13, 24, 44, 81, 149. So step 9 has 149 ways.

problems.stem: Sam is saving for a new bike that costs $90. He already has $30 saved and puts away $20 each week.
problems.ask: How many more weeks will it take Sam to have exactly enough?

problems.stem: Maya has taken three chemistry tests this term and scored 81, 86, and 77. There are 34 students in the class, and one test is left. She wants her average on all four tests to be exactly 82.
problems.ask: What score does Maya need on the last test?
steps: An average of 82 over 4 tests means a total of 82 × 4 = 328.

problems.stem: Ravi bought a set of wireless headphones at an electronics store during a 50%-off sale, and he also used a $20 coupon. The register took 50% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. The headphones run about 30 hours on a full charge. Before tax, Ravi paid $52.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the headphones?
steps: $72 is what was left after 50% off, so it is 50% of the original price.

problems.stem: In March, the hardware store where Ben works raised the price of a garden hose by 50%. In June, the store put it on sale for 10% off that new price. Ben has worked at the store for 8 months.
problems.ask: By what percent is the June price higher than the original price?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
135 is 35 above 100, so it is 35% higher.

problems.stem: Hana surveyed all 120 students in her grade about pets at home. The results are in the table. The "Has a dog" and "Has a cat" counts include the students who have both a dog and a cat. She handed out the surveys during a 9-minute homeroom.
problems.ask: How many students have both a dog and a cat?
steps: So the extra count is the 'both' group: 63 − 60 = 3.

problems.stem: Aiyana bowled four games at her league night on Saturday. Her scores were 122, 117, 107, and 98.
problems.ask: What was Aiyana's average score for the four games?

problems.stem: Dev works at a grocery store for $18 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times his regular rate. His shifts start at 7:00 each morning. Last week he worked 43 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Dev earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $18 = $27 an hour, for 43 − 40 = 3 hours.

problems.stem: The water trough at Silas's farm is a rectangular metal tank 4 feet long, 2.5 feet wide and 1.5 feet deep. It serves the four horses in the north pasture. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the trough hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Rosa rode her bike 36 miles to a lake, mostly uphill, averaging 12 miles per hour. She rode home the same way, mostly downhill, at 18 miles per hour. She packed two bottles of water for the ride.
problems.ask: What was Rosa's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 72 ÷ 5 = 14.4 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Kenji, who is 6 feet tall, stands on level ground in the shadow of an oak tree, 40 feet from its base. His own shadow is 8 feet long and points the same way, and its tip lands exactly on the tip of the oak tree's shadow. The tree was planted about 15 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the oak tree, in feet?
steps: The oak tree's shadow runs past Kenji to the same tip: 40 + 8 = 48 feet long.
Same sun angle, so height ÷ shadow matches: 6 ÷ 8 for Kenji.
Height of the oak tree = 48 × 6 ÷ 8 = 288 ÷ 8 = 36 feet.

bonus.stem: During a power outage, Owen reaches into his sock drawer in total darkness. The drawer holds 3 black, 10 white and 7 gray socks, all loose and all the same size.
bonus.ask: What is the fewest socks Owen must pull out to be sure of getting two gray socks?
steps: Worst case: he pulls every non-gray one first: 3 + 10 = 13.
Even the next one only gives him a single gray one.
One more must be gray, making two: 13 + 2 = 15 socks.

problems.stem: At the hardware store, 4 feet of rope costs $1.60. Elena needs 8 feet to hang a porch swing, and the store cuts rope to any length at the same price per foot.
problems.ask: How much will 8 feet of rope cost?

problems.stem: A smoothie recipe makes 6 servings and calls for 1 1/4 cups of plain yogurt. Leah is making 12 servings for her soccer team after practice. The yogurt was on sale for $2.50 a tub.
problems.ask: If she scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of yogurt will she need?

problems.stem: Amara's chemistry grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and her average so far. There are 34 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Amara need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 80?
steps: To finish at 80, the final must add 80 − 48.4 = 31.6 points.
The final is worth 40%, so the score needed is 31.6 ÷ 0.4 = 79.

problems.stem: Chloe needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. She plans to pick up the car at 7:30 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $16 more up front.
Company B costs $0.20 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.20.
Check: $63 + 80 × $0.15 = $75 and $47 + 80 × $0.35 = $75, so the answer is 80 miles.

problems.stem: Hugo snaps a photo of the clock tower in the town square at exactly 4:17. The tower is 75 feet tall. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 17 × 6 = 102 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 4 × 30 + 17 × 0.5 = 128.5 degrees past the 12.
That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 26.5 degrees.

problems.stem: Maya buys eight cans of tomatoes for a big pot of chili. Each can holds 8 ounces, and there are 16 ounces in a pound.
problems.ask: How many pounds of tomatoes is that in all?
steps: There are 16 ounces in a pound: 64 ÷ 16 = 4 pounds.

problems.stem: Sam is making lasagna for 10 guests and wants it ready to serve at 6:30 p.m. sharp. Assembling it takes 20 minutes, baking takes 60 minutes, and it must rest 10 minutes before serving. These steps happen one after another. It is 4:50 p.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Sam wait before starting?
steps: From 4:50 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. is 100 minutes.

problems.stem: Ezra is stocking up on peanut butter and compares the three jar sizes in the table. He goes through about three jars a month.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Ravi's club ran a bake sale on Saturday morning. They sold cookies, brownies and muffins in the ratio 3:5:2, and they sold 100 items in all. Every item was priced at $2.50.
problems.ask: How many cookies did the club sell?

problems.stem: Rosa teaches two sections of algebra. On Friday's test, the 8 students in her first-period class averaged 70 points, and the 22 students in her fourth-period class averaged 85 points. The test had 30 questions.
problems.ask: What was the average score for all of the students in both classes together, in points?

problems.stem: Noor is building a wooden garden gate shaped like a rectangle, 30 inches wide and 72 inches tall. To keep it from sagging, she will nail a straight brace from one corner to the opposite corner. The gate will hang on two hinges.
problems.ask: How long must the brace be, in inches?
steps: The brace is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs equal to the width and height.

problems.stem: The drama club at June's school sold 78 tickets for its Saturday show. Adult tickets cost $8 and student tickets cost $5. Ticket sales came to $507 in all, and the auditorium has 400 seats.
problems.ask: How many adult tickets were sold?
steps: The real total is $507, which is $507 − $390 = $117 more.
Each adult ticket adds $3 more than a student ticket, so there are $117 ÷ $3 = 39 adult tickets.

problems.stem: Fatima orders takeout noodles and dumplings for the family. The order comes to $64.80, and she adds a 20% tip for the delivery driver.
problems.ask: How much is the tip?

problems.stem: Mateo bikes to work. He rides 10 miles on a bike path at a steady 12 miles per hour, then 4 miles through city streets at a steady 10 miles per hour. The bike path has 17 benches along the way.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 10 ÷ 12 = 5/6 hour, which is 50 minutes.
Second part: 4 ÷ 10 = 2/5 hour, which is 24 minutes.

problems.stem: Jamal helped run a pancake breakfast at the fire station. Adult plates cost $11 and kids' plates cost $6. They served 77 plates and took in $702, with eight volunteers working the griddles.
problems.ask: How many adult plates did they serve?
steps: If all 77 were kids' plates, the total would be 77 × $6 = $462.
The actual total is $702 − $462 = $240 more than that.
Each adult plate brings in $5 more than each kids' plate, so adult plates: $240 ÷ $5 = 48.

problems.stem: Jade mixed 8 cups of fruit punch that is 40% juice for a party. It tastes too sweet, so she wants to add water until the punch is only 20% juice. Seventeen guests are coming.
problems.ask: How many cups of water should Jade add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 20% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 40/20 = 2: 8 × 2 = 16 cups.

problems.stem: A fruit bowl in Sam's kitchen holds 7 red apples and 4 green apples. He bought them at a farm stand that opened 15 years ago. On his way out the door, he grabs two apples at random, one after the other.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both apples are the same color?

problems.stem: Ben is planting a rectangular vegetable garden that measures 16 feet by 5 feet. He wants a short fence around it to keep rabbits out. One 16-foot side runs along the shed wall, so it needs no fence.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Ben need?
steps: Fence the other 16-foot side and both 5-foot sides.

problems.stem: A store is taking 30% off every winter coat, and June finds one with a regular price of $90. She also has a member coupon that takes 20% off the already reduced price. She waited in line for 5 minutes to pay.
problems.ask: How much does June pay for the winter coat, before tax?
steps: 30% of $90 is $27, so the sale price is $90 − $27 = $63.
The extra 20% comes off $63, not the original price: 20% of $63 is $12.60.

problems.stem: Ruth and five friends went out for dinner and waited 25 minutes for a table. They ordered six entrées at $17 each and one appetizer to share for $13. Sales tax is 10%, and they added a 15% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the dinner, including tax and tip?
steps: Tip: 10% of $115 is $11.50, plus half of that, $5.75, gives $17.25.

problems.stem: Jade's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 80 minutes.
problems.ask: What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
steps: With 26 values in order, the median is the average of the 13th and 14th values.
Running totals: through 0: 2, through 1: 8, through 2: 9, through 3: 14, through 4: 17, through 5: 26.
Both fall in the row for 3 goals, so the median is 3 goals.

problems.stem: Silas and Rosa start at opposite ends of a 8-mile lakeside path and walk toward each other. Silas walks at 2 miles per hour, and Rosa walks at 4 miles per hour. They leave at the same time. The lake is about 13 feet deep in the middle.
problems.ask: How many minutes after they leave do they meet?
steps: The gap closes at 2 + 4 = 6 miles per hour.

bonus.stem: A frog at the bottom of a 14-foot ditch hops 7 feet up the muddy bank every day, then slips back 6 feet every night.
bonus.ask: On which day does the frog first reach the top of the bank, if the first day of climbing is day 1?
steps: Each full day and night, the frog gains 7 − 6 = 1 foot.
On its last day it climbs 7 feet and never slides back, so it only needs to start that day at 14 − 7 = 7 feet.
Reaching 7 feet takes 7 ÷ 1 = 7 full days and nights.
It reaches the top on day 7 + 1 = 8.

problems.stem: Nadia is tiling her kitchen floor, a rectangle 16 feet long and 8 feet wide. She is using square tiles that measure 24 inches on each side, and they fit exactly with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many tiles does Nadia need?
steps: 24 inches is 2 feet. Along the length: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 tiles.

problems.stem: Nico is planning a hike with a trail map where 1 centimeter represents 5 kilometers. The trail to the waterfall measures 3.5 centimeters on the map, and the trail back to the parking lot measures 5 centimeters. The parking lot has 30 spaces.
problems.ask: How many kilometers long is the whole hike?

problems.stem: Kenji wants to buy a couch at a furniture store. The price is $770 if he pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $200 down, then 10 monthly payments of $79. The couch is 90 inches long.
problems.ask: How much more would Kenji pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Esme and Noor are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Esme could paint it in 3 hours, and Noor could paint it in 7 hours. The fence is 200 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Esme does 1/3 of the fence and Noor does 1/7.
Together: 1/3 + 1/7 = 7/21 + 3/21 = 10/21 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: Paige, Arjun, Andre and two of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Paige, Arjun and Andre are triplets and want to stand together, side by side. The photographer charges $75 for the session.
problems.ask: In how many different orders can the 5 of them line up?
steps: Glue the three into one block, leaving 3 units: 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 orders.
Inside the block the three can be ordered 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 ways.

problems.stem: Nadia orders a set of mixing bowls that costs $15 before tax. Her state charges an 8% sales tax on the purchase.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the set of mixing bowls, including tax?

problems.stem: Chloe is traveling in Italy, where prices are in euros. That week, 1 euro costs $1.20 in U.S. money. She buys a pair of sunglasses for 17 euros and a cookbook for 28 euros. Her hotel is 3 blocks from the shop.
problems.ask: How much did Chloe spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Tariq's grandmother gave him $2,500 for his 18th birthday. He put all of it in a certificate of deposit that pays 5% interest, compounded once a year, and left it alone.
problems.ask: How much interest will the money earn over the 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 5% of $2,500 is $125, so the value goes to $2,500 + $125 = $2,625.

problems.stem: Yuki started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 3 miles per hour. Ravi started running from the same spot 20 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 7 miles per hour. The path is 6 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Ravi catch up to Yuki?
steps: Head start: in 20 minutes (1/3 hour), Yuki covers 3 × 1/3 = 1 mile.
Time to close the gap: 1 ÷ 4 = 1/4 hour = 15 minutes.

problems.stem: Dmitri runs a prize wheel at the school fair. The wheel has 8 equal sections, each equally likely to land on top, and a spin costs $2. The table shows what the sections pay. The fair runs for 8 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the prize wheel make per spin after paying out prizes?
steps: If each section came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $10 + 2 × $1 = $12.
The booth keeps $2 − $1.50 = $0.50 per spin on average.

problems.stem: Victor and three friends go bowling. The lanes cost $50 for the night, and shoe rentals add $17. They split the total evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Victor plus three others makes 4 people.

problems.stem: Dev is putting laminate flooring in a rectangular home office that measures 15 feet by 9 feet. Each box of flooring covers 24 square feet and weighs 36 pounds. The store sells only whole boxes.
problems.ask: Ignoring waste, how many boxes does Dev need to buy?
steps: 5 boxes cover 5 × 24 = 120 square feet, which is not enough.
6 boxes cover 144 square feet, so Dev needs 6 boxes.

problems.stem: Last month, a bag of coffee beans at Kenji's grocery store cost $16. This month the same bag costs $18. Kenji goes through about one bag every 10 days.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bag increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $2 ÷ $16 = 1/8 = 0.125.
As a percent, that is an increase of 12.5%.

problems.stem: Ava is growing bacteria for a biology lab. She starts a dish with 400 bacteria, and under these conditions the population doubles every 30 minutes. The dish is 15 centimeters across.
problems.ask: How many bacteria will be in the dish after 3.5 hours?

problems.stem: Chloe is four times as old as her daughter, Ingrid. They live 8 blocks apart and walk together most weekends. In 5 years, Chloe will be three times as old as Ingrid.
problems.ask: How old is Ingrid now, in years?
steps: Let Ingrid's age now be x, so Chloe is 4x.
Subtract 3x and 5 from both sides: x = 15 − 5 = 10.
So Ingrid is 10 years old now. Check: in 5 years, 45 = 3 × 15.

problems.stem: Tariq shops at the farmers market on Saturday morning. He buys a jar of honey for $7.25, a loaf of sourdough for $6.25, and a pint of blueberries for $3.99. There's no sales tax, and he pays with a $50 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Tariq get back?

problems.stem: Mateo is stocking up at a garden center for his spring planting. The prices, with tax included, are in the table. The garden center is 3 miles from his house. Mateo orders two flower pots, four bags of potting soil, and four seed packets.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Mateo's order?

problems.stem: Andre is painting the four walls of his basement playroom, which is 20 feet long, 13 feet wide and 10 feet high. He wants two coats on every wall. The door and windows take up 40 square feet that won't be painted. One gallon of paint covers 400 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $32 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Andre need to buy?
steps: Minus the door and windows: 660 − 40 = 620 square feet.
1,240 ÷ 400 = 3.1, which is more than 3, so round up to 4 gallons.

problems.stem: In March, the hardware store where Chloe works raised the price of a patio umbrella by 30%. In June, the store put it on sale for 20% off that new price. Chloe has worked at the store for 12 months.
problems.ask: By what percent is the June price higher than the original price?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
104 is 4 above 100, so it is 4% higher.

problems.stem: Lucia's robotics club runs a weekly bake sale. In week 1 the club sets aside $20 for a trip, and each week after that it sets aside $0.50 more than the week before. The club has 10 members this year.
problems.ask: How much will the club have set aside in all after 13 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 13, week 2 with week 12, and so on: each pair adds to $20 + $26 = $46.
With 13 weeks, the average week is $46 ÷ 2 = $23, so the total is 13 × $23 = $299.

problems.stem: At 4:40 p.m., Isaac put a loaf of bread in the oven. He took it out at 5:20 p.m., when the crust was golden brown.
problems.ask: For how many minutes did the bread bake?
steps: From 4:40 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 20 minutes.
From 5:00 p.m. to 5:20 p.m. is 20 minutes.

problems.stem: Nadia is driving to a state park, which is 160 miles from home, and then driving back. Her car gets 20 miles per gallon, and gas costs $3.10 per gallon. She plans to leave at 7 in the morning.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the round trip?

problems.stem: Nico's company asked its employees how they usually get to work. Each person gave one answer, shown in the table. The office parking lot has 120 spaces.
problems.ask: What percent of the employees surveyed chose either "Drive" or "Bike"?

problems.stem: The water trough at Chloe's farm is a rectangular metal tank 4 feet long, 2.5 feet wide and 1.5 feet deep. It serves the five horses in the north pasture. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the trough hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Felix rode his bike 30 miles to a lake, mostly uphill, averaging 10 miles per hour. He rode home the same way, mostly downhill, at 15 miles per hour. He packed two bottles of water for the ride.
problems.ask: What was Felix's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Victor has a recipe for a 6-inch round cake, but he wants to bake it in a 9-inch round pan instead, filled to the same depth. The oven is set to 325 degrees.
problems.ask: How many times the original recipe should Victor make to fill the bigger pan?
steps: A circle's area is π × radius², so area grows with the square of the diameter.

problems.stem: At a pizza shop, customers build a pizza by choosing exactly 3 different toppings from a list of 6. Every pizza also gets one of 2 crusts: thin or regular. A large pizza is cut into 12 slices. The order the toppings are chosen in doesn't matter.
problems.ask: How many different pizzas can a customer build?
steps: Pick 3 of 6 toppings: 6 × 5 × 4 = 120 ordered picks, ÷ 6 (the 3 × 2 × 1 orders of the same three) = 20 sets.
Each set can go with any of the 2 crusts: 20 × 2 = 40 pizzas.

problems.stem: Ava spots a pair of hiking boots with a price tag of $71. A sign on the rack says the price will be 50% off at the register.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the pair of hiking boots, before tax?

problems.stem: Fatima is picking up bagels for the team's 9:30 a.m. meeting. The bakery sells bagels in packs of 6 for $6.75, or one at a time for $1.25 each. Fifteen people are coming, and Fatima wants at least one bagel per person. Leftovers are fine, but she can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Fatima can spend?
steps: 15 ÷ 6 = 2 full packs, with 3 people left over.

problems.stem: Jade's chemistry grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and her average so far. There are 33 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Jade need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 85?
steps: To finish at 85, the final must add 85 − 55.6 = 29.4 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 29.4 ÷ 0.3 = 98.

problems.stem: Kofi is signing up for pottery classes at a local studio, which offers the two options in the table. Each class lasts 90 minutes.
problems.ask: How many classes in a month would make the two options cost exactly the same?
steps: Drop-in costs $10 more per class, so each class closes the gap by $10.
Check: $90 + 9 × $9 = $171 and $0 + 9 × $19 = $171, so the answer is 9 classes.

problems.stem: At the school fair, a spinner has 5 equal sections, and two of them are marked Prize. Jordan trades 4 tickets for two spins.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Jordan lands on Prize at least once?
steps: Work with the opposite: one spin misses Prize with probability 3/5.

bonus.stem: Eli's grandfather clock strikes once for each hour, with the strikes evenly spaced. At 7 o'clock, it takes 6 seconds from the first strike to the last.
bonus.ask: How many seconds does it take from the first strike to the last at 10 o'clock?
steps: 7 strikes have only 6 gaps between them, so each gap is 6 ÷ 6 = 1 second.

problems.stem: Raul is saving for a camping tent that costs $95. He already has $55 saved and puts away $5 each week.
problems.ask: How many more weeks will it take Raul to have exactly enough?

problems.stem: Ben works at a warehouse for $14 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times his regular rate. His commute is 3 miles each way. Last week he worked 49 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Ben earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $14 = $21 an hour, for 49 − 40 = 9 hours.

problems.stem: Mei is mixing concrete for a garden path that is 15 feet long. Her mix uses cement, sand and gravel in the ratio 5:1:4 by volume. She needs 70 buckets of mix in all.
problems.ask: How many buckets of sand does Mei need?

problems.stem: A rectangular park near Imani's apartment is 960 meters long and 280 meters wide. Imani usually walks along two edges to get from one corner to the opposite corner. Today she cuts straight across the grass on the diagonal instead. The park has 9 benches.
problems.ask: How many meters shorter is the diagonal route than the route along the two edges?
steps: Shrink the numbers first: 960 = 40 × 24 and 280 = 40 × 7. Since 24² + 7² = 576 + 49 = 625 = 25², the diagonal is 40 × 25 = 1,000 meters.

problems.stem: A café asked 100 regular customers which drinks they had ordered in the past month. The results are in the table. The "Iced coffee" and "Hot tea" counts include the customers who ordered both drinks. The café has 13 tables.
problems.ask: How many of the 100 customers ordered neither drink?

bonus.stem: Ingrid is sewing a quilt that is a 4-by-4 grid of square patches. Looking at the grid lines, Ingrid wonders how many squares can be traced, counting every size, from single patches up to the biggest square that fits.
bonus.ask: How many squares of all sizes are in the 4-by-4 grid?
steps: A k-by-k square can start in 4 − k + 1 spots across and the same number down, so there are (4 − k + 1)² of them.

problems.stem: Felix keeps a weather log for a science project. The daily high temperatures from Monday to Friday were 67, 72, 60, 64, and 62 degrees Fahrenheit.
problems.ask: What was the average daily high for those five days, in degrees?

problems.stem: Dev must be at work by 8:30 a.m. for a meeting. He walks 15 minutes to the train station, rides the train for 35 minutes, and then walks 5 minutes to the office. A train ticket costs $3, and a train leaves the moment he reaches the platform. It is 6:55 a.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Dev wait before leaving home?
steps: From 6:55 a.m. to 8:30 a.m. is 95 minutes.

problems.stem: Owen is comparing three sizes of the same cereal, shown in the table. He eats about four ounces each morning.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Hana mixed 6 liters of liquid plant food that is 20% concentrate. The label says seedlings need a mix that is only 8% concentrate, so she will dilute it with water. She is growing four trays of seedlings.
problems.ask: How many liters of water should Hana add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 8% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 20/8 = 5/2: 6 × 5/2 = 15 liters.

problems.stem: The clock at the train station has a face 6 feet across. While Ezra waits on the platform, it reads 11:34. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 34 × 6 = 204 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 11 × 30 + 34 × 0.5 = 347 degrees past the 12.
That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 143 degrees.

problems.stem: Priya buys four cans of tomatoes for a big pot of chili. Each can holds 8 ounces, and there are 16 ounces in a pound.
problems.ask: How many pounds of tomatoes is that in all?
steps: There are 16 ounces in a pound: 32 ÷ 16 = 2 pounds.

problems.stem: Hugo bowls in a league with 10 teams. So far this season he has bowled four games, scoring 128, 142, 174, and 148. He wants his average after the next game to be exactly 150.
problems.ask: What score does Hugo need in the next game?
steps: An average of 150 over 5 games means a total of 150 × 5 = 750.

problems.stem: Raul helped run a pancake breakfast at the fire station. Adult plates cost $7 and kids' plates cost $4. They served 100 plates and took in $619, with nine volunteers working the griddles.
problems.ask: How many kids' plates did they serve?
steps: If all 100 were kids' plates, the total would be 100 × $4 = $400.
The actual total is $619 − $400 = $219 more than that.
Each adult plate brings in $3 more than each kids' plate, so adult plates: $219 ÷ $3 = 73.

problems.stem: Carmen's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 90 minutes.
problems.ask: What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
steps: With 35 values in order, the median is the 18th value.
Running totals: through 0: 3, through 1: 7, through 2: 14, through 3: 22, through 4: 26, through 5: 35.
The 18th value falls in the row for 3 goals, so the median is 3 goals.

problems.stem: Luis, who is 5 feet tall, stands on level ground in the shadow of a light pole, 12 feet from its base. His own shadow is 4 feet long and points the same way, and its tip lands exactly on the tip of the light pole's shadow. The parking lot around it has 21 spaces.
problems.ask: How tall is the light pole, in feet?
steps: The light pole's shadow runs past Luis to the same tip: 12 + 4 = 16 feet long.
Same sun angle, so height ÷ shadow matches: 5 ÷ 4 for Luis.
Height of the light pole = 16 × 5 ÷ 4 = 80 ÷ 4 = 20 feet.

problems.stem: A farm stand sells a 4-pound bag of apples for $5. Omar wants 7 pounds for pies, and the stand will weigh out any amount at the same price per pound.
problems.ask: How much will 7 pounds of apples cost?

problems.stem: Esme has her eye on a desk chair with a regular price of $130. This week it's marked 40% off. At checkout, she also uses a coupon for an extra 20% off the sale price. The sale price is good for 6 more days.
problems.ask: How much does Esme pay for the desk chair, before tax?
steps: 40% of $130 is $52, so the sale price is $130 − $52 = $78.
The extra 20% comes off $78, not the original price: 20% of $78 is $15.60.

problems.stem: Luis bought a winter coat at a department store during a 20%-off sale, and he also used a $10 coupon. The register took 20% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. The sale lasted six days. Before tax, Luis paid $146.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the coat?
steps: $156 is what was left after 20% off, so it is 80% of the original price.

problems.stem: Kenji's running club timed its members in a 5-kilometer race. The 8 runners in the morning group averaged 27 minutes, and the 12 runners in the evening group averaged 32 minutes. The course had four water stations.
problems.ask: What was the average time for all the runners in both groups, in minutes?

problems.stem: A fruit bowl in Noor's kitchen holds 5 red apples and 6 green apples. She bought them at a farm stand that opened 14 years ago. On her way out the door, she grabs two apples at random, one after the other.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both apples are the same color?

bonus.stem: Before a chess tournament, each of the 21 players shakes hands with every other player once. Carmen, the organizer, just watches.
bonus.ask: How many handshakes are there in all?
steps: Each of the 21 players takes part in 20 handshakes: 21 × 20 = 420.
That counts every one twice (once for each person in it), so divide by 2: 420 ÷ 2 = 210.

problems.stem: Lucia orders takeout noodles and dumplings for the family. The order comes to $42, and she adds a 15% tip for the delivery driver.
problems.ask: How much does Lucia pay in all, including the tip?

problems.stem: Mateo bikes to work. He rides 12 miles on a bike path at a steady 12 miles per hour, then 3 miles through city streets at a steady 6 miles per hour. His office is on the third floor.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 12 ÷ 12 = 1 hour, which is 60 minutes.
Second part: 3 ÷ 6 = 1/2 hour, which is 30 minutes.

problems.stem: Caleb buys a monthly bus pass. Last year the pass cost $65, and this year the transit agency raised the price to $78. He rides the bus about 20 days a month.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bus pass increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $13 ÷ $65 = 1/5 = 0.2.
As a percent, that is an increase of 20%.

problems.stem: Ezra has a recipe for a 6-inch round cake, but he wants to bake it in a 10-inch round pan instead, filled to the same depth. The oven is set to 350 degrees.
problems.ask: How many times the original recipe should Ezra make to fill the bigger pan?

problems.stem: The drama club at Arjun's school sold 116 tickets for its Saturday show. Adult tickets cost $12 and student tickets cost $7. Ticket sales came to $1,187 in all, and the auditorium has 400 seats.
problems.ask: How many adult tickets were sold?
steps: The real total is $1,187, which is $1,187 − $812 = $375 more.
Each adult ticket adds $5 more than a student ticket, so there are $375 ÷ $5 = 75 adult tickets.

bonus.stem: Today is Sunday. Rosa will be away for the next 82 days, starting tomorrow. Trash is picked up every Tuesday morning, so her neighbor has offered to take the bins out while she is gone.
bonus.ask: How many Tuesday pickups will fall during those 82 days?
steps: Each full week has exactly one Tuesday: 11.
The 5 extra days fall on the same weekdays as the first 5: Monday through Friday, which includes one more Tuesday.

problems.stem: Victor is laying square pavers for a backyard patio. The patio will be a rectangle 18 feet by 16 feet, and each paver is 24 inches on a side. The pavers fit exactly, with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many pavers does Victor need?
steps: 24 inches is 2 feet. Along the length: 18 ÷ 2 = 9 pavers.

problems.stem: A smoothie recipe makes 8 servings and calls for 1 1/2 cups of plain yogurt. Kenji is making 24 servings for his soccer team after practice. The yogurt was on sale for $4 a tub.
problems.ask: If he scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of yogurt will he need?

problems.stem: Tess wants to buy a laptop at an electronics store. The price is $834 if she pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $100 down, then 24 monthly payments of $36. The laptop weighs about 4 pounds.
problems.ask: How much more would Tess pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Fatima's grandmother gave her $4,000 for her 18th birthday. She put all of it in a certificate of deposit that pays 5% interest, compounded once a year, and left it alone.
problems.ask: How much will the certificate of deposit be worth after 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 5% of $4,000 is $200, so the value goes to $4,000 + $200 = $4,200.

problems.stem: Hugo and Theo are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Hugo could paint it in 12 hours, and Theo could paint it in 28 hours. The fence is 80 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Hugo does 1/12 of the fence and Theo does 1/28.
Together: 1/12 + 1/28 = 7/84 + 3/84 = 10/84 = 5/42 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: Noor owns 6 shares of a company's stock. On Monday the share price rose 40%. On Tuesday it fell 30% from Monday's closing price.
problems.ask: By what percent is Tuesday's closing price lower than the price before Monday's change?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
98 is 2 below 100, so it is 2% lower.

problems.stem: Six friends, including Esme, Rosa and Nadia, have 6 seats together in one row at the movies. Esme, Rosa and Nadia want three seats in a row together. The movie runs 95 minutes.
problems.ask: In how many different ways can the 6 friends fill the 6 seats?
steps: Glue the three into one block, leaving 4 units: 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24 orders.
Inside the block the three can be ordered 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 ways.

problems.stem: Ben is fencing in a rectangular play area for his kids. The area is 25 feet long and 16 feet wide. One 25-foot side runs along the barn wall, so it needs no fence.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Ben need?
steps: Fence the other 25-foot side and both 16-foot sides.

problems.stem: Wes is planning a road trip to the coast with a paper map. On the map, 1 inch represents 50 miles. The route has two straight stretches: the first measures 4 inches, and the second measures 1 1/4 inches. He plans to leave at 9 in the morning.
problems.ask: How many miles long is the route?

problems.stem: Malik took his family out for brunch at a diner that opened 20 years ago. They ordered five pancake plates at $21 each and a pitcher of orange juice for $14. Sales tax is 6%, and they added a 15% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the brunch, including tax and tip?
steps: Tip: 10% of $119 is $11.90, plus half of that, $5.95, gives $17.85.

problems.stem: Hana set out on her bike along the river trail, riding at a steady 12 miles per hour. Lucia left from the same spot 10 minutes later and followed the same trail at a steady 17 miles per hour. The trail is 20 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting did Lucia catch up to Hana?
steps: Head start: in 10 minutes (1/6 hour), Hana covers 12 × 1/6 = 2 miles.
Time to close the gap: 2 ÷ 5 = 2/5 hour = 24 minutes.

problems.stem: Carmen's booth at the town festival has 10 rubber ducks floating in a pool. A player pays $3, picks one duck at random, and wins the prize marked underneath; the duck then goes back in. The table shows the prizes. The festival lasts 5 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the booth make per game after paying out prizes?
steps: If each duck came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $20 + 2 × $2 = $24.
The booth keeps $3 − $2.40 = $0.60 per game on average.

problems.stem: Dev is shopping for a new bike helmet and finds one priced at $30. The sales tax where he lives is 6%, added at the register.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the bike helmet, including tax?

problems.stem: On a trip to Mexico, Zoe exchanges money at a rate of 20 pesos per U.S. dollar. At an outdoor market, she buys a painted bowl for 200 pesos and a straw hat for 440 pesos. She has seven days left on the trip.
problems.ask: How much did Zoe spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Caleb is painting the four walls of his bedroom, which is 18 feet long, 12 feet wide and 10 feet high. He wants two coats on every wall. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $36 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Caleb need to buy?
steps: 1,200 ÷ 350 ≈ 3.4, which is more than 3, so round up to 4 gallons.

problems.stem: Algae is spreading across the pond on Kenji's farm. Right now it covers 6 square feet, and the area it covers doubles every 3 days. The pond is about 4 feet deep.
problems.ask: If it keeps doubling at this rate, how many square feet will the algae cover 18 days from now?

problems.stem: Andre is three times as old as his daughter, Chloe. This spring they planted 3 tomato plants together. Exactly 7 years ago, Andre was five times as old as Chloe.
problems.ask: How old is Andre now, in years?
steps: Let Chloe's age now be x, so Andre is 3x.
Move the x terms to one side: 2x = 35 − 7 = 28, so x = 14.
So Andre is 3 × 14 = 42 years old now. Check: 7 years ago, 35 = 5 × 7.

problems.stem: Dev and five friends rent a lake cabin for a weekend. The rental costs $480, plus a $75 cleaning fee. They split the whole cost evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Dev plus five others makes 6 people.

problems.stem: Nico is sealing a rectangular concrete patio that is 21 feet long and 14 feet wide. One gallon of sealer covers 50 square feet, and it needs 24 hours to dry. Sealer is sold only by the whole gallon.
problems.ask: How many gallons must Nico buy to give the patio one coat?
steps: 5 gallons cover 5 × 50 = 250 square feet, which is not enough.
6 gallons cover 300 square feet, so Nico needs 6 gallons.

problems.stem: The water trough at Carmen's farm is a rectangular metal tank 8 feet long, 2 feet wide and 2 feet deep. It serves the three horses in the north pasture. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the trough hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Nadia needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. She plans to pick up the car at 8 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $27 more up front.
Company B costs $0.15 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.15.

problems.stem: Eli just started a dog-walking business. He moves $7 into savings the first week, and each week after that he moves $2 more than the week before. He has 7 regular customers.
problems.ask: How much will Eli have set aside in all after 19 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 19, week 2 with week 18, and so on: each pair adds to $7 + $43 = $50.
With 19 weeks, the average week is $50 ÷ 2 = $25, so the total is 19 × $25 = $475.

bonus.stem: A hotel hallway has 168 lamps, numbered 1 to 168, all switched off. One by one, 168 guests walk past. Guest 1 flips the switch on every lamp, guest 2 flips every 2nd lamp, guest 3 flips every 3rd lamp, and so on, until guest 168 flips only lamp 168. Leah is the last guest.
bonus.ask: How many lamps are on at the end?
steps: A lamp is switched once for each number that divides it (lamp 12: by 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12).
Divisors come in pairs (1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4), so most lamps are switched an even number of times and end off.
Only perfect squares have an odd number of divisors, because one pair repeats (6 × 6 = 36).
Perfect squares up to 168: 1, 4, 9, …, 144, which is 12 lamps on.

problems.stem: At 11:25 a.m., Mei put a loaf of bread in the oven. She took it out at 12:10 p.m., when the crust was golden brown.
problems.ask: For how many minutes did the bread bake?
steps: From 11:25 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. is 35 minutes.
From 12:00 p.m. to 12:10 p.m. is 10 minutes.

problems.stem: Luis is buying snacks for his family at a baseball game. The snack bar's prices, tax included, are in the table. Their seats are in row 14. Luis orders one hot dog, two pretzels, and four lemonades.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Luis's order?

problems.stem: Hana's biology grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and her average so far. There are 33 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Hana need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 80?
steps: To finish at 80, the final must add 80 − 56.3 = 23.7 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 23.7 ÷ 0.3 = 79.

problems.stem: Carmen rode her bike 30 miles to a lake, mostly uphill, averaging 12 miles per hour. She rode home the same way, mostly downhill, at 20 miles per hour. She packed three bottles of water for the ride.
problems.ask: What was Carmen's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: At an ice cream stand, customers build a sundae by choosing exactly 3 different toppings from a list of 6. Every sundae also gets one of 3 ice cream flavors: vanilla, chocolate or strawberry. Each sundae comes in a 16-ounce cup. The order the toppings are chosen in doesn't matter.
problems.ask: How many different sundaes can a customer build?
steps: Pick 3 of 6 toppings: 6 × 5 × 4 = 120 ordered picks, ÷ 6 (the 3 × 2 × 1 orders of the same three) = 20 sets.
Each set can go with any of the 3 ice cream flavors: 20 × 3 = 60 sundaes.

problems.stem: Carmen shops at the farmers market on Saturday morning. She buys a jar of honey for $6.50, a loaf of sourdough for $6.25, and a pint of blueberries for $4.25. There's no sales tax, and she pays with a $20 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Carmen get back?

problems.stem: Owen is making lasagna for 7 guests and wants it ready to serve at 6:00 p.m. sharp. Assembling it takes 30 minutes, baking takes 55 minutes, and it must rest 10 minutes before serving. These steps happen one after another. It is 3:40 p.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Owen wait before starting?
steps: From 3:40 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. is 140 minutes.

problems.stem: Chloe's club ran a bake sale on Saturday morning. They sold cookies, brownies and muffins in the ratio 3:2:2, and they sold 91 items in all. Every item was priced at $1.50.
problems.ask: How many muffins did the club sell?

problems.stem: A rectangular park near Raul's apartment is 400 meters long and 300 meters wide. Raul usually walks along two edges to get from one corner to the opposite corner. Today he cuts straight across the grass on the diagonal instead. The park has 15 benches.
problems.ask: How many meters shorter is the diagonal route than the route along the two edges?
steps: Shrink the numbers first: 400 = 100 × 4 and 300 = 100 × 3. Since 4² + 3² = 16 + 9 = 25 = 5², the diagonal is 100 × 5 = 500 meters.

problems.stem: Kofi and Leah are 70 miles apart on the same highway and drive toward each other to meet for dinner. Kofi drives at 60 miles per hour, and Leah drives at 40 miles per hour. Leah leaves 30 minutes after Kofi. Kofi's car holds 15 gallons of gas.
problems.ask: How many minutes after Kofi leaves do they meet?
steps: Head start: in 30 minutes, Kofi covers 60 × 1/2 = 30 miles.
Distance left when Leah leaves: 70 − 30 = 40 miles.
Together they close 60 + 40 = 100 miles per hour: 40 ÷ 100 = 2/5 hour = 24 minutes after Leah leaves.
Counting from when Kofi leaves: 30 + 24 = 54 minutes.

problems.stem: The store is taking 20% off everything this week, including the board game Ava has had her eye on. Its regular price is $20.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the board game, before tax?

problems.stem: Noor is driving 280 miles to a college campus for a tour, where she'll catch a ride home with family. Her car gets 35 miles per gallon, and gas costs $3.20 per gallon. The drive takes about 5 hours, with one stop for lunch.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the drive?

problems.stem: Priya works at the town library and asked visitors their main reason for coming in. Each visitor gave one answer, shown in the table. The library is open 60 hours a week.
problems.ask: What percent of the visitors surveyed chose "Use computers"?

problems.stem: Nadia mixed 5 liters of liquid plant food that is 20% concentrate. The label says seedlings need a mix that is only 8% concentrate, so she will dilute it with water. She is growing three trays of seedlings.
problems.ask: How many liters of water should Nadia add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 8% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 20/8 = 5/2: 5 × 5/2 = 12.5 liters.

problems.stem: A community center asked 60 members which summer trips they would sign up for. The results are in the table. The "Hiking trip" and "Kayaking trip" counts include the members who signed up for both trips. The sign-up sheet was posted for 17 days.
problems.ask: How many members signed up for both trips?
steps: So the extra count is the 'both' group: 19 − 14 = 5.

problems.stem: Lena is saving for a used guitar that costs $175. She already has $35 saved and puts away $20 each week.
problems.ask: How many more weeks will it take Lena to have exactly enough?

problems.stem: Fatima is picking up bagels for the team's 8 a.m. meeting. The bakery sells bagels in packs of 6 for $6.75, or one at a time for $1.25 each. Thirteen people are coming, and Fatima wants at least one bagel per person. Leftovers are fine, but she can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Fatima can spend?
steps: 13 ÷ 6 = 2 full packs, with 1 person left over.

problems.stem: Arjun's swim team held a car wash to raise money. They charged $10 for each car and $15 for each truck or SUV. Over five hours on Saturday, they washed 73 vehicles and collected $940.
problems.ask: How many cars did the team wash?
steps: If all 73 were cars, the total would be 73 × $10 = $730.
The actual total is $940 − $730 = $210 more than that.
Each truck or SUV brings in $5 more than each car, so trucks and SUVs: $210 ÷ $5 = 42.

problems.stem: Last month, a bag of coffee beans at Ben's grocery store cost $20. This month the same bag costs $24. Ben goes through about one bag every 13 days.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bag increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $4 ÷ $20 = 1/5 = 0.2.
As a percent, that is an increase of 20%.

problems.stem: At the warehouse where Silas works, the 26 workers on the day shift packed an average of 52 boxes each on Monday. The 14 workers on the night shift, which started at midnight, packed an average of 72 boxes each.
problems.ask: What was the average number of boxes packed per worker across both shifts?

problems.stem: Priya's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 80 minutes.
problems.ask: What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
steps: With 28 values in order, the median is the average of the 14th and 15th values.
Running totals: through 0: 6, through 1: 13, through 2: 19, through 3: 20, through 4: 25, through 5: 28.
Both fall in the row for 2 goals, so the median is 2 goals.

problems.stem: In a board game, Sofia's piece is stuck in the jail space. Under the house rules, she rolls a standard six-sided die three times, and she escapes if any roll is a 6. The board has 30 spaces in all.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Sofia escapes?
steps: Work with the opposite: one roll is not a 6 with probability 5/6.

problems.stem: Malik is tracking how long he practices piano. From Monday to Friday, he practiced 38, 33, 40, 43, and 41 minutes.
problems.ask: What was his average practice time per day, in minutes?

problems.stem: Yuki works at a garden center for $14 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times her regular rate. She has worked there for 5 years. Last week she worked 44 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Yuki earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $14 = $21 an hour, for 44 − 40 = 4 hours.

problems.stem: Wes bought a used car for $11,000. His mechanic estimates that the car will lose 20% of its value each year, based on what it is worth at the start of that year. The car gets about 32 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: Using that estimate, how much value will the car lose over the 2 years?

problems.stem: Kofi is ordering pizza for nine friends. The pizzeria sells round pizzas in two sizes: a 10-inch small and a 14-inch large, where the size is the diameter. Both have the same crust and toppings.
problems.ask: The large pizza has how many times the area of the small pizza?

problems.stem: A fruit bowl in Nadia's kitchen holds 5 red apples and 3 green apples. She bought them at a farm stand that opened 18 years ago. On her way out the door, she grabs two apples at random, one after the other.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both apples are the same color?

problems.stem: A farm stand sells a 3-pound bag of apples for $7.50. Marcus wants 4 pounds for pies, and the stand will weigh out any amount at the same price per pound.
problems.ask: How much will 4 pounds of apples cost?

problems.stem: Ava bowls in a league with 12 teams. So far this season she has bowled four games, scoring 167, 142, 120, and 164. She wants her average after the next game to be exactly 150.
problems.ask: What score does Ava need in the next game?
steps: An average of 150 over 5 games means a total of 150 × 5 = 750.

problems.stem: Dev is buying laundry detergent. The store sells the same brand in the three sizes shown in the table. He does about five loads of laundry a week.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per fluid ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Malik is writing a report about his town. Its population shrank by 10% from 2016 to 2020, then grew by 20% from 2020 to 2024. The town has 8 public parks.
problems.ask: By what percent is the 2024 population higher than the 2016 population?
steps: Start with a population of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
108 is 8 above 100, so it is 8% higher.

problems.stem: Eli glances at the clock above the classroom door during a math quiz. It reads 9:48, and the quiz started 22 minutes earlier. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 48 × 6 = 288 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 9 × 30 + 48 × 0.5 = 294 degrees past the 12.
That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 6 degrees.

problems.stem: Yuki is running a lemonade stand. She makes six pitchers of lemonade, and each pitcher holds 10 cups. There are 4 cups in a quart.
problems.ask: How many quarts of lemonade does Yuki make?
steps: There are 4 cups in a quart: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 quarts.

problems.stem: Nico has his eye on a desk chair with a regular price of $200. This week it's marked 25% off. At checkout, he also uses a coupon for an extra 10% off the sale price. The sale price is good for 6 more days.
problems.ask: How much does Nico pay for the desk chair, before tax?
steps: 25% of $200 is $50, so the sale price is $200 − $50 = $150.
The extra 10% comes off $150, not the original price: 10% of $150 is $15.

problems.stem: Caleb bought a set of wireless headphones at an electronics store during a 50%-off sale, and he also used a $10 coupon. The register took 50% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. The headphones run about 40 hours on a full charge. Before tax, Caleb paid $79.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the headphones?
steps: $89 is what was left after 50% off, so it is 50% of the original price.

problems.stem: June and Jordan are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, June could paint it in 12 hours, and Jordan could paint it in 28 hours. The fence is 150 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, June does 1/12 of the fence and Jordan does 1/28.
Together: 1/12 + 1/28 = 7/84 + 3/84 = 10/84 = 5/42 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: On level ground, Ava holds a 3-foot yardstick straight up, and its shadow is 10 feet long. At the same moment, the shadow of a nearby oak tree is 65 feet long. The tree was planted about 12 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the oak tree, in feet?
steps: The sun hits both at the same angle, so height ÷ shadow is the same for the oak tree and the yardstick: 3 ÷ 10.
Height of the oak tree = 65 × 3 ÷ 10 = 195 ÷ 10 = 19.5 feet.

bonus.stem: Fatima is numbering the pages of a long report, from page 1 to page 80, one digit at a time.
bonus.ask: How many digits will that take in all?

problems.stem: Amara is tiling her kitchen floor, a rectangle 11 feet long and 6 feet wide. She is using square tiles that measure 12 inches on each side, and they fit exactly with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many tiles does Amara need?
steps: 12 inches is 1 foot, so each tile covers 1 square foot.
