problems.stem: Nico bikes to work. He rides 5 miles on a bike path at a steady 15 miles per hour, then 2 miles through city streets at a steady 6 miles per hour. The bike path has 19 benches along the way.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 5 ÷ 15 = 1/3 hour, which is 20 minutes.
Second part: 2 ÷ 6 = 1/3 hour, which is 20 minutes.

problems.stem: Zoe wants to buy a couch at a furniture store. The price is $750 if she pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $50 down, then 10 monthly payments of $92. The couch is 84 inches long.
problems.ask: How much more would Zoe pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Ben is studying a 240-gram sample of a radioactive substance in a lab. The substance has a half-life of 4 days, which means half of whatever is left decays every 4 days. The sample is stored in a case that weighs 15 pounds.
problems.ask: How many days will it take until only 15 grams of the substance remain?
steps: Halve until 15 grams remain: 240 → 120 → 60 → 30 → 15. That is 4 halvings.

problems.stem: Arjun, Nadia and two of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Arjun and Nadia are twins and insist on standing next to each other. The photographer charges $50 for the session.
problems.ask: In how many different orders can the 4 of them line up?
steps: Glue Arjun and Nadia into one block, leaving 3 units to arrange.
Inside the block they can switch places: 6 × 2 = 12.

problems.stem: Lucia and two coworkers stop at a diner for breakfast, and Lucia offers to pay. The check is $65.20. She plans to add a 20% tip on the full check.
problems.ask: How much does Lucia pay in all, including the tip?

problems.stem: Jade's chili recipe serves 6 people and uses 3/4 cup of chopped onion. She is cooking for 18 people at a neighborhood potluck, and the chili needs to simmer for 45 minutes.
problems.ask: If she scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of chopped onion will she need?

problems.stem: Chloe is painting the four walls of her dining room, which is 20 feet long, 10 feet wide and 8 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $36 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Chloe need to buy?
steps: 960 ÷ 350 ≈ 2.7, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

problems.stem: Leah started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 4 miles per hour. Theo started running from the same spot 15 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 7 miles per hour. The path is 8 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Theo catch up to Leah?
steps: Head start: in 15 minutes (1/4 hour), Leah covers 4 × 1/4 = 1 mile.
Time to close the gap: 1 ÷ 3 = 1/3 hour = 20 minutes.

problems.stem: Caleb runs a prize wheel at the school fair. The wheel has 10 equal sections, each equally likely to land on top, and a spin costs $5. The table shows what the sections pay. The fair runs for 4 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the prize wheel make per spin after paying out prizes?
steps: If each section came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $5 + 4 × $1 = $9.
The booth keeps $5 − $0.90 = $4.10 per spin on average.

problems.stem: Carmen is building a rectangular dog run in her backyard. It will be 23 feet long and 20 feet wide. One 23-foot side runs along the house wall, so it needs no fence.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Carmen need?
steps: Fence the other 23-foot side and both 20-foot sides.

problems.stem: Victor is planning a road trip to the coast with a paper map. On the map, 1 inch represents 20 miles. The route has two straight stretches: the first measures 1 1/4 inches, and the second measures 2 inches. He plans to leave at 3 in the morning.
problems.ask: How many miles long is the route?

problems.stem: Tariq ordered lunch from a café for a team meeting that ran 60 minutes. The order was six sandwich boxes at $13 each plus a fruit tray for $6. Sales tax is 5%, and he added a 20% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the lunch order, including tax and tip?

problems.stem: Maya needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. She plans to pick up the car at 7:30 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $39 more up front.
Company B costs $0.15 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.15.

problems.stem: June just started a dog-walking business. She moves $19 into savings the first week, and each week after that she moves $5 more than the week before. She has 9 regular customers.
problems.ask: How much will June have set aside in all after 19 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 19, week 2 with week 18, and so on: each pair adds to $19 + $109 = $128.
With 19 weeks, the average week is $128 ÷ 2 = $64, so the total is 19 × $64 = $1,216.

problems.stem: A garden hose at the local store is marked $36. Ezra decides to buy it, and 8% sales tax is added at checkout.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the garden hose, including tax?

problems.stem: On a trip to Mexico, Nadia exchanges money at a rate of 20 pesos per U.S. dollar. At an outdoor market, she buys a painted bowl for 420 pesos and a straw hat for 540 pesos. She has eight days left on the trip.
problems.ask: How much did Nadia spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Diego's chemistry grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and his average so far. There are 31 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Diego need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 85?
steps: To finish at 85, the final must add 85 − 59.2 = 25.8 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 25.8 ÷ 0.3 = 86.

problems.stem: Sofia surveyed the students in her grade about their favorite school lunch. Each student picked exactly one option, and the table shows the results. She collected the answers over five days.
problems.ask: What percent of the students surveyed did not choose "Tacos"?

problems.stem: Elena drove 120 miles to visit her aunt and averaged 60 miles per hour on the way there. Coming home on the same roads, heavy traffic held her to an average of 30 miles per hour. Her car gets about 30 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: What was Elena's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 240 ÷ 6 = 40 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Jordan leans a 26-foot ladder against the side of his house to clean the gutters. For safety, the bottom of the ladder sits 10 feet out from the wall, on level ground. The ladder is rated to hold 225 pounds.
problems.ask: How high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach, in feet?
steps: The wall, the ground and the ladder form a right triangle, with the ladder as the hypotenuse.

problems.stem: Owen is eight times as old as his grandson, Jamal. Every summer the two of them go fishing at a lake 9 miles from home. Exactly 2 years ago, Owen was ten times as old as Jamal.
problems.ask: How old is Owen now, in years?
steps: Let Jamal's age now be x, so Owen is 8x.
Move the x terms to one side: 2x = 20 − 2 = 18, so x = 9.
So Owen is 8 × 9 = 72 years old now. Check: 2 years ago, 70 = 10 × 7.

problems.stem: At 9:20 a.m., Felix started a volunteer shift at the library. The shift ended at 12:40 p.m., and he walked home.
problems.ask: How many minutes long was the shift?
steps: From 9:20 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 40 minutes.
From 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. is 2 hours, or 120 minutes.
From 12:00 p.m. to 12:40 p.m. is 40 minutes.

problems.stem: Rosa is sealing a rectangular concrete patio that is 19 feet long and 16 feet wide. One gallon of sealer covers 50 square feet, and it needs 48 hours to dry. Sealer is sold only by the whole gallon.
problems.ask: How many gallons must Rosa buy to give the patio one coat?
steps: 6 gallons cover 6 × 50 = 300 square feet, which is not enough.
7 gallons cover 350 square feet, so Rosa needs 7 gallons.

problems.stem: Tess bought a rectangular glass aquarium that is 36 inches long, 12 inches wide and 24 inches tall. She plans to keep ten small fish in it. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the aquarium hold when completely full?
steps: Convert to feet (÷ 12): 36 in = 3 ft, 12 in = 1 ft, 24 in = 2 ft.

problems.stem: Chloe mixed 16 cups of fruit punch that is 10% juice for a party. It tastes too sweet, so she wants to add water until the punch is only 8% juice. Twenty guests are coming.
problems.ask: How many cups of water should Chloe add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 8% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 10/8 = 5/4: 16 × 5/4 = 20 cups.

problems.stem: Andre buys 28 stamps at the post office: some 60-cent postcard stamps and some 75-cent letter stamps. He spends $17.25 in all. There are 9 people in line behind him.
problems.ask: How many letter stamps does Andre buy?
steps: Suppose all 28 were postcard stamps: 28 × 60 cents = 1,680 cents.
The real total is 1,725 cents, which is 1,725 cents − 1,680 cents = 45 cents more.
Each letter stamp adds 15 cents more than a postcard stamp, so there are 45 cents ÷ 15 cents = 3 letter stamps (check: 3 × 15 cents = 45 cents).

problems.stem: Leah and four friends go bowling. The lanes cost $66 for the night, and shoe rentals add $22.50. They split the total evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Leah plus four others makes 5 people.

problems.stem: Ravi is buying snacks for his family at a baseball game. The snack bar's prices, tax included, are in the table. Their seats are in row 14. Ravi orders three hot dogs, two lemonades, and two bottles of water.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Ravi's order?

problems.stem: June is making trail mix for a weekend hike. Her recipe mixes peanuts, raisins and chocolate chips in the ratio 5:6:1 by weight. She wants 60 ounces of trail mix in all, which she'll pack into six bags.
problems.ask: How many more ounces of peanuts than chocolate chips will the mix contain?
steps: Peanuts minus chocolate chips: 5 − 1 = 4 parts, and 4 × 5 = 20 ounces.

problems.stem: At the warehouse where Jade works, the 30 workers on the day shift packed an average of 72 boxes each on Monday. The 10 workers on the night shift, which started at midnight, packed an average of 62 boxes each.
problems.ask: What was the average number of boxes packed per worker across both shifts?

problems.stem: At a burrito stand, customers build a burrito bowl by choosing exactly 2 different fillings from a list of 7. Every burrito bowl also gets one of 2 bases: white rice or brown rice. The stand serves about 200 bowls on a busy day. The order the fillings are chosen in doesn't matter.
problems.ask: How many different burrito bowls can a customer build?
steps: Pick 2 of 7 fillings: 7 × 6 = 42 ordered picks, ÷ 2 because order doesn't matter = 21 sets.
Each set can go with any of the 2 bases: 21 × 2 = 42 burrito bowls.

problems.stem: Imani shops at the farmers market on Saturday morning. She buys a jar of honey for $7.25, a loaf of sourdough for $6.25, and a pint of blueberries for $4.50. There's no sales tax, and she pays with a $20 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Imani get back?

problems.stem: Aiyana must be at work by 8:30 a.m. for a meeting. She walks 15 minutes to the train station, rides the train for 25 minutes, and then walks 5 minutes to the office. A train ticket costs $2.75, and a train leaves the moment she reaches the platform. It is 7:10 a.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Aiyana wait before leaving home?
steps: From 7:10 a.m. to 8:30 a.m. is 80 minutes.

problems.stem: Caleb's home internet bill used to be $50 a month. After he upgraded his plan, the monthly bill became $57.50. The new plan has a download speed of 300 megabits per second.
problems.ask: By what percent did Caleb's monthly internet bill increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $7.50 ÷ $50 = 3/20 = 0.15.
As a percent, that is an increase of 15%.

problems.stem: Diego asked every household on his street how many pets it has and recorded the results in the table. It took him three afternoons to reach everyone.
problems.ask: What is the median number of pets per household?
steps: With 18 values in order, the median is the average of the 9th and 10th values.
Running totals: through 0: 4, through 1: 5, through 2: 8, through 3: 10, through 4: 18.
Both fall in the row for 3 pets, so the median is 3 pets.

problems.stem: A community center asked 90 members which summer trips they would sign up for. The results are in the table. The "Hiking trip" and "Kayaking trip" counts include the members who signed up for both trips. The sign-up sheet was posted for 11 days.
problems.ask: How many members signed up for both trips?
steps: So the extra count is the 'both' group: 32 − 25 = 7.

problems.stem: Yuki has been waiting for a sale on a rain jacket that normally costs $60. This weekend the store has it marked 10% off.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the rain jacket, before tax?

problems.stem: Elena is driving 100 miles to her cousin's wedding, where she'll catch a ride home with family. Her car gets 20 miles per gallon, and gas costs $3.60 per gallon. Her car's tank holds 16 gallons.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the drive?

problems.stem: Ravi ran the ticket table for the drama club's spring play and sold 170 tickets in all. Adult tickets cost $12 and student tickets cost $7. The auditorium has 400 seats, and at the end of the night the cash box held $1,380 from ticket sales.
problems.ask: How many adult tickets did Ravi sell?
steps: If all 170 were student tickets, the total would be 170 × $7 = $1,190.
The actual total is $1,380 − $1,190 = $190 more than that.
Each adult ticket brings in $5 more than each student ticket, so adult tickets: $190 ÷ $5 = 38.

problems.stem: Ava has a recipe for a 6-inch round cake, but she wants to bake it in an 8-inch round pan instead, filled to the same depth. The oven is set to 350 degrees.
problems.ask: How many times the original recipe should Ava make to fill the bigger pan?

problems.stem: Andre and Jordan are 54 miles apart on the same highway and drive toward each other to meet for dinner. Andre drives at 65 miles per hour, and Jordan drives at 55 miles per hour. They leave at the same time. Andre's car holds 13 gallons of gas.
problems.ask: How many minutes after they leave do they meet?
steps: The gap closes at 65 + 55 = 120 miles per hour.

problems.stem: Zoe is reading a 300-page novel for her book club and has already read 220 pages. She plans to read 20 pages each day until she finishes.
problems.ask: How many more days will it take to finish the book?

problems.stem: Chloe is picking up sandwiches for the 9:30 a.m. volunteer shift at the food bank. The deli sells sandwiches in packs of 4 for $4.25, or one at a time for $1.25 each. Seventeen volunteers are on the list, and Chloe wants at least one sandwich per person. Leftovers are fine, but she can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Chloe can spend?
steps: 17 ÷ 4 = 4 full packs, with 1 person left over.

problems.stem: Jade bought a used car for $16,000. Her mechanic estimates that the car will lose 10% of its value each year, based on what it is worth at the start of that year. The car gets about 28 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: Using that estimate, what will the car be worth after 2 years?

problems.stem: In March, the hardware store where Felix works cut the price of a patio umbrella by 10%. In June, the store raised that new price by 50%. Felix has worked at the store for 6 months.
problems.ask: By what percent is the June price higher than the original price?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
135 is 35 above 100, so it is 35% higher.

problems.stem: At the school fair, a spinner has 10 equal sections, and two of them are marked Prize. Ruth trades 3 tickets for two spins.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Ruth lands on Prize at least once?
steps: Work with the opposite: one spin misses Prize with probability 8/10 = 4/5.

problems.stem: The bulk bin at the grocery store charges $15 for 3 pounds of trail mix. Tess wants 2 pounds for a camping trip.
problems.ask: At the same price per pound, how much will 2 pounds cost?

problems.stem: Theo works at a garden center for $12 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times his regular rate. He has worked there for 2 years. Last week he worked 48 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Theo earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $12 = $18 an hour, for 48 − 40 = 8 hours.

problems.stem: Nico is painting the four walls of his home office, which is 19 feet long, 13 feet wide and 8 feet high. He wants two coats on every wall. The door and windows take up 60 square feet that won't be painted. One gallon of paint covers 400 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $39 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Nico need to buy?
steps: Minus the door and windows: 512 − 60 = 452 square feet.
904 ÷ 400 ≈ 2.3, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

problems.stem: Algae is spreading across the pond on Ravi's farm. Right now it covers 15 square feet, and the area it covers doubles every 2 days. The pond is about 5 feet deep.
problems.ask: If it keeps doubling at this rate, how many square feet will the algae cover 10 days from now?

problems.stem: Raul keeps a tin of cookies on his desk. It holds 9 chocolate chip cookies and 8 oatmeal cookies, all the same size. The tin was a gift from his neighbor 5 years ago. Without looking, he takes out two cookies, one after the other, and doesn't put either back.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both cookies are the same kind?

bonus.stem: Nadia buys a notebook and a pen at the campus bookstore for $1.70 in total. The notebook costs exactly $1 more than the pen.
bonus.ask: How much does the pen cost?
steps: Call the price of the pen x, so the notebook costs x + $1.

problems.stem: Dmitri rode his bike to work four days this week. The rides took 22, 26, 25, and 23 minutes.
problems.ask: What was his average ride time, in minutes?

problems.stem: Theo is shopping for a pair of running shoes. The one he wants normally sells for $120, but it's on sale for 20% off. The cashier then applies an extra 25% off the sale price for new members. The store is 9 miles from his home.
problems.ask: How much does Theo pay for the pair of running shoes, before tax?
steps: 20% of $120 is $24, so the sale price is $120 − $24 = $96.
The extra 25% comes off $96, not the original price: 25% of $96 is $24.

problems.stem: Marcus is stocking up on peanut butter and compares the three jar sizes in the table. He goes through about two jars a month.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Ingrid's company asked its employees how they usually get to work. Each person gave one answer, shown in the table. The office parking lot has 120 spaces.
problems.ask: What percent of the employees surveyed chose either "Drive" or "Bike"?

problems.stem: Paige started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 3 miles per hour. Ben started running from the same spot 15 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 8 miles per hour. The path is 5 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Ben catch up to Paige?
steps: Head start: in 15 minutes (1/4 hour), Paige covers 3 × 1/4 = 0.75 miles.
Time to close the gap: 0.75 ÷ 5 = 3/20 hour = 9 minutes.

problems.stem: Amara is signing up for pottery classes at a local studio, which offers the two options in the table. Each class lasts 150 minutes.
problems.ask: How many classes in a month would make the two options cost exactly the same?
steps: Drop-in costs $10 more per class, so each class closes the gap by $10.
Check: $70 + 7 × $12 = $154 and $0 + 7 × $22 = $154, so the answer is 7 classes.

problems.stem: The clock at the train station has a face 3 feet across. While Noor waits on the platform, it reads 6:01. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 1 × 6 = 6 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 6 × 30 + 1 × 0.5 = 180.5 degrees past the 12.
That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 174.5 degrees.

problems.stem: Carmen is running a lemonade stand. She makes seven pitchers of lemonade, and each pitcher holds 8 cups. There are 4 cups in a quart.
problems.ask: How many quarts of lemonade does Carmen make?
steps: There are 4 cups in a quart: 56 ÷ 4 = 14 quarts.

problems.stem: Omar has taken three algebra tests this term and scored 84, 86, and 74. There are 32 students in the class, and one test is left. He wants his average on all four tests to be exactly 85.
problems.ask: What score does Omar need on the last test?
steps: An average of 85 over 4 tests means a total of 85 × 4 = 340.

problems.stem: Jade bought a pair of running shoes at a sporting-goods store during a 25%-off sale, and she also used a $10 coupon. The register took 25% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. Only three pairs in her size were left on the shelf. Before tax, Jade paid $89.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the shoes?
steps: $99 is what was left after 25% off, so it is 75% of the original price.

problems.stem: Ingrid and Yuki are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Ingrid could paint it in 2 hours, and Yuki could paint it in 3 hours. The fence is 150 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Ingrid does 1/2 of the fence and Yuki does 1/3.
Together: 1/2 + 1/3 = 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: Raul, who is 5 feet tall, stands on level ground and notices that his shadow is 8 feet long. At the same moment, the shadow of a nearby flagpole is 48 feet long. The flagpole was put up 32 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the flagpole, in feet?
steps: The sun hits both at the same angle, so height ÷ shadow is the same for the flagpole and Raul: 5 ÷ 8.
The flagpole's shadow is 48 ÷ 8 = 6 times as long as Raul's.
So the flagpole is 6 × 5 = 30 feet tall.

bonus.stem: Isaac is building a straight fence 115 feet long along the edge of his yard. He sets a post every 5 feet, with a post at each end.
bonus.ask: How many posts does Isaac need?
steps: There is one more post than gaps (count the end): 23 + 1 = 24.

problems.stem: Andre is covering a playroom floor with square foam mats that are 24 inches on each side. The room is a rectangle 12 feet long and 6 feet wide, and the mats fit exactly.
problems.ask: How many mats does Andre need?
steps: 24 inches is 2 feet. Along the length: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 mats.

problems.stem: Lucia bikes to work. She rides 12 miles on a bike path at a steady 12 miles per hour, then 2 miles through city streets at a steady 6 miles per hour. Her bike has 16 gears.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 12 ÷ 12 = 1 hour, which is 60 minutes.
Second part: 2 ÷ 6 = 1/3 hour, which is 20 minutes.

problems.stem: Nadia wants to buy a laptop at an electronics store. The price is $825 if she pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $75 down, then 10 monthly payments of $86. The laptop weighs about 4 pounds.
problems.ask: How much more would Nadia pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Sam mixed 4 liters of liquid plant food that is 20% concentrate. The label says seedlings need a mix that is only 8% concentrate, so he will dilute it with water. He is growing four trays of seedlings.
problems.ask: How many liters of water should Sam add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 8% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 20/8 = 5/2: 4 × 5/2 = 10 liters.

problems.stem: Raul runs a prize wheel at the school fair. The wheel has 8 equal sections, each equally likely to land on top, and a spin costs $3. The table shows what the sections pay. The fair runs for 8 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the prize wheel make per spin after paying out prizes?
steps: If each section came up once, the prizes would total 2 × $5 + 2 × $2 = $14.
The booth keeps $3 − $1.75 = $1.25 per spin on average.

bonus.stem: A row of 7 stepping stones crosses a creek. Diego starts on the bank, and each hop moves him forward one or two stones. He must end exactly on the last stone.
bonus.ask: In how many different ways can Diego hop from the bank to the last stone?
steps: To land on stone k, the last move came from k − 1 or k − 2, so ways(k) = ways(k − 1) + ways(k − 2).
Keep adding: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21. So stone 7 has 21 ways.

problems.stem: After a long hike, Nadia stops at a cafe for dinner. Her bill is $26.80 before tip. She always tips 15% of the bill.
problems.ask: How much does Nadia pay in all, including the tip?

problems.stem: A muffin recipe makes 18 muffins and uses 1/4 cup of sugar. Victor needs 27 muffins for a school bake sale. The muffins bake at 375 degrees for 20 minutes.
problems.ask: If he scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of sugar will he need?

problems.stem: Jordan's statistics grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and his average so far. There are 23 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Jordan need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 85?
steps: To finish at 85, the final must add 85 − 50.6 = 34.4 points.
The final is worth 40%, so the score needed is 34.4 ÷ 0.4 = 86.

problems.stem: Jamal is building a wooden garden gate shaped like a rectangle, 36 inches wide and 48 inches tall. To keep it from sagging, he will nail a straight brace from one corner to the opposite corner. The gate will hang on two hinges.
problems.ask: How long must the brace be, in inches?
steps: The brace is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs equal to the width and height.

problems.stem: Tess, Ezra, Lucia and three of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Tess, Ezra and Lucia are triplets and want to stand together, side by side. The photographer charges $50 for the session.
problems.ask: In how many different orders can the 6 of them line up?
steps: Glue the three into one block, leaving 4 units: 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24 orders.
Inside the block the three can be ordered 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 ways.

problems.stem: Nico is shopping for a new toaster and finds one priced at $60. The sales tax where he lives is 5%, added at the register.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the toaster, including tax?
steps: 10% of $60 is $6, so 5% is half of that: $3.

problems.stem: Marcus is planning a road trip to the coast with a paper map. On the map, 1 inch represents 50 miles. The route has two straight stretches: the first measures 3 1/2 inches, and the second measures 1 1/2 inches. He plans to leave at 5 in the morning.
problems.ask: How many miles long is the route?

problems.stem: Esme ordered lunch from a café for a team meeting that ran 90 minutes. The order was six sandwich boxes at $9 each plus a fruit tray for $6. Sales tax is 5%, and she added a 20% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the lunch order, including tax and tip?

problems.stem: At the warehouse where Owen works, the 7 workers on the day shift packed an average of 69 boxes each on Monday. The 18 workers on the night shift, which started at midnight, packed an average of 44 boxes each.
problems.ask: What was the average number of boxes packed per worker across both shifts?

problems.stem: Lena is saving for a new bike. She puts $16 in a jar the first week, and every week after that she puts in $1.50 more than the week before. She started the plan on her 15th birthday.
problems.ask: How much will Lena have saved in all after 10 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 10, week 2 with week 9, and so on: each pair adds to $16 + $29.50 = $45.50.

problems.stem: Omar is planting a rectangular vegetable garden that measures 10 feet by 5 feet. He wants a short fence around it to keep rabbits out. One 10-foot side runs along the shed wall, so it needs no fence.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Omar need?
steps: Fence the other 10-foot side and both 5-foot sides.

problems.stem: On a trip to Mexico, Jade exchanges money at a rate of 20 pesos per U.S. dollar. At an outdoor market, she buys a woven blanket for 280 pesos and a pair of sandals for 190 pesos. She has five days left on the trip.
problems.ask: How much did Jade spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Ruth's club ran a bake sale on Saturday morning. They sold cookies, brownies and muffins in the ratio 1:5:3, and they sold 90 items in all. Every item was priced at $1.50.
problems.ask: How many more brownies than cookies did the club sell?
steps: Brownies minus cookies: 5 − 1 = 4 parts, and 4 × 10 = 40 brownies.

problems.stem: Sam rode his bike 21 miles to a lake, mostly uphill, averaging 7 miles per hour. He rode home the same way, mostly downhill, at 21 miles per hour. He packed two bottles of water for the ride.
problems.ask: What was Sam's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 42 ÷ 4 = 10.5 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Sofia is eleven times as old as her grandson, Diego. Every summer the two of them go fishing at a lake 8 miles from home. Exactly 2 years ago, Sofia was sixteen times as old as Diego.
problems.ask: How old is Diego now, in years?
steps: Let Diego's age now be x, so Sofia is 11x.
Move the x terms to one side: 5x = 32 − 2 = 30, so x = 6.
So Diego is 6 years old now. Check: 2 years ago, 64 = 16 × 4.

problems.stem: At 4:15 p.m., Priya put a loaf of bread in the oven. She took it out at 5:30 p.m., when the crust was golden brown.
problems.ask: For how many minutes did the bread bake?
steps: From 4:15 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 45 minutes.
From 5:00 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. is 30 minutes.

problems.stem: Fatima is picking up breakfast for her study group at a coffee shop. The prices, which include tax, are in the table. The shop opens at 6:30 every morning. Fatima orders two bagels, two hot chocolates, and four drip coffees.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Fatima's order?

problems.stem: Luis built a rectangular backyard pond that is 12 feet long, 3 feet wide and 2.5 feet deep, and he stocked it with nine goldfish. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the pond hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Ben is ordering pizza for six friends. The pizzeria sells round pizzas in two sizes: a 10-inch small and a 12-inch large, where the size is the diameter. Both have the same crust and toppings.
problems.ask: The large pizza has how many times the area of the small pizza?

problems.stem: Kofi is organizing a chess league with 7 players this season. Every player will play every other player exactly twice during the regular season. Each match takes about 30 minutes.
problems.ask: How many matches will be played in the regular season?
steps: Each match is a pair of players. Each of the 7 players pairs with 6 others: 7 × 6 = 42.
That counts every pair twice, so divide by 2: 42 ÷ 2 = 21 pairs.

problems.stem: Sam and three friends order pizza for game night. The pizzas come to $38, and drinks and dessert add $9 more. They agree to split the total evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Sam plus three others makes 4 people.

problems.stem: Fatima is putting laminate flooring in a rectangular bedroom that measures 14 feet by 9 feet. Each box of flooring covers 24 square feet and weighs 31 pounds. The store sells only whole boxes.
problems.ask: Ignoring waste, how many boxes does Fatima need to buy?
steps: 5 boxes cover 5 × 24 = 120 square feet, which is not enough.
6 boxes cover 144 square feet, so Fatima needs 6 boxes.

problems.stem: Mei's home internet bill used to be $95 a month. After she upgraded her plan, the monthly bill became $133. The new plan has a download speed of 300 megabits per second.
problems.ask: By what percent did Mei's monthly internet bill increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $38 ÷ $95 = 2/5 = 0.4.
As a percent, that is an increase of 40%.

problems.stem: Elena ran the ticket table for the drama club's spring play and sold 177 tickets in all. Adult tickets cost $9 and student tickets cost $4. The auditorium has 350 seats, and at the end of the night the cash box held $1,123 from ticket sales.
problems.ask: How many student tickets did Elena sell?
steps: If all 177 were student tickets, the total would be 177 × $4 = $708.
The actual total is $1,123 − $708 = $415 more than that.
Each adult ticket brings in $5 more than each student ticket, so adult tickets: $415 ÷ $5 = 83.

problems.stem: Caleb's class kept track of how many books each student read over winter break, and the table shows the results. The school library lets each student borrow up to six books at a time.
problems.ask: What is the median number of books read over the break?
steps: With 20 values in order, the median is the average of the 10th and 11th values.
Running totals: through 0: 4, through 1: 9, through 2: 11, through 3: 12, through 4: 14, through 5: 20.
Both fall in the row for 2 books, so the median is 2 books.

problems.stem: Wes takes a 500-milligram dose of a medicine at 6:45 p.m. with a glass of water. The amount of the medicine in the body drops by half every 2 hours.
problems.ask: How many milligrams of the medicine are left in his body 4 hours after the dose?

problems.stem: Marcus and Leah start at opposite ends of a 5-mile lakeside path and walk toward each other. Marcus walks at 3 miles per hour, and Leah walks at 2 miles per hour. They leave at the same time. The lake is about 14 feet deep in the middle.
problems.ask: How many minutes after they leave do they meet?
steps: The gap closes at 3 + 2 = 5 miles per hour.

problems.stem: Kenji picks up school supplies before classes start. He buys a binder for $4.25, a pack of pens for $1.99, and a calculator for $9.75. There's no sales tax, and he pays with a $20 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Kenji get back?

problems.stem: Ezra is baking a cake for a birthday party, and it must be frosted by 1:45 p.m. when the guests arrive. Baking takes 40 minutes, cooling takes 45 minutes, and frosting takes 15 minutes, one after another. The cake will feed 17 people. It is 11:50 a.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Ezra wait before starting?
steps: From 11:50 a.m. to 1:45 p.m. is 115 minutes.

problems.stem: Arjun deposited $1,200 in a savings account that earns 3% interest, compounded once a year. He won't add or take out any money. The bank requires a $100 minimum balance.
problems.ask: How much will be in the account after 2 years?
steps: Year 1: 3% of $1,200 is $36, so the value goes to $1,200 + $36 = $1,236.

problems.stem: In March, the hardware store where Chloe works cut the price of a snow shovel by 25%. In June, the store raised that new price by 30%. Chloe has worked at the store for 40 months.
problems.ask: By what percent is the June price lower than the original price?
steps: Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
97.5 is 2.5 below 100, so it is 2.5% lower.

problems.stem: The drama club at Hana's school sold 62 tickets for its Saturday show. Adult tickets cost $10 and student tickets cost $6. Ticket sales came to $488 in all, and the auditorium has 300 seats.
problems.ask: How many adult tickets were sold?
steps: The real total is $488, which is $488 − $372 = $116 more.
Each adult ticket adds $4 more than a student ticket, so there are $116 ÷ $4 = 29 adult tickets.

problems.stem: The store is taking 40% off everything this week, including the desk lamp Rosa has had her eye on. Its regular price is $30.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the desk lamp, before tax?

problems.stem: Silas is picking up bagels for the team's 7:45 a.m. meeting. The bakery sells bagels in packs of 4 for $3.50, or one at a time for $1.25 each. Eighteen people are coming, and Silas wants at least one bagel per person. Leftovers are fine, but he can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Silas can spend?
steps: 18 ÷ 4 = 4 full packs, with 2 people left over.

problems.stem: Omar is painting the four walls of his bedroom, which is 16 feet long, 13 feet wide and 10 feet high. He wants two coats on every wall. The door and windows take up 60 square feet that won't be painted. One gallon of paint covers 400 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $32 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Omar need to buy?
steps: Minus the door and windows: 580 − 60 = 520 square feet.
1,040 ÷ 400 = 2.6, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

problems.stem: Hana started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 4 miles per hour. Hugo started running from the same spot 6 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 6 miles per hour. The path is 8 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Hugo catch up to Hana?
steps: Head start: in 6 minutes (1/10 hour), Hana covers 4 × 1/10 = 0.4 miles.
Time to close the gap: 0.4 ÷ 2 = 1/5 hour = 12 minutes.

problems.stem: In a board game, Tariq's piece is stuck in the jail space. Under the house rules, he rolls a standard six-sided die three times, and he escapes if any roll is a 5 or a 6. The board has 48 spaces in all.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Tariq escapes?
steps: Work with the opposite: one roll is not a 5 or a 6 with probability 4/6 = 2/3.

problems.stem: Lena is working on a 750-piece jigsaw puzzle. She has placed 625 pieces so far and places 25 more pieces each night.
problems.ask: How many more nights will it take to finish the puzzle?

problems.stem: Zoe works at a restaurant for $12 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times her regular rate. She has worked there for 5 years. Last week she worked five shifts of 10 hours each.
problems.ask: How much did Zoe earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $12 = $18 an hour, for 50 − 40 = 10 hours.

problems.stem: Silas works at the town library and asked visitors their main reason for coming in. Each visitor gave one answer, shown in the table. The library is open 48 hours a week.
problems.ask: What percent of the visitors surveyed did not choose "Use computers"?

problems.stem: Aiyana is signing up for pottery classes at a local studio, which offers the two options in the table. Each class lasts 90 minutes.
problems.ask: How many classes in a month would make the two options cost exactly the same?
steps: Drop-in costs $11 more per class, so each class closes the gap by $11.
Check: $55 + 5 × $10 = $105 and $0 + 5 × $21 = $105, so the answer is 5 classes.

problems.stem: A fruit bowl in Priya's kitchen holds 4 red apples and 8 green apples. She bought them at a farm stand that opened 22 years ago. On her way out the door, she grabs two apples at random, one after the other.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both apples are the same color?

bonus.stem: Raul's mudroom bin holds 6 pairs of black gloves and 6 pairs of brown gloves, all jumbled together. Each glove fits only a left hand or only a right hand. It's still dark when Raul heads out, so he grabs gloves without looking.
bonus.ask: What is the fewest gloves Raul must grab to be sure of getting a left and a right glove of the same color?
steps: Worst case: every glove he grabs is a left glove: 6 + 6 = 12 gloves, and still no match.
Now only right gloves are left, so the next one matches a left glove of its color: 12 + 1 = 13 gloves.

problems.stem: Yuki bowled four games at her league night on Saturday. Her scores were 119, 128, 126, and 123.
problems.ask: What was Yuki's average score for the four games?

problems.stem: A store is taking 50% off every pair of running shoes, and Diego finds one with a regular price of $140. He also has a member coupon that takes 20% off the already reduced price. The sale price is good for 12 more days.
problems.ask: How much does Diego pay for the pair of running shoes, before tax?
steps: 50% of $140 is $70, so the sale price is $140 − $70 = $70.
The extra 20% comes off $70, not the original price: 20% of $70 is $14.

problems.stem: Kenji is comparing three sizes of the same cereal, shown in the table. He eats about three ounces each morning.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Theo has 20 ounces of a cleaning spray that is 30% vinegar. For washing windows, he wants a weaker spray that is only 10% vinegar, so he'll add water. He has six windows to clean.
problems.ask: How many ounces of water should Theo add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 10% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 30/10 = 3: 20 × 3 = 60 ounces.

problems.stem: A café asked 64 regular customers which drinks they had ordered in the past month. The results are in the table. The "Iced coffee" and "Hot tea" counts include the customers who ordered both drinks. The café has 18 tables.
problems.ask: How many customers ordered both drinks?
steps: So the extra count is the 'both' group: 39 − 36 = 3.

problems.stem: Lena buys six cans of tomatoes for a big pot of chili. Each can holds 8 ounces, and there are 16 ounces in a pound.
problems.ask: How many pounds of tomatoes is that in all?
steps: There are 16 ounces in a pound: 48 ÷ 16 = 3 pounds.

problems.stem: Chloe is driving to a family reunion, which is 210 miles from home, and then driving back. Her car gets 35 miles per gallon, and gas costs $2.90 per gallon. Her car's tank holds 13 gallons.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the round trip?

problems.stem: Elena is mixing concrete for a garden path that is 20 feet long. Her mix uses cement, sand and gravel in the ratio 4:5:3 by volume. She needs 60 buckets of mix in all.
problems.ask: How many more buckets of cement than gravel does Elena need?
steps: Cement minus gravel: 4 − 3 = 1 part, and 1 × 5 = 5 buckets.

problems.stem: Theo and Marcus are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Theo could paint it in 2 hours, and Marcus could paint it in 6 hours. The fence is 120 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Theo does 1/2 of the fence and Marcus does 1/6.
Together: 1/2 + 1/6 = 3/6 + 1/6 = 4/6 = 2/3 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: The clock at the train station has a face 5 feet across. While Andre waits on the platform, it reads 8:16. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 16 × 6 = 96 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 8 × 30 + 16 × 0.5 = 248 degrees past the 12.
That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 152 degrees.

bonus.stem: Raul is stacking soup cans into a flat, triangle-shaped display in a store window. The bottom row has 15 cans, each row has one fewer can than the row below it, and the top row has 1 can.
bonus.ask: How many cans are in the display?
steps: Rows: from 1 up to 15 cans is 15 − 1 + 1 = 15 rows.
Pair the first and last rows, the second and second-to-last, and so on: each pair holds 1 + 15 = 16.
With 15 rows, the average row is 16 ÷ 2 = 8, so the total is 15 × 8 = 120 cans.

problems.stem: Caleb is tiling his kitchen floor, a rectangle 12 feet long and 6 feet wide. He is using square tiles that measure 24 inches on each side, and they fit exactly with no cutting.
problems.ask: How many tiles does Caleb need?
steps: 24 inches is 2 feet. Along the length: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 tiles.

problems.stem: Silas bowls in a league with 17 teams. So far this season he has bowled four games, scoring 166, 167, 184, and 150. He wants his average after the next game to be exactly 180.
problems.ask: What score does Silas need in the next game?
steps: An average of 180 over 5 games means a total of 180 × 5 = 900.

problems.stem: Maya bought a pair of running shoes at a sporting-goods store during a 20%-off sale, and she also used a $5 coupon. The register took 20% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. Only five pairs in her size were left on the shelf. Before tax, Maya paid $55.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the shoes?
steps: $60 is what was left after 20% off, so it is 80% of the original price.

problems.stem: Tariq paddled a kayak 8 miles upstream at 2 miles per hour, then turned around and paddled the same 8 miles back downstream at 8 miles per hour. His kayak is 14 feet long.
problems.ask: What was Tariq's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 16 ÷ 5 = 3.2 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: Paige runs a prize wheel at the school fair. The wheel has 20 equal sections, each equally likely to land on top, and a spin costs $2. The table shows what the sections pay. The fair runs for 4 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the prize wheel make per spin after paying out prizes?
steps: If each section came up once, the prizes would total 2 × $10 + 3 × $2 = $26.
The booth keeps $2 − $1.30 = $0.70 per spin on average.

problems.stem: Maya and two coworkers stop at a diner for breakfast, and Maya offers to pay. The check is $71.40. She plans to add a 15% tip on the full check.
problems.ask: How much does Maya pay in all, including the tip?

problems.stem: Chloe bikes to work. She rides 9 miles on a bike path at a steady 15 miles per hour, then 2 miles through city streets at a steady 8 miles per hour. The bike path has 17 benches along the way.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 9 ÷ 15 = 3/5 hour, which is 36 minutes.
Second part: 2 ÷ 8 = 1/4 hour, which is 15 minutes.

problems.stem: Ava's economics grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and her average so far. There are 19 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Ava need on the final exam to finish with exactly a 90?
steps: To finish at 90, the final must add 90 − 60.9 = 29.1 points.
The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 29.1 ÷ 0.3 = 97.

problems.stem: Ben built a rectangular backyard pond that is 12 feet long, 5 feet wide and 2.5 feet deep, and he stocked it with fifteen goldfish. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the pond hold when completely full?

problems.stem: A rectangular park near Dmitri's apartment is 480 meters long and 140 meters wide. Dmitri usually walks along two edges to get from one corner to the opposite corner. Today he cuts straight across the grass on the diagonal instead. The park has 20 benches.
problems.ask: How many meters shorter is the diagonal route than the route along the two edges?
steps: Shrink the numbers first: 480 = 20 × 24 and 140 = 20 × 7. Since 24² + 7² = 576 + 49 = 625 = 25², the diagonal is 20 × 25 = 500 meters.

problems.stem: Tariq's class kept track of how many books each student read over winter break, and the table shows the results. The school library lets each student borrow up to six books at a time.
problems.ask: What is the median number of books read over the break?
steps: With 23 values in order, the median is the 12th value.
Running totals: through 0: 4, through 1: 10, through 2: 15, through 3: 18, through 4: 19, through 5: 23.
The 12th value falls in the row for 2 books, so the median is 2 books.

problems.stem: Malik, Marcus and two of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Malik and Marcus keep making each other laugh, so they can't stand side by side. The photographer charges $50 for the session.
problems.ask: In how many different orders can the 4 of them line up?
steps: Orders with them together: glue them into a block, 3 × 2 × 1 = 6, times 2 for their order = 12.

problems.stem: Sofia is shopping for a new toaster and finds one priced at $46. The sales tax where she lives is 7%, added at the register.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the toaster, including tax?

problems.stem: Lena's pancake recipe makes 16 pancakes and calls for 1 1/2 cups of flour. She is making 8 pancakes for a family brunch. The recipe says to cook each pancake for 2 minutes per side.
problems.ask: If she scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of flour will she need?

problems.stem: Nadia and one friends went out for dinner and waited 30 minutes for a table. They ordered two entrées at $21 each and one appetizer to share for $11. Sales tax is 5%, and they added a 20% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the dinner, including tax and tip?

problems.stem: Priya teaches two sections of algebra. On Friday's test, the 9 students in her first-period class averaged 62 points, and the 21 students in her fourth-period class averaged 77 points. The test had 20 questions.
problems.ask: What was the average score for all of the students in both classes together, in points?

problems.stem: Theo, who is 5 feet tall, stands on level ground and notices that his shadow is 9 feet long. At the same moment, the shadow of a nearby oak tree is 72 feet long. The tree was planted about 32 years ago.
problems.ask: How tall is the oak tree, in feet?
steps: The sun hits both at the same angle, so height ÷ shadow is the same for the oak tree and Theo: 5 ÷ 9.
The oak tree's shadow is 72 ÷ 9 = 8 times as long as Theo's.
So the oak tree is 8 × 5 = 40 feet tall.

bonus.stem: Diego's grandfather clock strikes once for each hour, with the strikes evenly spaced. At 5 o'clock, it takes 4 seconds from the first strike to the last.
bonus.ask: How many seconds does it take from the first strike to the last at 10 o'clock?
steps: 5 strikes have only 4 gaps between them, so each gap is 4 ÷ 4 = 1 second.

problems.stem: A farm stand sells a 6-pound bag of apples for $7.50. Esme wants 10 pounds for pies, and the stand will weigh out any amount at the same price per pound.
problems.ask: How much will 10 pounds of apples cost?

problems.stem: Tariq is mapping out a bike ride. On the town's trail map, 1 inch stands for 4 miles. The ride follows the river trail for 2 3/4 inches on the map, then the park loop for 2 1/4 inches. The trail map shows 10 drinking fountains.
problems.ask: How many miles long is the ride?

problems.stem: Luis wants to buy a couch at a furniture store. The price is $691 if he pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $50 down, then 24 monthly payments of $34. The couch is 90 inches long.
problems.ask: How much more would Luis pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Lena is ordering pizza for four friends. The pizzeria sells round pizzas in two sizes: a 16-inch small and an 18-inch large, where the size is the diameter. Both have the same crust and toppings.
problems.ask: The large pizza has how many times the area of the small pizza?

problems.stem: Malik's robotics club runs a weekly bake sale. In week 1 the club sets aside $11 for a trip, and each week after that it sets aside $1 more than the week before. The club has 22 members this year.
problems.ask: How much will the club have set aside in all after 14 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 14, week 2 with week 13, and so on: each pair adds to $11 + $24 = $35.

bonus.stem: A beetle starts at the bottom of a 25-foot garden wall. Every day it crawls 3 feet up, and every night it slides back down 1 foot. Andre checks on it each morning.
bonus.ask: On which day does the beetle first reach the top of the wall, if the first day of climbing is day 1?
steps: Each full day and night, the beetle gains 3 − 1 = 2 feet.
On its last day it climbs 3 feet and never slides back, so it only needs to start that day at 25 − 3 = 22 feet.
Reaching 22 feet takes 22 ÷ 2 = 11 full days and nights.
It reaches the top on day 11 + 1 = 12.

problems.stem: June is fencing in a rectangular play area for her kids. The area is 18 feet long and 14 feet wide. She'll fence all four sides.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does June need?
steps: One length plus one width: 18 + 14 = 32 feet.
Going all the way around doubles that: 2 × 32 = 64 feet.

problems.stem: Paige is picking up breakfast for her study group at a coffee shop. The prices, which include tax, are in the table. The shop opens at 6:30 every morning. Paige orders three bagels, three drip coffees, and two hot chocolates.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Paige's order?

problems.stem: Mateo helped run a pancake breakfast at the fire station. Adult plates cost $8 and kids' plates cost $5. They served 102 plates and took in $630, with nine volunteers working the griddles.
problems.ask: How many kids' plates did they serve?
steps: If all 102 were kids' plates, the total would be 102 × $5 = $510.
The actual total is $630 − $510 = $120 more than that.
Each adult plate brings in $3 more than each kids' plate, so adult plates: $120 ÷ $3 = 40.

problems.stem: Luis is studying a 320-gram sample of a radioactive substance in a lab. The substance has a half-life of 12 days, which means half of whatever is left decays every 12 days. The sample is stored in a case that weighs 12 pounds.
problems.ask: How many days will it take until only 20 grams of the substance remain?
steps: Halve until 20 grams remain: 320 → 160 → 80 → 40 → 20. That is 4 halvings.

problems.stem: Arjun is organizing a volleyball league with 9 teams this season. Every team will play every other team exactly once during the regular season. Each game takes about 30 minutes.
problems.ask: How many games will be played in the regular season?
steps: Each game is a pair of teams. Each of the 9 teams pairs with 8 others: 9 × 8 = 72.
That counts every pair twice, so divide by 2: 72 ÷ 2 = 36 pairs.
Each pair plays once, so there are 36 games.

problems.stem: Hugo's movie started at 1:05 p.m., and the credits began rolling at 3:15 p.m. as he headed for the exit.
problems.ask: How many minutes long was the movie, from start to credits?
steps: From 1:05 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. is 55 minutes.
From 2:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 1 hour, or 60 minutes.
From 3:00 p.m. to 3:15 p.m. is 15 minutes.

problems.stem: On a trip to Mexico, Sofia exchanges money at a rate of 20 pesos per U.S. dollar. At an outdoor market, she buys a painted bowl for 630 pesos and a straw hat for 220 pesos. She has nine days left on the trip.
problems.ask: How much did Sofia spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Eli has been watching a mountain bike at a sporting-goods store. It was priced at $550, and this week the store marked it down to $275. The sale ends in 10 days.
problems.ask: By what percent was the price of the bike reduced?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $275 ÷ $550 = 1/2 = 0.5.
As a percent, that is a decrease of 50%.

problems.stem: Jamal started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 3 miles per hour. Omar started running from the same spot 10 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 5 miles per hour. The path is 8 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting to run did Omar catch up to Jamal?
steps: Head start: in 10 minutes (1/6 hour), Jamal covers 3 × 1/6 = 0.5 miles.
Time to close the gap: 0.5 ÷ 2 = 1/4 hour = 15 minutes.

problems.stem: Mateo is four times as old as his nephew, Marcus. This spring they planted 25 tomato plants together. In 20 years, Mateo will be twice as old as Marcus.
problems.ask: How old is Mateo now, in years?
steps: Let Marcus's age now be x, so Mateo is 4x.
Subtract 2x and 20 from both sides: 2x = 40 − 20 = 20, so x = 10.
So Mateo is 4 × 10 = 40 years old now. Check: in 20 years, 60 = 2 × 30.

problems.stem: Zoe and five friends go bowling. The lanes cost $48 for the night, and shoe rentals add $12. They split the total evenly.
problems.ask: How much does each person pay?
steps: Zoe plus five others makes 6 people.

problems.stem: Theo is putting laminate flooring in a rectangular bedroom that measures 11 feet by 8 feet. Each box of flooring covers 25 square feet and weighs 37 pounds. The store sells only whole boxes.
problems.ask: Ignoring waste, how many boxes does Theo need to buy?
steps: 3 boxes cover 3 × 25 = 75 square feet, which is not enough.
4 boxes cover 100 square feet, so Theo needs 4 boxes.

problems.stem: Ezra bought a used car for $8,000. His mechanic estimates that the car will lose 20% of its value each year, based on what it is worth at the start of that year. The car gets about 34 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: Using that estimate, what will the car be worth after 2 years?

problems.stem: Malik is writing a report about his town. Its population grew by 20% from 2016 to 2020, then shrank by 25% from 2020 to 2024. The town has 15 public parks.
problems.ask: By what percent is the 2024 population lower than the 2016 population?
steps: Start with a population of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
90 is 10 below 100, so it is 10% lower.

problems.stem: The drama club at Mateo's school sold 66 tickets for its Saturday show. Adult tickets cost $9 and student tickets cost $5. Ticket sales came to $382 in all, and the auditorium has 350 seats.
problems.ask: How many adult tickets were sold?
steps: The real total is $382, which is $382 − $330 = $52 more.
Each adult ticket adds $4 more than a student ticket, so there are $52 ÷ $4 = 13 adult tickets.

problems.stem: Kofi has been waiting for a sale on a board game that normally costs $25. This weekend the store has it marked 30% off.
problems.ask: What is the sale price of the board game, before tax?

problems.stem: Jade is baking a cake for a birthday party, and it must be frosted by 4:00 p.m. when the guests arrive. Baking takes 40 minutes, cooling takes 50 minutes, and frosting takes 20 minutes, one after another. The cake will feed 17 people. It is 1:30 p.m. now.
problems.ask: At most, how many minutes can Jade wait before starting?
steps: From 1:30 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 150 minutes.

problems.stem: Caleb is painting the four walls of his living room, which is 15 feet long, 12 feet wide and 9 feet high. He wants two coats on every wall. The door and windows take up 50 square feet that won't be painted. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $39 a gallon.
problems.ask: If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Caleb need to buy?
steps: Minus the door and windows: 486 − 50 = 436 square feet.
872 ÷ 350 ≈ 2.5, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

problems.stem: Lucia needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. She plans to pick up the car at 9:15 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $15 more up front.
Company B costs $0.10 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.10.

problems.stem: Mateo and Jamal are 85 miles apart on the same highway and drive toward each other to meet for dinner. Mateo drives at 50 miles per hour, and Jamal drives at 40 miles per hour. Jamal leaves 30 minutes after Mateo. Mateo's car holds 11 gallons of gas.
problems.ask: How many minutes after Mateo leaves do they meet?
steps: Head start: in 30 minutes, Mateo covers 50 × 1/2 = 25 miles.
Distance left when Jamal leaves: 85 − 25 = 60 miles.
Together they close 50 + 40 = 90 miles per hour: 60 ÷ 90 = 2/3 hour = 40 minutes after Jamal leaves.
Counting from when Mateo leaves: 30 + 40 = 70 minutes.

problems.stem: Kofi shops at the farmers market on Saturday morning. He buys a jar of honey for $6.50, a loaf of sourdough for $5.75, and a pint of blueberries for $4.50. There's no sales tax, and he pays with a $20 bill.
problems.ask: How much change should Kofi get back?

problems.stem: A store is taking 20% off every stand mixer, and Paige finds one with a regular price of $180. She also has a member coupon that takes 10% off the already reduced price. The sale ends in 12 days.
problems.ask: How much does Paige pay for the stand mixer, before tax?
steps: 20% of $180 is $36, so the sale price is $180 − $36 = $144.
The extra 10% comes off $144, not the original price: 10% of $144 is $14.40.

problems.stem: Owen works at the town library and asked visitors their main reason for coming in. Each visitor gave one answer, shown in the table. The library is open 64 hours a week.
problems.ask: What percent of the visitors surveyed chose either "Borrow books" or "Attend events"?

problems.stem: Amara's club ran a bake sale on Saturday morning. They sold cookies, brownies and muffins in the ratio 3:2:5, and they sold 120 items in all. Every item was priced at $2.
problems.ask: How many muffins did the club sell?

problems.stem: Maya and Jordan are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Maya could paint it in 10 hours, and Jordan could paint it in 15 hours. The fence is 120 feet long.
problems.ask: If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
steps: In one hour, Maya does 1/10 of the fence and Jordan does 1/15.
Together: 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6 of the fence per hour.

problems.stem: A rectangular park near Malik's apartment is 400 meters long and 300 meters wide. Malik usually walks along two edges to get from one corner to the opposite corner. Today he cuts straight across the grass on the diagonal instead. The park has 19 benches.
problems.ask: How many meters shorter is the diagonal route than the route along the two edges?
steps: Shrink the numbers first: 400 = 100 × 4 and 300 = 100 × 3. Since 4² + 3² = 16 + 9 = 25 = 5², the diagonal is 100 × 5 = 500 meters.

problems.stem: Hugo and his brother flip a coin each night to decide who washes the dinner dishes; heads means Hugo washes. This week they'll flip for four nights in a row. Dinner is usually ready by 7:00 each evening.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that Hugo washes the dishes at least once in those 4 nights?
steps: Work with the opposite: Hugo never washes only if every flip is tails. One flip is tails with probability 1/2.

problems.stem: Rosa is reading a 270-page novel for her book club and has already read 110 pages. She plans to read 20 pages each day until she finishes.
problems.ask: How many more days will it take to finish the book?

problems.stem: Tess is picking up bagels for the team's 8 a.m. meeting. The bakery sells bagels in packs of 6 for $6, or one at a time for $1.25 each. 22 people are coming, and Tess wants at least one bagel per person. Leftovers are fine, but she can't split a pack.
problems.ask: What is the least Tess can spend?
steps: 22 ÷ 6 = 3 full packs, with 4 people left over.

problems.stem: Imani built a rectangular backyard pond that is 8 feet long, 3 feet wide and 1.5 feet deep, and she stocked it with nine goldfish. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water.
problems.ask: Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the pond hold when completely full?

problems.stem: Esme mixed 11 liters of liquid plant food that is 10% concentrate. The label says seedlings need a mix that is only 4% concentrate, so she will dilute it with water. She is growing five trays of seedlings.
problems.ask: How many liters of water should Esme add?
steps: Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 4% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 10/4 = 5/2: 11 × 5/2 = 27.5 liters.

problems.stem: A fruit bowl in Mateo's kitchen holds 9 red apples and 8 green apples. He bought them at a farm stand that opened 32 years ago. On his way out the door, he grabs two apples at random, one after the other.
problems.ask: What is the probability, as a fraction, that both apples are the same color?

bonus.stem: Ben is laying a 3-by-3 patio of square tiles, all the same size. Looking at the grid lines, Ben wonders how many squares can be traced, counting every size, from single tiles up to the biggest square that fits.
bonus.ask: How many squares of all sizes are in the 3-by-3 grid?
steps: A k-by-k square can start in 3 − k + 1 spots across and the same number down, so there are (3 − k + 1)² of them.

problems.stem: Mei spends a rainy Saturday watching a baking show. She watches nine episodes, and each one is 25 minutes long.
problems.ask: How many hours of the show does Mei watch?
steps: There are 60 minutes in an hour: 225 ÷ 60 = 3.75 hours.

problems.stem: Carmen works at a bike shop for $12 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times her regular rate. She has worked there for 2 years. Last week she worked 48 hours.
problems.ask: How much did Carmen earn last week, before taxes?
steps: Overtime rate: 1.5 × $12 = $18 an hour, for 48 − 40 = 8 hours.

problems.stem: Nico's world history grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and his average so far. There are 32 students in the class, and only the final exam is left.
problems.ask: What score does Nico need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 88?
steps: To finish at 88, the final must add 88 − 50 = 38 points.
The final is worth 40%, so the score needed is 38 ÷ 0.4 = 95.

problems.stem: Lena drove 120 miles to visit her aunt and averaged 60 miles per hour on the way there. Coming home on the same roads, heavy traffic held her to an average of 40 miles per hour. Her car gets about 28 miles per gallon.
problems.ask: What was Lena's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

problems.stem: A community center asked 60 members which summer trips they would sign up for. The results are in the table. The "Hiking trip" and "Kayaking trip" counts include the members who signed up for both trips. The sign-up sheet was posted for 9 days.
problems.ask: How many of the 60 members signed up for neither trip?

problems.stem: Lena is tracking how long she practices piano. From Monday to Friday, she practiced 22, 29, 36, 38, and 30 minutes.
problems.ask: What was her average practice time per day, in minutes?

problems.stem: Maya is driving 300 miles to a family reunion, where she'll catch a ride home with family. Her car gets 25 miles per gallon, and gas costs $3.40 per gallon. Her car's tank holds 14 gallons.
problems.ask: How much will gas cost for the drive?

problems.stem: Hana's swim team held a car wash to raise money. They charged $7 for each car and $11 for each truck or SUV. Over four hours on Saturday, they washed 95 vehicles and collected $885.
problems.ask: How many cars did the team wash?
steps: If all 95 were cars, the total would be 95 × $7 = $665.
The actual total is $885 − $665 = $220 more than that.
Each truck or SUV brings in $4 more than each car, so trucks and SUVs: $220 ÷ $4 = 55.

problems.stem: Jordan's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 60 minutes.
problems.ask: What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
steps: With 39 values in order, the median is the 20th value.
Running totals: through 0: 7, through 1: 11, through 2: 19, through 3: 26, through 4: 33, through 5: 39.
The 20th value falls in the row for 3 goals, so the median is 3 goals.

problems.stem: Nico snaps a photo of the clock tower in the town square at exactly 12:27. The tower is 91 feet tall. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass.
problems.ask: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
steps: The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 27 × 6 = 162 degrees past the 12.
The hour hand moves 0.5 degree per minute, starting at the 12: 27 × 0.5 = 13.5 degrees past the 12.
That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 148.5 degrees.

bonus.stem: Before a chess tournament, each of the 18 players shakes hands with every other player once. Kenji, the organizer, just watches.
bonus.ask: How many handshakes are there in all?
steps: Each of the 18 players takes part in 17 handshakes: 18 × 17 = 306.
That counts every one twice (once for each person in it), so divide by 2: 306 ÷ 2 = 153.

problems.stem: Sofia orders takeout noodles and dumplings for the family. The order comes to $62.20, and she adds a 20% tip for the delivery driver.
problems.ask: How much does Sofia pay in all, including the tip?

problems.stem: Lena bowls in a league with 20 teams. So far this season she has bowled three games, scoring 172, 191, and 200. She wants her average after the next game to be exactly 180.
problems.ask: What score does Lena need in the next game?
steps: An average of 180 over 4 games means a total of 180 × 4 = 720.

problems.stem: Raul buys a monthly bus pass. Last year the pass cost $65, and this year the transit agency raised the price to $84.50. He rides the bus about 19 days a month.
problems.ask: By what percent did the price of the bus pass increase?
steps: Compare it with the original price: $19.50 ÷ $65 = 3/10 = 0.3.
As a percent, that is an increase of 30%.

problems.stem: Tess's living room has a round rug that is 6 feet across. She wants to replace it with a round rug that is 10 feet across. The room is 18 feet long.
problems.ask: The new rug will cover how many times as much floor area as the old rug?

problems.stem: Diego, Victor and two of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Diego and Victor are twins and insist on standing next to each other. The photographer charges $40 for the session.
problems.ask: In how many different orders can the 4 of them line up?
steps: Glue Diego and Victor into one block, leaving 3 units to arrange.
Inside the block they can switch places: 6 × 2 = 12.

problems.stem: A garden hose at the local store is marked $44. Andre decides to buy it, and 6% sales tax is added at checkout.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of the garden hose, including tax?

problems.stem: Tariq bikes to work. He rides 5 miles on a bike path at a steady 15 miles per hour, then 2 miles through city streets at a steady 6 miles per hour. His office is on the third floor.
problems.ask: How many minutes does the whole trip take?
steps: First part: 5 ÷ 15 = 1/3 hour, which is 20 minutes.
Second part: 2 ÷ 6 = 1/3 hour, which is 20 minutes.

problems.stem: Jamal is stocking up on peanut butter and compares the three jar sizes in the table. He goes through about two jars a month.
problems.ask: What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per ounce among the three sizes?

problems.stem: Nadia is studying an 800-gram sample of a radioactive substance in a lab. The substance has a half-life of 10 days, which means half of whatever is left decays every 10 days. The sample is stored in a case that weighs 12 pounds.
problems.ask: How many days will it take until only 100 grams of the substance remain?
steps: Halve until 100 grams remain: 800 → 400 → 200 → 100. That is 3 halvings.

problems.stem: Sam runs a prize wheel at the school fair. The wheel has 12 equal sections, each equally likely to land on top, and a spin costs $5. The table shows what the sections pay. The fair runs for 4 hours.
problems.ask: On average, how much money does the prize wheel make per spin after paying out prizes?
steps: If each section came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $20 + 2 × $2 = $24.
The booth keeps $5 − $2 = $3 per spin on average.

problems.stem: Diego is sewing curtains. The fabric he likes costs $16.50 for 3 yards, and the shop sells it by the yard at that same rate. He needs 12 yards.
problems.ask: How much will the fabric cost?

problems.stem: A smoothie recipe makes 8 servings and calls for 1 1/4 cups of plain yogurt. Lena is making 16 servings for her soccer team after practice. The yogurt was on sale for $4 a tub.
problems.ask: If she scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of yogurt will she need?

problems.stem: Jordan bought a pair of running shoes at a sporting-goods store during a 20%-off sale, and he also used a $10 coupon. The register took 20% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. Only four pairs in his size were left on the shelf. Before tax, Jordan paid $106.
problems.ask: What was the original price of the shoes?
steps: $116 is what was left after 20% off, so it is 80% of the original price.

problems.stem: Caleb's running club timed its members in a 5-kilometer race. The 8 runners in the morning group averaged 25 minutes, and the 12 runners in the evening group averaged 30 minutes. The course had four water stations.
problems.ask: What was the average time for all the runners in both groups, in minutes?

problems.stem: Felix, who is 6 feet tall, stands on level ground in the shadow of a light pole, 38 feet from its base. His own shadow is 8 feet long and points the same way, and its tip lands exactly on the tip of the light pole's shadow. The parking lot around it has 13 spaces.
problems.ask: How tall is the light pole, in feet?
steps: The light pole's shadow runs past Felix to the same tip: 38 + 8 = 46 feet long.
Same sun angle, so height ÷ shadow matches: 6 ÷ 8 for Felix.
Height of the light pole = 46 × 6 ÷ 8 = 276 ÷ 8 = 34.5 feet.

problems.stem: Sofia is covering a playroom floor with square foam mats that are 24 inches on each side. The room is a rectangle 18 feet long and 10 feet wide, and the mats fit exactly.
problems.ask: How many mats does Sofia need?
steps: 24 inches is 2 feet. Along the length: 18 ÷ 2 = 9 mats.

problems.stem: Zoe is planning a road trip to the coast with a paper map. On the map, 1 inch represents 25 miles. The route has two straight stretches: the first measures 3 3/4 inches, and the second measures 2 3/4 inches. She plans to leave at 4 in the morning.
problems.ask: How many miles long is the route?

problems.stem: Hana ordered lunch from a café for a team meeting that ran 60 minutes. The order was six sandwich boxes at $9 each plus a fruit tray for $8. Sales tax is 5%, and she added a 20% tip figured on the food cost before tax.
problems.ask: What was the total cost of the lunch order, including tax and tip?

problems.stem: Ravi surveyed the students in his grade about their favorite school lunch. Each student picked exactly one option, and the table shows the results. He collected the answers over five days.
problems.ask: What percent of the students surveyed chose "Pasta"?

problems.stem: Lena set out on her bike along the river trail, riding at a steady 10 miles per hour. Grace left from the same spot 30 minutes later and followed the same trail at a steady 16 miles per hour. The trail is 30 miles long.
problems.ask: How many minutes after starting did Grace catch up to Lena?
steps: Head start: in 30 minutes (1/2 hour), Lena covers 10 × 1/2 = 5 miles.
Time to close the gap: 5 ÷ 6 = 5/6 hour = 50 minutes.

problems.stem: Leah is writing a report about her town. Its population grew by 10% from 2016 to 2020, then shrank by 10% from 2020 to 2024. The town has 15 public parks.
problems.ask: By what percent is the 2024 population lower than the 2016 population?
steps: Start with a population of 100 (any starting value works the same way).
99 is 1 below 100, so it is 1% lower.

problems.stem: Silas is saving for a new bike. He puts $4 in a jar the first week, and every week after that he puts in $1 more than the week before. He started the plan on his 14th birthday.
problems.ask: How much will Silas have saved in all after 15 weeks?
steps: Pair week 1 with week 15, week 2 with week 14, and so on: each pair adds to $4 + $18 = $22.
With 15 weeks, the average week is $22 ÷ 2 = $11, so the total is 15 × $11 = $165.

problems.stem: Ezra is fencing in a rectangular play area for his kids. The area is 24 feet long and 16 feet wide. He'll fence all four sides.
problems.ask: How many feet of fencing does Ezra need?
steps: One length plus one width: 24 + 16 = 40 feet.
Going all the way around doubles that: 2 × 40 = 80 feet.

problems.stem: Nico is picking up breakfast for his study group at a coffee shop. The prices, which include tax, are in the table. The shop opens at 6:30 every morning. Nico orders three hot chocolates, two drip coffees, and two bagels.
problems.ask: What is the total cost of Nico's order?

problems.stem: Imani wants to buy a laptop at an electronics store. The price is $875 if she pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $75 down, then 10 monthly payments of $87. The laptop weighs about 4 pounds.
problems.ask: How much more would Imani pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?

problems.stem: Diego needs a rental car for one day and is comparing the two companies in the table. He plans to pick up the car at 7:30 a.m. on Friday.
problems.ask: For how many miles of driving would the two companies charge exactly the same amount?
steps: Company A costs $33 more up front.
Company B costs $0.10 more per mile, so each mile closes the gap by $0.10.

problems.stem: Sam is organizing a chess league with 10 players this season. Every player will play every other player exactly twice during the regular season. Each match takes about 45 minutes.
problems.ask: How many matches will be played in the regular season?
steps: Each match is a pair of players. Each of the 10 players pairs with 9 others: 10 × 9 = 90.
That counts every pair twice, so divide by 2: 90 ÷ 2 = 45 pairs.

problems.stem: At 12:30 p.m., Yuki put a loaf of bread in the oven. She took it out at 1:35 p.m., when the crust was golden brown.
problems.ask: For how many minutes did the bread bake?
steps: From 12:30 p.m. to 1:00 p.m. is 30 minutes.
From 1:00 p.m. to 1:35 p.m. is 35 minutes.

problems.stem: Omar is traveling in Italy, where prices are in euros. That week, 1 euro costs $1.10 in U.S. money. He buys a pair of sunglasses for 18 euros and a cookbook for 12 euros. His hotel is 7 blocks from the shop.
problems.ask: How much did Omar spend in all, in U.S. dollars?

problems.stem: Dmitri is painting the four walls of his bedroom, which is 16 feet long, 8 feet wide and 10 feet high. He wants two coats on every wall. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $28 a gallon.
